--[[
	Follow  -  what Forces do to a play. Part of Reactor/Play, split out for size: Follow.methods
	are mixed into Play, so each takes the play as `self` and reads and writes its own tables.

	A play follows the Forces it was told of for as long as each is alive (play.kicks: record ->
	the pieces that record has kicked). An Impulse kicks each piece once, when its front reaches
	it; a Continuous Force carries what lies in it (Reactor/Driven).

	Following is not waiting. A play's Delay runs from the moment its pieces lie still, and a
	Force that is still alive holds it up (play.held) only while it may yet move a piece here:
	a piece inside its shape that its front has not reached, a Force that is on its way
	somewhere (record.moving, Force/init) and has not kicked every piece, or a flow that still
	covers the place a piece was carried from (Reactor/Driven.capture). An Impulse that stands
	still, and any Force that reaches nothing of the play, holds nothing up.
	Cross-file: Play:step reads play.held, which _followForces works out afresh every step.

	methods: watch(record), strike(record), answer(record, cutsFirst),
	kickAgain(record, kicked, indices), _takeTime(record), _applyImpulse(record, kicked),
	_followForces()
]]

local Fields = require(script.Parent.Parent.Force.Fields)
local Driven = require(script.Parent.Driven)
local Crack = require(script.Parent.Crack)
local Slash = require(script.Parent.Slash)

local RESTING = 0
local GONE = 3

local Follow = {}
local methods = {}
Follow.methods = methods

-- Starts following a Force. False while the play is fading or returning: those finish first.
function methods:watch(record)
	if self.phase ~= "live" then
		return false
	end
	if not self.kicks[record] then
		self.kicks[record] = {}
	end
	return true
end

-- The kick of an Impulse that arrived before this play existed, given NOW: a Reactor whose
-- shards were still being cut (Reactor/init) answers late. An Impulse lasts a frame or two, so
-- one that is merely followed can be over before this play's first step and its kick lost.
-- One still alive is followed as well, and remembers the pieces it has kicked here.
-- Returns true and the list of the pieces it kicked, which a later crack asks for (kickAgain).
function methods:strike(record)
	if self.phase ~= "live" then
		return false
	end
	local kicked = {}
	if not record.ended and self:watch(record) then
		kicked = self.kicks[record]
	end
	self:_applyImpulse(record, kicked)
	self.idleFor = 0
	return true, kicked
end

-- What a play does with a Force that reached its Reactor before the play could answer: an
-- Impulse strikes now, a flow that is still alive is followed. cutsFirst: the Force's blade
-- has a cut of its own to make first (Reactor/Recarve), which holds its kick until then.
-- Returns whether the play answers, and the record's list of the pieces it has kicked.
function methods:answer(record, cutsFirst)
	if record.actsAs == "Impulse" and not cutsFirst then
		return self:strike(record)
	end
	if record.actsAs ~= "Impulse" and record.ended then
		return false, nil
	end
	return self:watch(record), self.kicks[record]
end

-- The kick of an Impulse, given to pieces it has passed by: a later crack (Reactor/Recut) made
-- them or took them over after the Impulse arrived. `kicked` is that Impulse's own list of the
-- pieces it has kicked here, kept by whoever asked for the crack; no other piece is kicked twice.
function methods:kickAgain(record, kicked, indices)
	if self.phase ~= "live" then
		return
	end
	for _, index in ipairs(indices) do
		kicked[index] = nil
	end
	self:_applyImpulse(record, kicked)
	self.idleFor = 0
end

-- A Force that moves a piece of this play lends the play its time. Following one is not
-- enough: a play out of place follows every Force of its Group, however far away.
function methods:_takeTime(record)
	local times = self.times
	local carried = record.time
	if carried and not table.find(times, carried) then
		table.insert(times, carried)
	end
	local own = record.ownTime
	if own and not table.find(times, own) then
		table.insert(times, own)
	end
end

-- One kick for every piece the front of an Impulse has reached since the last frame.
function methods:_applyImpulse(record, kicked)
	local settings = self.settings
	local field = record.field
	local front = record.front
	local strength = record.strength
	local pulls = strength < 0
	local waits = self.recracking[record]
	local moving = record.moving == true
	Slash.kick(self, record, kicked)
	for index, piece in ipairs(self.pieces) do
		local standsBy = waits and (waits == "all" or (piece.strike ~= nil and self.state[index] == RESTING))
		if not kicked[index] and self.state[index] ~= GONE and not piece.fixed and not standsBy then
			local direction, distance, distance01 = Fields.sample(field, self:_position(index), pulls)
			if not direction then
				-- A split is wider than the Linear shape that made it.
				direction, distance, distance01 = Crack.reached(piece, record, pulls)
			end
			if direction and distance <= front then
				kicked[index] = true
				-- Cracked ground that is no wound's: the last Force with an After of its own has the word.
				if piece.strike and settings.takesAfter and record.after then
					settings.After = record.after
					settings.AfterDelay = record.afterDelay or settings.AfterDelay
				end
				local share = Fields.sizeShare(piece.size, record.sizeResponse)
				local spread = 1 + record.variation * (settings.random() * 2 - 1)
				local throw = strength * Fields.kept(record.falloff, distance01) * share * spread
				if math.abs(throw) > self:_holdOf(index) and not Crack.holds(piece) then
					self:_push(index, direction * Fields.throwSpeed(throw, self:_rolled(index)))
					self:_takeTime(record)
				elseif piece.strike then
					Crack.strike(self, index, strength)
				end
			elseif direction or moving then
				-- The front is still on its way to this piece, or the Force itself is.
				self.held = true
			end
		end
	end
end

function methods:_followForces()
	self.held = false
	for record, kicked in pairs(self.kicks) do
		if record.ended then
			self.kicks[record] = nil
		elseif record.actsAs == "Impulse" then
			self:_applyImpulse(record, kicked)
		else
			Driven.capture(self, record)
			-- A flow that is on its way somewhere may yet take up what lies here.
			if record.moving then
				self.held = true
			end
		end
	end
end

return Follow

--[[
	Footprint  -  what one Impulse cracks of a ground's struck face (Reactor/Wounds), and the
	template each rectangle of it is cut from (Reactor/Patches). Numbers only, no instances.

	A round Force opens a square around its hit, PATCH_REACH Ranges to each side: a little past
	what it can move, so the pieces along the square's sides stay at rest, and two Forces
	farther apart than twice that along one axis of the face never share ground. A Linear Force
	that lies along the face opens a strip around its split's path (Reactor/Fissure).

	Footprint.of(ground, field, hitInPart, reach, seed) -> footprint
	    ground: { frame, size, face = { axis, side }, uAxis, vAxis } (Reactor/Wounds).
	    field: Force/Fields'. hitInPart: where the Force is, in the ground's space. reach: its
	    Range. seed: the split's path is drawn from it, the same for every ground and every
	    later crack of one Force at one place (Reactor/Recut draws it again from that seed).
	    footprint = { minU, minV, maxU, maxV, area, reach, probes, line }: the rectangle of the
	    face, how far the crack's hairlines go, places just under the face to ask the field
	    at, and for a split its line (Reactor/Fissure.of, with the seed its places are laid
	    from), nil for a round crack.
	Footprint.reaches(footprint, rectangle) -> whether the crack moves any of that rectangle
	Footprint.job(ground, rectangle, footprint, hitInPart, seed, alone, pieces) -> job
	    The template one rectangle is cut from: { size, frame, hit, reach, count, seed, face,
	    line, whole, variant }. hit and line are in the template's own space. A rectangle that
	    is all of a round crack's square (alone = it is the footprint's only one) is whole: its
	    cut depends on nothing but its size, the Range, the count and `variant`, so
	    Reactor/Patches keeps it. A split is never whole: its path turns with its Force.
	    A rectangle of a blade's wound is carved, not cracked: its job has bladeFrame,
	    bladeSize and slash in the template's space, the cut's mode, and stands = true, since
	    what a blade leaves of the ground never moves (Reactor/Carve).
	    A round crack's rectangle gets its share of `pieces` by its area. A split's rectangles
	    all carry the whole count and the line's seed: its places are laid once along the
	    path, and each rectangle keeps those that fall in it (Reactor/Sites.cracks).
	Footprint.pieces(footprint, jobs) -> the pieces those jobs are expected to bring: every
	    place gives Sites.LAYERS of them, every job a base; a carved rectangle its one side
	    and, with Band, the most bits a cut gives
	Footprint.ofBlade(ground, blade, mode, room) -> footprint or nil
	    The wound of a Force with a Cut (Reactor/Blade): the rectangle of the face its blade
	    stands over, BLADE_MARGIN studs more to every side, so the blade ends inside the patch
	    and the patch stays in one piece with a gash in it. nil when there is no blade or it
	    does not come down into the ground. room: the pieces the budget still has room for;
	    with too little for a Band's debris the gash is cut as Halves. footprint = { minU,
	    minV, maxU, maxV, area, reach = 0, blade, mode, under }, under the blade's own rectangle.
	Footprint.bladePieces(mode) -> the pieces one cut of a blade may bring
]]

local Sites = require(script.Parent.Sites)
local Fissure = require(script.Parent.Fissure)
local Blade = require(script.Parent.Blade)
local Carve = require(script.Parent.Carve)
local Layers = require(script.Parent.Layers)

local Footprint = {}

Footprint.PATCH_REACH = 1.3
-- A split's strip of ground lies this many times its reach to either side of its path: past
-- its long outer pieces.
local STRIP_REACH = 2.2
-- The different cuts kept of one whole square (Reactor/Patches).
local VARIANTS = 3
-- Two lengths this near are the same length.
local SAME_LENGTH = 1e-3
-- A blade's wound reaches this many studs past the blade to every side.
local BLADE_MARGIN = 2
-- A blade that comes less than this far under the face cuts nothing worth a wound.
local LEAST_DEPTH = 0.05
local SIGNS = { -1, 1 }

function Footprint.ofBlade(ground, blade, mode, room)
	local size = ground.size
	if not blade or not Blade.touches(blade, ground.frame, size) then
		return nil
	end
	-- Debris is made only while the budget has room for it: the cut itself always shows.
	if mode == "Band" and room and room < 2 * Footprint.bladePieces(mode) then
		mode = "Halves"
	end
	local axis, side = ground.face.axis, ground.face.side
	local uAxis, vAxis = ground.uAxis, ground.vAxis
	local own = Blade.inPart(blade, ground.frame)
	local half = blade.size / 2
	local minU, minV, maxU, maxV = math.huge, math.huge, -math.huge, -math.huge
	local deepest = -math.huge
	for _, x in ipairs(SIGNS) do
		for _, y in ipairs(SIGNS) do
			for _, z in ipairs(SIGNS) do
				local corner = own:PointToWorldSpace(Vector3.new(x * half.X, y * half.Y, z * half.Z))
				minU = math.min(minU, corner[uAxis])
				maxU = math.max(maxU, corner[uAxis])
				minV = math.min(minV, corner[vAxis])
				maxV = math.max(maxV, corner[vAxis])
				deepest = math.max(deepest, size[axis] / 2 - corner[axis] * side)
			end
		end
	end
	if deepest < LEAST_DEPTH then
		return nil
	end
	return {
		minU = minU - BLADE_MARGIN, minV = minV - BLADE_MARGIN, maxU = maxU + BLADE_MARGIN, maxV = maxV + BLADE_MARGIN,
		area = (maxU - minU + 2 * BLADE_MARGIN) * (maxV - minV + 2 * BLADE_MARGIN),
		reach = 0,
		blade = blade,
		mode = mode,
		under = { minU = minU, minV = minV, maxU = maxU, maxV = maxV },
	}
end

function Footprint.of(ground, field, hitInPart, reach, seed)
	local size = ground.size
	local axis, side = ground.face.axis, ground.face.side
	local uAxis, vAxis = ground.uAxis, ground.vAxis
	local normal = Sites.alongFace(axis, 0, 0, side)
	local faceAt = normal * (size[axis] / 2)
	local line = Fissure.of(field, ground.frame, faceAt, normal, Sites.sequence(seed))
	if line then
		local least, most = Fissure.bounds(line.path)
		local margin = line.reach * STRIP_REACH
		local minU, maxU = least[uAxis] - margin, most[uAxis] + margin
		local minV, maxV = least[vAxis] - margin, most[vAxis] + margin
		line.seed = seed
		return {
			minU = minU, minV = minV, maxU = maxU, maxV = maxV,
			area = (maxU - minU) * (maxV - minV),
			reach = line.reach,
			probes = line.probes,
			line = line,
			uAxis = uAxis, vAxis = vAxis,
		}
	end
	local u, v = hitInPart[uAxis], hitInPart[vAxis]
	local half = reach * Footprint.PATCH_REACH
	return {
		minU = u - half, minV = v - half, maxU = u + half, maxV = v + half,
		area = 4 * half * half,
		reach = reach,
		probes = Sites.probes(size, axis, side, u, v, reach),
		u = u, v = v, half = half,
	}
end

-- How far (u, v) lies from a rectangle of the face.
local function awayFrom(rectangle, u, v)
	local awayU = math.max(rectangle.minU - u, 0, u - rectangle.maxU)
	local awayV = math.max(rectangle.minV - v, 0, v - rectangle.maxV)
	return math.sqrt(awayU * awayU + awayV * awayV)
end

function Footprint.reaches(footprint, rectangle)
	local under = footprint.under
	if under then
		return rectangle.minU < under.maxU and rectangle.maxU > under.minU and rectangle.minV < under.maxV and rectangle.maxV > under.minV
	end
	local line = footprint.line
	if not line then
		return awayFrom(rectangle, footprint.u, footprint.v) <= footprint.reach
	end
	for _, point in ipairs(line.path.points) do
		if awayFrom(rectangle, point[footprint.uAxis], point[footprint.vAxis]) <= line.reach then
			return true
		end
	end
	return false
end

function Footprint.job(ground, rectangle, footprint, hitInPart, seed, alone, pieces)
	local width = rectangle.maxU - rectangle.minU
	local height = rectangle.maxV - rectangle.minV
	local axis = ground.face.axis
	local centre = Sites.alongFace(axis, (rectangle.minU + rectangle.maxU) / 2, (rectangle.minV + rectangle.maxV) / 2, 0)
	local size = Sites.alongFace(axis, width, height, ground.size[axis])
	-- A stacked ground's patch is cut layer by layer (Reactor/Layers).
	local layers = nil
	if ground.layers then
		layers = Layers.inPatch(ground, centre, size)
	end
	local blade = footprint.blade
	if blade then
		local patch = ground.frame * CFrame.new(centre.X, centre.Y, centre.Z)
		-- Asked with the whole ground: every patch of it is cut by the same ribbon.
		local ribbon, ribbonFrame = Blade.ribbonFor(blade, ground.frame, ground.size, patch:Inverse())
		return {
			size = size,
			frame = patch,
			layers = layers,
			face = ground.face,
			seed = seed,
			-- Reactor/Patches cuts no job that asks for fewer than two pieces.
			count = 2,
			bladeFrame = Blade.inPart(blade, patch),
			bladeSize = blade.size,
			ribbon = ribbon,
			ribbonFrame = ribbonFrame,
			always = true,
			slash = {
				origin = patch:PointToObjectSpace(blade.origin),
				normal = patch:VectorToObjectSpace(blade.normal),
				heading = patch:VectorToObjectSpace(blade.heading),
				kerf = blade.kerf,
			},
			mode = footprint.mode,
			stands = true,
		}
	end
	-- A rectangle that is a part of the footprint gets that share of the points.
	local wanted = math.max(math.floor(pieces * width * height / footprint.area + 0.5), 2)
	local job = {
		size = size,
		frame = ground.frame * CFrame.new(centre.X, centre.Y, centre.Z),
		hit = hitInPart - centre,
		reach = footprint.reach,
		count = Sites.count(size, wanted),
		seed = seed,
		face = ground.face,
		layers = layers,
	}
	local line = footprint.line
	if line then
		job.count = Sites.count(size, pieces)
		job.line = { path = Fissure.moved(line.path, CFrame.new(centre.X, centre.Y, centre.Z), true), reach = line.reach, seed = line.seed }
		return job
	end
	local side = 2 * footprint.half
	local skinned = false
	for _, share in ipairs(layers or {}) do
		skinned = skinned or share.skin ~= nil
	end
	-- Under a skin a square is no cut of its size alone: the skin's outline differs from place to place.
	if alone and not skinned and math.abs(width - side) < SAME_LENGTH and math.abs(height - side) < SAME_LENGTH then
		job.whole = true
		job.variant = math.floor(seed / 4) % VARIANTS
		job.hit = Sites.alongFace(axis, 0, 0, ground.face.side * ground.size[axis] / 2)
	end
	return job
end

-- The pieces one cut of a blade may bring: a side, and with Band the most debris a cut gives.
function Footprint.bladePieces(mode)
	if mode == "Band" then
		return 1 + Carve.MOST_BITS
	end
	return 1
end

function Footprint.pieces(footprint, jobs)
	if footprint.blade then
		-- A blade carves each layer of a stacked ground by itself.
		local carved = 0
		for _, job in ipairs(jobs) do
			if job.layers then
				carved += #job.layers
			else
				carved += 1
			end
		end
		return carved * Footprint.bladePieces(footprint.mode)
	end
	local bases = #jobs
	local places = 0
	for _, job in ipairs(jobs) do
		if footprint.line then
			places = math.max(places, job.count)
		else
			places += job.count
		end
	end
	return places * Sites.LAYERS + bases
end

return Footprint

--[[
	Ground  -  one face of a block-shaped part as rectangles: what of it open cracks hold
	(Reactor/Wounds) and what is left intact. Numbers only, no instances.

	A place is (u, v) on the face, in studs from its middle. A rectangle is
	{ minU, minV, maxU, maxV }.

	Ground.new(halfU, halfV, snap) -> ground
	    snap: the least width of anything this makes. An edge nearer than that to an edge
	    already there is laid onto it, so no strip thinner than `snap` is ever left.
	ground:claim(owner, centreU, centreV, half) -> { rectangle }
	    The square of half-side `half` around the centre, cut to the face, less what is held
	    already. The rectangles returned are intact ground no longer: they are `owner`'s until
	    released. Empty when the square holds nothing intact.
	ground:claimArea(owner, minU, minV, maxU, maxV) -> { rectangle }
	    The same for any rectangle of the face: a split along a line needs a strip, not a square.
	ground:release(owner)
	ground:held(owner) -> { rectangle }: what `owner` holds, or nil
	ground:touching(minU, minV, maxU, maxV) -> { owner }: whose rectangles overlap that area,
	    in the order they claimed
	ground:remainder(unshown) -> { rectangle }: the intact ground, as few large rectangles
	    unshown: nil, or a set of owners (owner -> true) whose rectangles still count as
	    intact: a crack that holds its ground while its pieces are being cut.
	ground:isWhole() -> boolean: nothing is held

	Every edge on an axis is `snap` or more from every other, the face's own two included:
	claim keeps that, and the grid of cells between the edges has no cell thinner than `snap`.
]]

local Ground = {}
Ground.__index = Ground

function Ground.new(halfU, halfV, snap)
	local self = setmetatable({}, Ground)
	self.halfU = halfU
	self.halfV = halfV
	self.snap = snap
	-- owner -> its rectangles, and the owners in the order they claimed.
	self.rectangles = {}
	self.owners = {}
	return self
end

-- Every edge on one axis: the face's two and those of every held rectangle.
local function edgesOf(self, minKey, maxKey, half)
	local edges = { -half, half }
	for _, owner in ipairs(self.owners) do
		for _, rectangle in ipairs(self.rectangles[owner]) do
			table.insert(edges, rectangle[minKey])
			table.insert(edges, rectangle[maxKey])
		end
	end
	return edges
end

-- `value`, laid onto the nearest of `edges` when one is nearer than `snap`.
local function snapped(value, edges, snap)
	local best = value
	local least = snap
	for _, edge in ipairs(edges) do
		local distance = math.abs(edge - value)
		if distance < least then
			least = distance
			best = edge
		end
	end
	return best
end

-- The distinct values of `edges` from `low` to `high`, both ends among them, in order, and the
-- place of each value in that list.
local function cuts(edges, low, high)
	local within = { low, high }
	for _, edge in ipairs(edges) do
		if edge > low and edge < high then
			table.insert(within, edge)
		end
	end
	table.sort(within)
	local distinct = {}
	local placeOf = {}
	for _, edge in ipairs(within) do
		if distinct[#distinct] ~= edge then
			table.insert(distinct, edge)
			placeOf[edge] = #distinct
		end
	end
	return distinct, placeOf
end

-- The part of an area that nobody holds, as rectangles. The held rectangles' edges make a grid
-- of cells over the area; the free cells are merged, row by row, into the largest rectangles
-- they give (greedy meshing). `unshown`: owners whose rectangles count as free.
local function freeIn(self, minU, minV, maxU, maxV, unshown)
	local us, columnOf = cuts(edgesOf(self, "minU", "maxU", self.halfU), minU, maxU)
	local vs, rowOf = cuts(edgesOf(self, "minV", "maxV", self.halfV), minV, maxV)
	local columns = #us - 1
	local rows = #vs - 1

	local taken = {}
	for _, owner in ipairs(self.owners) do
		local counted = self.rectangles[owner]
		if unshown and unshown[owner] then
			counted = {}
		end
		for _, rectangle in ipairs(counted) do
			local overlaps = rectangle.minU < maxU and rectangle.maxU > minU and rectangle.minV < maxV and rectangle.maxV > minV
			if overlaps then
				local firstColumn = columnOf[math.max(rectangle.minU, minU)]
				local lastColumn = columnOf[math.min(rectangle.maxU, maxU)] - 1
				local firstRow = rowOf[math.max(rectangle.minV, minV)]
				local lastRow = rowOf[math.min(rectangle.maxV, maxV)] - 1
				for row = firstRow, lastRow do
					for column = firstColumn, lastColumn do
						taken[(row - 1) * columns + column] = true
					end
				end
			end
		end
	end

	local rectangles = {}
	for row = 1, rows do
		for column = 1, columns do
			if not taken[(row - 1) * columns + column] then
				local lastColumn = column
				while lastColumn < columns and not taken[(row - 1) * columns + lastColumn + 1] do
					lastColumn += 1
				end
				local lastRow = row
				local grows = true
				while grows and lastRow < rows do
					for across = column, lastColumn do
						if taken[lastRow * columns + across] then
							grows = false
							break
						end
					end
					if grows then
						lastRow += 1
					end
				end
				for filled = row, lastRow do
					for across = column, lastColumn do
						taken[(filled - 1) * columns + across] = true
					end
				end
				table.insert(rectangles, { minU = us[column], minV = vs[row], maxU = us[lastColumn + 1], maxV = vs[lastRow + 1] })
			end
		end
	end
	return rectangles
end

function Ground:claim(owner, centreU, centreV, half)
	return self:claimArea(owner, centreU - half, centreV - half, centreU + half, centreV + half)
end

function Ground:claimArea(owner, lowU, lowV, highU, highV)
	local snap = self.snap
	local uEdges = edgesOf(self, "minU", "maxU", self.halfU)
	local vEdges = edgesOf(self, "minV", "maxV", self.halfV)
	local minU = snapped(math.max(lowU, -self.halfU), uEdges, snap)
	local maxU = snapped(math.min(highU, self.halfU), uEdges, snap)
	local minV = snapped(math.max(lowV, -self.halfV), vEdges, snap)
	local maxV = snapped(math.min(highV, self.halfV), vEdges, snap)
	if maxU - minU < snap or maxV - minV < snap then
		return {}
	end
	local rectangles = freeIn(self, minU, minV, maxU, maxV)
	if #rectangles == 0 then
		return rectangles
	end
	local own = self.rectangles[owner]
	if not own then
		self.rectangles[owner] = rectangles
		table.insert(self.owners, owner)
		return rectangles
	end
	for _, rectangle in ipairs(rectangles) do
		table.insert(own, rectangle)
	end
	return rectangles
end

function Ground:release(owner)
	if not self.rectangles[owner] then
		return
	end
	self.rectangles[owner] = nil
	table.remove(self.owners, table.find(self.owners, owner))
end

function Ground:held(owner)
	return self.rectangles[owner]
end

function Ground:touching(minU, minV, maxU, maxV)
	local found = {}
	for _, owner in ipairs(self.owners) do
		for _, rectangle in ipairs(self.rectangles[owner]) do
			if rectangle.minU < maxU and rectangle.maxU > minU and rectangle.minV < maxV and rectangle.maxV > minV then
				table.insert(found, owner)
				break
			end
		end
	end
	return found
end

function Ground:remainder(unshown)
	return freeIn(self, -self.halfU, -self.halfV, self.halfU, self.halfV, unshown)
end

function Ground:isWhole()
	return #self.owners == 0
end

return Ground

--[[
	GroundDisplay  -  what is left intact of a ground that has open cracks (Reactor/Wounds):
	plain boxes around the wounds, in the ground's look, while the ground itself is hidden.

	The ground is LIVE user content. It is written in one way only, Reactor/Display's hide and
	show, once per ground however many wounds are open, and it stays solid: what is thrown out
	of a wound lands on it, and nobody falls through a crater. The boxes are copies that are
	not saved (Archivable off, under the runtime's folder, marked _PartIcleEmit) and that
	nothing collides with.

	A tiling Texture on the struck face is carried onto the boxes, its offset moved so the
	pattern runs on across them. Measured in Studio for the top face only: a Texture is laid
	from the face's +X and +Z edges. On another face the boxes carry no Texture. A Decal is
	stretched over its whole face and cannot be carried at all.

	GroundDisplay.new(folder, onServer, without) -> display
	    without: Reactor/Shards.without, for the skins (Reactor/SkinDisplay).
	display.draw(ground, rectangles, face)
	    ground: { part, frame, size } (Reactor/Wounds). rectangles: the intact rest of its
	    face `face` ({ axis, side }), each { minU, minV, maxU, maxV } (Reactor/Ground); the
	    boxes are those rectangles through the ground. nil: the ground is whole again, its
	    boxes go and it is shown. A stacked ground (Reactor/Layers) is drawn layer by layer,
	    each as a ground of its own (its slice), so every layer's part is hidden and shown.
	display.clear()   every ground whole again
]]

local Display = require(script.Parent.Display)
local Index = require(script.Parent.Index)
local Sites = require(script.Parent.Sites)
local Layers = require(script.Parent.Layers)
local SkinDisplay = require(script.Parent.SkinDisplay)

local GroundDisplay = {}

-- A bare copy of the ground, to be sized as one box of it.
local function makeBox(part, folder)
	local box = Instance.fromExisting(part)
	box.Name = "GroundBox"
	box.Archivable = false
	box.Anchored = true
	box.CanCollide = false
	box.CanQuery = false
	box.CanTouch = false
	box.Locked = true
	-- On a server the ground is hidden through its own Transparency, which the copy took.
	box.Transparency = Display.ownTransparency(part)
	Index.unmark(box)
	box:SetAttribute("_PartIcleEmit", true)
	box.Parent = folder
	return box
end

-- The ground's Textures that tile its struck face, when that face is one they can be carried on.
local function carried(ground, face)
	local part = ground.part
	local textures = {}
	-- plain: a layer turned otherwise than its stack has its own Top elsewhere.
	if ground.plain or face.axis ~= "Y" or face.side ~= 1 then
		return textures
	end
	for _, child in ipairs(part:GetChildren()) do
		if child:IsA("Texture") and child.Face == Enum.NormalId.Top then
			table.insert(textures, child)
		end
	end
	return textures
end

function GroundDisplay.new(folder, onServer, without)
	-- part -> { boxes, kept (what Display.show puts back), textures }
	local drawn = {}
	local display = {}
	-- A skin (Reactor/Layers) is no box: what is intact of it is the skin with holes in it.
	local skins = SkinDisplay.new(folder, onServer, without)

	local function whole(part)
		local state = drawn[part]
		if not state then
			return
		end
		drawn[part] = nil
		for _, box in ipairs(state.boxes) do
			box:Destroy()
		end
		Display.show(part, onServer, state.kept)
	end

	function display.draw(ground, rectangles, face)
		if ground.layers then
			for _, layer in ipairs(ground.layers) do
				if layer.skin then
					skins.draw(ground, layer, rectangles, face)
				else
					local own = rectangles
					if own then
						own = Layers.clip(ground, layer, rectangles, face)
					end
					display.draw(layer.slice, own, face)
				end
			end
			return
		end
		local part = ground.part
		if not rectangles then
			whole(part)
			return
		end
		local state = drawn[part]
		if not state then
			-- The Textures are read before the ground is hidden: hiding writes them too.
			state = { boxes = {}, textures = carried(ground, face) }
			drawn[part] = state
		end
		local boxes = state.boxes
		for position = #boxes, #rectangles + 1, -1 do
			boxes[position]:Destroy()
			boxes[position] = nil
		end
		local thickness = ground.size[face.axis]
		for position, rectangle in ipairs(rectangles) do
			local box = boxes[position]
			if not box then
				box = makeBox(part, folder)
				for _, texture in ipairs(state.textures) do
					local copy = texture:Clone()
					-- The ground's own Texture is hidden with it: the copy is not.
					Display.unhidden(copy, texture)
					copy.Parent = box
				end
				boxes[position] = box
			end
			local centre = Sites.alongFace(face.axis, (rectangle.minU + rectangle.maxU) / 2, (rectangle.minV + rectangle.maxV) / 2, 0)
			box.Size = Sites.alongFace(face.axis, rectangle.maxU - rectangle.minU, rectangle.maxV - rectangle.minV, thickness)
			box.CFrame = ground.frame * CFrame.new(centre.X, centre.Y, centre.Z)
			if #state.textures > 0 then
				local copies = {}
				for _, child in ipairs(box:GetChildren()) do
					if child:IsA("Texture") then
						table.insert(copies, child)
					end
				end
				for place, texture in ipairs(state.textures) do
					copies[place].OffsetStudsU = texture.OffsetStudsU + ground.size.X / 2 - rectangle.maxU
					copies[place].OffsetStudsV = texture.OffsetStudsV + ground.size.Z / 2 - rectangle.maxV
				end
			end
		end
		-- Hidden last, so the boxes are there in the frame the ground goes.
		if not state.kept then
			state.kept = Display.hide(part, onServer, true)
		end
	end

	function display.clear()
		for part in pairs(table.clone(drawn)) do
			whole(part)
		end
		skins.clear()
	end

	return display
end

return GroundDisplay

--[[
	HandOver Mixin  -  a mesh part-icle that becomes a Reactor. A mesh whose config says
	Reacts plays as authored until a Force of its Group reaches its emitted copy. In that frame
	its own play ends for good and the copy is handed to the Reactor code: an entry is made
	around it (Reactor/Entries, with an owner: Reactor/Owned), and Play, After and the rest
	run it from there by the Reactor settings on the item's own config.

	_watchForForces(pData, settings, whole)
	    EmitPart calls it for a play whose data has Reactor settings, before it registers the
	    play. The play is listed in Particle._watched, and pData._onReclaim, which every
	    removal route runs (LifecycleRelease._reclaimPData), takes it off again. `whole`: a
	    Matte carries the copy, which then reacts in one piece and is never cut.
	    The engine is asked now whether it cuts the copy's mesh at all (Shards.judge, once a
	    mesh a session): its refusal takes half a second, and a copy of a mesh it refuses
	    flies whole in the frame a Force reaches it.
	_handOverReached(now)
	    Engine's step calls it before it walks ActiveEmits. Nothing is done while no play is
	    watched or no Force is alive. Else each record's place and reach are read once, and
	    for each watched play: for each record its Group, then the copy's place and size and
	    a distance, and only then Reactor/Reach. Makes no table, but for a Force with a Cut
	    whose box the copy is in (one blade a record a frame, and Reactor/Blade.touches).
	_followReacted(record)
	    Reactor/init's _reactToForce calls it: a copy that has reacted follows a later Force
	    of its Group that could reach one of its pieces. It carries no tag to be found by, and
	    there may be hundreds: one that lies out of a Force's reach stays off the engine's list.
	_endReacted(item, token)
	    Releases at once every reacted copy of an item (item given) or of one play (token
	    given). Lifecycle.Disable and PlayHandle:Disable call it: a copy that lies where it
	    fell is on no list they sweep.

	The hand-over: the copy's own velocity is measured (Reactor/Momentum); its play leaves
	ActiveEmits without dying and is kept by the owner, which ends it when the copy is gone;
	the entry lets every piece go at that velocity (Owned.adopt) and the Force strikes. A copy
	the engine has to cut first (Break, or a blade) hangs where it was reached until the cut
	is in, as a Reactor answers late. The copies reached in one frame are one pass
	(Reactor/Batch): they answer together when the last of their cuts is in, and a copy that
	needs no cut hangs with those that do.
	Max Pieces is the most reacted pieces of one item that may be out at once: a hand-over
	that would pass it sends the oldest away, sunk in a moment where they lie.

	Mutates: the copy and its play (both the runtime's own).
	Cross-file: a Part play had no _onReclaim before this; one that needs it must chain.
	Flipbook.luau and MeshFrames.luau stop a play's tasks on pData._handedOver.
]]

local ForceRegistry = require(script.Parent.Parent.Force.Registry)
local Index = require(script.Parent.Index)
local Entries = require(script.Parent.Entries)
local Play = require(script.Parent.Play)
local Owned = require(script.Parent.Owned)
local Reach = require(script.Parent.Reach)
local Momentum = require(script.Parent.Momentum)
local Blade = require(script.Parent.Blade)
local Shards = require(script.Parent.Shards)
local Batch = require(script.Parent.Batch)

-- Seconds a copy the cap sends away takes to sink where it lies.
local LEAVE_SECONDS = 0.25

return function(Particle)

-- The plays that may react, in no order; pData._watchIndex is a play's place in it.
Particle._watched = {}
-- The owners of the copies that have reacted, oldest first (Reactor/Owned).
Particle._reacted = {}

-- record -> { at, blade }: a cutting Force's blade where the Force stands this frame.
local blades = setmetatable({}, { __mode = "k" })
-- One pass's scratch: where each live record stands and how far its shape reaches.
local origins = {}
local reaches = {}

-- Takes a play off the watch list. Every watched play has it as its _onReclaim.
local function unwatch(pData)
	local watched = Particle._watched
	local place = pData._watchIndex
	if not place or watched[place] ~= pData then
		return
	end
	local last = #watched
	local moved = watched[last]
	watched[place] = moved
	moved._watchIndex = place
	watched[last] = nil
	pData._watchIndex = nil
end

function Particle:_watchForForces(pData, settings, whole)
	if whole and settings.Break ~= "None" then
		settings = table.clone(settings)
		settings.Break = "None"
	end
	pData._reacts = settings
	pData._reactWhole = whole == true
	local visual = pData.VisualPart
	if visual and not whole then
		Shards.judge(visual)
	end
	-- Its own Hold, rolled once: asked again every frame, a roll would let it through in the end.
	pData._reactHold = settings.Hold * (1 + settings.HoldSpread * (math.random() * 2 - 1))
	local watched = self._watched
	pData._watchIndex = #watched + 1
	watched[pData._watchIndex] = pData
	pData._onReclaim = unwatch
end

-- Whether the blade of a cutting record touches a copy.
local function cutBy(record, visual, position, radius, age)
	if not Reach.inBlade(record, position, radius, age) then
		return false
	end
	local origin = record.field.origin
	local kept = blades[record]
	if not kept then
		kept = {}
		blades[record] = kept
	end
	if kept.at ~= origin then
		kept.at = origin
		kept.blade = Blade.of(record.field, record.cut)
	end
	return kept.blade ~= nil and Blade.touches(kept.blade, visual.ExtentsCFrame, visual.ExtentsSize)
end

-- The first of the `live` records that reaches a watched play, or nil. The copy is read only
-- for a record of its Group, and the record's shape only inside a ball round it.
local function reachedBy(pData, visual, records, live, now)
	local group = pData._reacts.Group
	local position, extent, radius = nil, nil, 0
	for place = 1, live do
		local record = records[place]
		if Index.groupMatches(record.group, group) then
			if not position then
				position = visual.CFrame.Position
				extent = visual.Size
				radius = extent.Magnitude / 2
			end
			if (position - origins[place]).Magnitude <= radius + reaches[place] then
				local age = now - pData.StartTime
				if Reach.moved(record, position, extent, pData._reactHold, age) then
					return record
				end
				if record.cut and not pData._reactWhole and cutBy(record, visual, position, radius, age) then
					return record
				end
			end
		end
	end
	return nil
end

-- Ends an owner at once, from outside: what waits for its cut is dropped, its entry discarded.
local function release(self, owner)
	Entries.forget(self._reactorCutting[owner.copy])
	if owner.entry and self._reactorPlays[owner.copy] == owner.entry then
		Entries.discard(self, owner.entry)
	end
	Owned.gone(self, owner, false)
end

-- How many pieces an owner has out.
local function piecesOf(owner)
	local entry = owner.entry
	if entry then
		return math.max(entry.play.awake, 1)
	end
	return 1
end

-- Sends an owner away for the cap: one that lies where it fell sinks there and is then gone
-- by itself; one still in flight, or still being cut, goes at once.
local function leave(self, owner)
	owner.leaving = true
	local entry = owner.entry
	if not entry or entry.pData or entry.play.phase ~= "live" then
		release(self, owner)
		return
	end
	local settings = entry.play.settings
	settings.After = "Fade"
	settings.AfterDelay = 0
	settings.AfterTime = LEAVE_SECONDS
	entry.play.idleFor = 0
	if not Entries.resume(self, entry) then
		release(self, owner)
	end
end

-- Keeps the reacted pieces of the newest owner's item within its Max Pieces: the oldest go.
local function keepWithin(self, newest)
	local source = newest.source
	local most = math.max(newest.settings.MaxPieces, 1)
	local reacted = self._reacted
	local out = 0
	for _, owner in ipairs(reacted) do
		if owner.source == source and not owner.leaving then
			out += piecesOf(owner)
		end
	end
	local place = 1
	while out > most and place <= #reacted do
		local owner = reacted[place]
		if owner ~= newest and owner.source == source and not owner.leaving then
			out -= piecesOf(owner)
			leave(self, owner)
		end
		-- An owner that went at once has left the list: the next one stands in its place.
		if reacted[place] == owner then
			place += 1
		end
	end
end

local function handOver(self, pData, record, now)
	local copy = pData.VisualPart
	local emits = self.ActiveEmits
	local listed = table.find(emits, pData)
	unwatch(pData)
	if not listed then
		return
	end
	local velocity = Momentum.of(self, pData, now)
	-- The play leaves the engine's list without dying: its owner keeps it and ends it.
	local last = #emits
	emits[listed] = emits[last]
	emits[last] = nil
	pData._onReclaim = nil
	pData._handedOver = true
	pData._noPool = true

	local token = pData._playToken
	local owner = {
		copy = copy,
		particle = pData,
		source = pData._sourceItem,
		settings = pData._reacts,
		velocity = velocity,
		whole = pData._reactWhole,
		context = token and { _playToken = token } or nil,
	}
	table.insert(self._reacted, owner)
	keepWithin(self, owner)

	-- A Matte's shape is never cut: its entry is made without the Force's blade.
	local asking = record
	if owner.whole then
		asking = nil
	end
	local entry, cutting = Entries.entryFor(self, copy, nil, asking, owner)
	if cutting then
		Entries.owe(cutting, record)
		return
	end
	if not entry then
		release(self, owner)
		return
	end
	-- The Force that reached the copy is given to its entry with the rest of this frame's
	-- pass (Reactor/init's _tellEntry): an Impulse strikes, a later blade cuts before it kicks.
	self:_tellEntry(entry, record, true)
end

-- One frame's pass over the watched plays (Reactor/Batch.pass runs it).
-- Backwards: a play handed over leaves the list, and the last one takes its place.
local function handOverAll(self, watched, count, records, live, now)
	for place = count, 1, -1 do
		local pData = watched[place]
		local visual = pData.VisualPart
		if visual and visual.Parent then
			local record = reachedBy(pData, visual, records, live, now)
			if record then
				handOver(self, pData, record, now)
			end
		end
	end
end

function Particle:_handOverReached(now)
	local watched = self._watched
	local count = #watched
	if count == 0 then
		return
	end
	local records = ForceRegistry.list()
	local live = #records
	if live == 0 then
		return
	end
	for place = 1, live do
		local field = records[place].field
		origins[place] = field.origin.Position
		reaches[place] = Index.reachOf(field)
	end
	Batch.pass(handOverAll, self, watched, count, records, live, now)
end

-- Whether a Force could reach a piece of an owned entry that is still there: a ball round the
-- piece against a ball round the Force's shape.
local function couldReach(record, entry)
	local play = entry.play
	local field = record.field
	for index, piece in ipairs(play.pieces) do
		if play.state[index] ~= Play.GONE and Index.reaches(field, play:_position(index), piece.reach) then
			return true
		end
	end
	return false
end

function Particle:_followReacted(record)
	local reacted = self._reacted
	for place = #reacted, 1, -1 do
		local owner = reacted[place]
		local entry = owner.entry
		if not owner.copy.Parent then
			release(self, owner)
		elseif entry and not owner.leaving and Index.groupMatches(record.group, entry.group) and couldReach(record, entry) then
			self:_tellEntry(entry, record, false)
		end
	end
end

function Particle:_endReacted(item, token)
	local reacted = self._reacted
	for place = #reacted, 1, -1 do
		local owner = reacted[place]
		if owner and ((item ~= nil and owner.source == item) or (token ~= nil and owner.particle._playToken == token)) then
			release(self, owner)
		end
	end
end

end

--[[
	Index  -  which Reactors a Force could reach. A Reactor is found by its tag (set by
	TransformReactor), so nothing is scanned: a place with no Reactors costs one empty list.
	Index.reaches is a first, generous test (a ball around the Reactor against a ball around
	the Force's shape); Reactor/Play decides piece by piece.
	Index.unmark makes a copy of a Reactor an ordinary instance again (Reactor/Display's
	stand-ins, the plugin's Modules/Scatter).
]]

local CollectionService = game:GetService("CollectionService")

local Index = {}

Index.TAG = "PartIcleReactor"
-- The item attributes TransformReactor (Reactor/init.luau) stamps; one added there is added here.
Index.MARKS = { "Transformed", "Qwinkle", "IsReactor", "IsEmitter", "EmitCount", "EmitDuration", "EmitDelay", "EmissionMode", "AnimateLoop" }

-- Every tagged Reactor that is in the world right now.
function Index.reactors()
	local found = {}
	for _, reactor in ipairs(CollectionService:GetTagged(Index.TAG)) do
		if reactor:IsDescendantOf(workspace) and not reactor:GetAttribute("_PartIcleEmit") then
			table.insert(found, reactor)
		end
	end
	return found
end

-- The farthest any point of a field's shape is from its origin.
function Index.reachOf(field)
	if field.shape == "Linear" then
		return math.sqrt(field.range * field.range + field.halfWidth * field.halfWidth + field.halfHeight * field.halfHeight)
	elseif field.shape == "Vortex" then
		return math.sqrt(field.range * field.range + field.height * field.height)
	end
	return field.range
end

function Index.reaches(field, centre, radius)
	return (centre - field.origin.Position).Magnitude <= radius + Index.reachOf(field)
end

-- Takes a Reactor's attributes and tag off a COPY of one. Never called on the Reactor itself.
function Index.unmark(copy)
	for _, mark in ipairs(Index.MARKS) do
		copy:SetAttribute(mark, nil)
	end
	copy:RemoveTag(Index.TAG)
end

-- A Force's Group reaches a Reactor when it is empty or the same.
function Index.groupMatches(forceGroup, reactorGroup)
	return forceGroup == "" or forceGroup == reactorGroup
end

return Index

--[[
	LayerCuts  -  the engine's cut of a patch of a stacked ground (Reactor/Layers): every layer
	around the very same points, the fragments of one point joined into one shard. Called by
	Reactor/Shards, which hands in its own `fragment` (the engine's cut of one part around
	world points, or nil) and `shardOf` (a fragment as a shard record).

	A patch's template is first cut into its layers' slabs, a plane a border, because a
	fragment keeps the CFrame of what it was cut from: every slab, and everything cut from it
	now or later, has the patch's own frame, which is the frame a cut's points are given in.

	The layers' cuts of one step (the crusts off their bases, the crusts around the points)
	are asked of the engine at once, so a stack waits for about one cut more than a block.

	LayerCuts.cut(job, whole, frame, points, split) -> shards | false
	    For a job with more than one share (job.layers, Layers.inPatch): `whole` the patch's
	    template, `frame` its frame, `points` the cut's world points, `split` Sites.cracks'
	    crust and base points or nil. A shard of more than one layer has `parts`: for each
	    fragment { template, layer, standOffset, offset, size }, the last two its own box in
	    the shard's. Every shard has `layer`, the layer of its (first) fragment. The base
	    under the crust is one shard of every layer's share of it.
	LayerCuts.carve(job, frame, carve) -> shards | false
	    A blade through such a patch: each layer is carved by itself (Reactor/Carve.cut,
	    handed in), its sides and bits pieces of their own. A ground's patch stands, so
	    nothing shows that they are not joined.
	LayerCuts.cutAgain(job) -> shards | false
	    Reactor/Shards.recut for a piece of several fragments (job.layered, a piece's own
	    list): each is cut around the job's points and the results joined by point again.
	LayerCuts.stamp(shards, share)   marks the shards of a patch that lies in one layer
	LayerCuts.use(fragment, shardOf, clip) the functions of Reactor/Shards, given once: clip(template,
	    part, into) is what of the template's box lies inside a part, the part taken by `into`
	    to where the template stands (job.place is where the patch stands in the world). A skin's share (share.skin, Reactor/Layers)
	    is its slab clipped to the skin, so a skin of any outline is cut where it is, and a
	    patch the skin does not come to has no such layer.

	Yields wherever the engine cuts. Mutates nothing of the place: templates and fragments
	are kept out of the world.
]]

local AXES = { "X", "Y", "Z" }
-- A share's offset shorter than this along an axis is none.
local THIN = 0.01

local LayerCuts = {}

local fragment = nil
local shardOf = nil
local clip = nil

function LayerCuts.use(fragmentOf, shardFrom, clipTo)
	fragment = fragmentOf
	shardOf = shardFrom
	clip = clipTo
end

local function along(axis, value)
	if axis == "X" then
		return Vector3.new(value, 0, 0)
	elseif axis == "Y" then
		return Vector3.new(0, value, 0)
	end
	return Vector3.new(0, 0, value)
end

function LayerCuts.stamp(shards, share)
	for _, shard in ipairs(shards) do
		shard.layer = share.index
	end
end

-- The fragments of one point as one shard. Fragments are the engine's and keep the patch
-- template's frame, so their boxes lie along `frame`'s axes.
local function joined(frame, group, fixed, siteIndex)
	local first = group[1]
	if #group == 1 then
		local shard = shardOf(first.instance, frame, fixed, siteIndex)
		shard.layer = first.layer
		return shard
	end
	local low, high = nil, nil
	for _, member in ipairs(group) do
		local middle = frame:PointToObjectSpace(member.instance.ExtentsCFrame.Position)
		local half = member.instance.ExtentsSize / 2
		local from = middle - half
		local to = middle + half
		if low then
			low = Vector3.new(math.min(low.X, from.X), math.min(low.Y, from.Y), math.min(low.Z, from.Z))
			high = Vector3.new(math.max(high.X, to.X), math.max(high.Y, to.Y), math.max(high.Z, to.Z))
		else
			low, high = from, to
		end
	end
	local box = CFrame.new((low + high) / 2)
	local world = frame * box
	local parts = table.create(#group)
	for position, member in ipairs(group) do
		local template = member.instance
		parts[position] = {
			template = template,
			layer = member.layer,
			standOffset = world:ToObjectSpace(template.CFrame),
			offset = world:ToObjectSpace(template.ExtentsCFrame),
			size = template.ExtentsSize,
		}
	end
	return {
		template = first.instance,
		box = box,
		size = high - low,
		standOffset = parts[1].standOffset,
		fixed = fixed,
		siteIndex = siteIndex,
		layer = first.layer,
		parts = parts,
	}
end

local function gather(bySite, order, entries, layer)
	for _, entry in ipairs(entries) do
		local group = bySite[entry.Index]
		if not group then
			group = {}
			bySite[entry.Index] = group
			table.insert(order, entry.Index)
		end
		table.insert(group, { instance = entry.Instance, layer = layer })
	end
end

local function destroyGroups(bySite, bases)
	for _, group in pairs(bySite) do
		for _, member in ipairs(group) do
			member.instance:Destroy()
		end
	end
	for _, member in ipairs(bases or {}) do
		member.instance:Destroy()
	end
end

-- The shards of the points that gave any, in the points' order, or false for fewer than two.
local function shardsOf(frame, bySite, order, bases)
	if #order < 2 then
		destroyGroups(bySite, bases)
		return false
	end
	table.sort(order)
	local shards = table.create(#order + 1)
	for _, site in ipairs(order) do
		table.insert(shards, joined(frame, bySite[site], false, site))
	end
	if bases and #bases > 0 then
		table.insert(shards, joined(frame, bases, true, nil))
	end
	return shards
end

-- The stack's axis in the patch: the one its shares are offset along.
local function axisOf(shares)
	local offset = shares[2].offset - shares[1].offset
	for _, axis in ipairs(AXES) do
		if math.abs(offset[axis]) > THIN then
			return axis
		end
	end
	return "Y"
end

-- A patch's template cut into its layers' slabs, in the shares' order: a plane a border, by
-- two points a stud to either side of it. An entry is false where the engine gave none; nil
-- when it would not cut at all. Yields. The template itself is left as it is.
local function slabsOf(whole, frame, shares, place)
	local axis = axisOf(shares)
	local slabs = table.create(#shares, false)
	local rest = whole
	for position = 1, #shares - 1 do
		local share = shares[position]
		local border = share.offset[axis] + share.size[axis] / 2
		local halves = fragment(rest, {
			frame:PointToWorldSpace(along(axis, border - 1)),
			frame:PointToWorldSpace(along(axis, border + 1)),
		})
		if rest ~= whole then
			rest:Destroy()
		end
		rest = nil
		if not halves then
			for _, slab in ipairs(slabs) do
				if slab then
					slab:Destroy()
				end
			end
			return nil
		end
		for _, entry in ipairs(halves) do
			-- White, as every source of a cut is: what a blade cuts off a slab keeps the slab's
			-- colour in its geometry, and its stand-in is given its part's colour on top.
			entry.Instance.Color = Color3.new(1, 1, 1)
			if entry.Index == 1 then
				slabs[position] = entry.Instance
			else
				rest = entry.Instance
			end
		end
		if not rest then
			break
		end
	end
	if rest then
		slabs[#shares] = rest
	end
	-- A skin's slab is what of the patch the skin fills: the template's box cut to the skin,
	-- white and in the patch's frame as the others are. The template need not stand where the
	-- patch does (job.place): the skin is taken to it.
	local into = place and frame * place:Inverse() or nil
	for position, share in ipairs(shares) do
		local slab = slabs[position]
		if slab and share.skin then
			slabs[position] = clip(whole, share.skin, into) or false
			slab:Destroy()
		end
	end
	return slabs
end

-- The engine's cut of several sources at once, all around the same points: the results in
-- the sources' order, false where a source is none or the engine gave nothing. A layer's cut
-- waits for no other's. Yields until the last is in.
local function together(sources, points)
	local results = table.create(#sources, false)
	local waiting = coroutine.running()
	local pending = #sources
	local parked = false
	for position, source in ipairs(sources) do
		task.spawn(function()
			if source then
				results[position] = fragment(source, points) or false
			end
			pending -= 1
			if pending == 0 and parked then
				task.spawn(waiting)
			end
		end)
	end
	if pending > 0 then
		parked = true
		coroutine.yield()
	end
	return results
end

function LayerCuts.cut(job, whole, frame, points, split)
	local shares = job.layers
	local slabs = slabsOf(whole, frame, shares, job.place)
	if not slabs then
		return false
	end
	local crustPoint, basePoint = nil, nil
	if split then
		crustPoint = frame:PointToWorldSpace(split.inCrust)
		basePoint = frame:PointToWorldSpace(split.inBase)
	end
	local bySite, order, bases = {}, {}, {}
	-- The crust off its base in every layer: a layer may be all of the one or the other.
	local crusts = slabs
	if split then
		local halves = together(slabs, { crustPoint, basePoint })
		crusts = table.create(#shares, false)
		for position, share in ipairs(shares) do
			local slab = slabs[position]
			local halved = halves[position]
			if halved then
				for _, entry in ipairs(halved) do
					if entry.Index == 1 then
						crusts[position] = entry.Instance
					else
						table.insert(bases, { instance = entry.Instance, layer = share.index })
					end
				end
				slab:Destroy()
			else
				crusts[position] = slab
			end
		end
	end
	local rings = together(crusts, points)
	for position, share in ipairs(shares) do
		local crust = crusts[position]
		local fragments = rings[position]
		if fragments and #fragments > 0 then
			gather(bySite, order, fragments, share.index)
			crust:Destroy()
		elseif crust then
			-- The engine gave no cut of this layer's crust: it stands with the base.
			table.insert(bases, { instance = crust, layer = share.index })
		end
	end
	return shardsOf(frame, bySite, order, bases)
end

function LayerCuts.carve(job, frame, carve)
	local shares = job.layers
	local slabs = slabsOf(job.part, frame, shares, job.place)
	if not slabs then
		return false
	end
	local shards = {}
	for position, share in ipairs(shares) do
		local slab = slabs[position]
		if slab then
			local own = table.clone(job)
			own.template = slab
			own.frame = frame
			own.layers = nil
			local carved = carve(own, fragment, shardOf)
			if carved then
				for _, shard in ipairs(carved) do
					shard.layer = share.index
					table.insert(shards, shard)
				end
				slab:Destroy()
			else
				-- The engine would not carve this layer: its slab stands as it is.
				local shard = shardOf(slab, frame, true, nil)
				shard.layer = share.index
				table.insert(shards, shard)
			end
		end
	end
	if #shards == 0 then
		return false
	end
	shards.slash = job.slash
	return shards
end

function LayerCuts.cutAgain(job)
	local frame = job.template.CFrame
	local points = table.create(#job.points)
	for index, offset in ipairs(job.points) do
		points[index] = frame:PointToWorldSpace(offset)
	end
	local templates = table.create(#job.layered)
	for position, part in ipairs(job.layered) do
		templates[position] = part.shard
	end
	local cuts = together(templates, points)
	local bySite, order = {}, {}
	for position, part in ipairs(job.layered) do
		if cuts[position] then
			gather(bySite, order, cuts[position], part.layer)
		end
	end
	return shardsOf(frame, bySite, order, nil)
end

return LayerCuts

--[[
	Layers  -  plain blocks of a Reactor that lie on each other crack as ONE ground: a grass
	slab on the block of earth under it. Every piece of such ground is all of it that lies
	nearest one point of the crack: a fragment of each layer the point's cell passes through,
	moved as one piece.

	The engine cuts a part by the cells of ALL the points it is given, those outside the part
	included (measured in Studio, 2026-10-13: a slab cut around 16 points lying in the block
	under it gave 16 fragments whose outlines met that block's to 0.000 studs). So each layer
	is cut around the very same points, and the fragments of one point, told by their Index,
	are one piece. A patch's template is first cut into its layers' slabs by the engine, a
	plane a border, because a fragment keeps the CFrame of what it was cut from: every slab,
	and everything cut from it now or later, has the patch's own frame.

	A stacked ground is { part, frame, size, axis, layers }: frame and size are the box around
	all its layers, in the first block's own turn; axis is the box's own axis the layers lie
	along; layers, in their order along it, are { part, low, high, aligned, slice }: low and
	high along the axis, from the box's middle; aligned when the part is turned as the box is
	(a Texture is carried from such a part alone); slice the layer's own share of the box as a
	ground of its own, for Reactor/GroundDisplay ({ part, frame, size, plain }).
	Stacked: of one footprint, face on face, turned alike but for quarter turns. Blocks that
	only overlap in part crack each on its own, as every block did before.

	A skin is a layer of another kind: a thin part that is no plain block (a mesh part, a
	union: grass over a baseplate) lying flush on an end of a block or of a stack, whatever
	its outline. Its layer has `skin = true`; the ground keeps the blocks' footprint, so what
	of a skin hangs over it is never opened. A skin's share of a patch is what the engine
	finds of the skin inside that share (Reactor/LayerCuts), and what is intact of it is
	drawn by Reactor/SkinDisplay, never as boxes.

	Layers.grounds(parts, others) -> grounds, skins
	    The plain blocks of a Reactor as its grounds: a block in no stack and under no skin is
	    { part, frame, size }. others: the parts that may be skins, or nil; skins: those that
	    are, as a set.
	Layers.inPatch(ground, centre, size) -> shares
	    The layers' shares of a patch, a box of that centre and size in the ground's space:
	    { { index, offset, size, skin } }, offset from the patch's middle, skin the layer's
	    part when it is a skin. A job's `layers`.
	Layers.clip(ground, layer, rectangles, face) -> rectangles
	    Rectangles of the ground's face `face` as rectangles of that layer's slice.
	The cut itself is Reactor/LayerCuts.

	Maths only: the parts' CFrame and Size are read and nothing else.
]]

local Sites = require(script.Parent.Sites)

-- Two faces this near lie on each other; two lengths this near are the same.
local FLUSH = 0.05
-- An axis counts as another's when it lies along it this nearly (about a degree).
local SQUARE = 0.9998
-- A share of a patch thinner than this is none.
local THIN = 0.01
-- Stacks are looked for among this many blocks at most: every pair is tried.
local MOST_BLOCKS = 400
-- A skin is no thicker than this share of its own narrower side, and covers at least this
-- share of the face it lies on.
local SKIN_THIN = 0.2
local SKIN_COVER = 0.25
local AXES = { "X", "Y", "Z" }

local Layers = {}

local function along(axis, value)
	if axis == "X" then
		return Vector3.new(value, 0, 0)
	elseif axis == "Y" then
		return Vector3.new(0, value, 0)
	end
	return Vector3.new(0, 0, value)
end

local function withAxis(vector, axis, value)
	if axis == "X" then
		return Vector3.new(value, vector.Y, vector.Z)
	elseif axis == "Y" then
		return Vector3.new(vector.X, value, vector.Z)
	end
	return Vector3.new(vector.X, vector.Y, value)
end

-- The size of a block along another's axes, when its own axes are those in some order
-- (`relative` is its frame in the other's space); nil when it is turned otherwise.
local function sizeAlong(relative, size)
	local turned = { relative.XVector, relative.YVector, relative.ZVector }
	local lengths = {}
	for position, vector in ipairs(turned) do
		local found = nil
		for _, axis in ipairs(AXES) do
			if math.abs(vector[axis]) >= SQUARE then
				found = axis
			end
		end
		if not found or lengths[found] then
			return nil
		end
		lengths[found] = size[AXES[position]]
	end
	return Vector3.new(lengths.X, lengths.Y, lengths.Z)
end

-- The blocks that lie on `root`'s own line along one of its axes with its footprint, by that
-- axis: { part, low, high, aligned }, low and high along the axis from root's middle.
local function inLine(root, parts, taken)
	local byAxis = {}
	local frame = root.CFrame
	local own = root.Size
	for _, other in ipairs(parts) do
		if other ~= root and not taken[other] then
			local relative = frame:ToObjectSpace(other.CFrame)
			local offset = relative.Position
			local axis = nil
			local apart = 0
			for _, name in ipairs(AXES) do
				if math.abs(offset[name]) > FLUSH then
					axis = name
					apart += 1
				end
			end
			local size = apart == 1 and sizeAlong(relative, other.Size)
			if size then
				local same = true
				for _, name in ipairs(AXES) do
					if name ~= axis and math.abs(own[name] - size[name]) > FLUSH then
						same = false
					end
				end
				if same then
					local list = byAxis[axis]
					if not list then
						list = {}
						byAxis[axis] = list
					end
					table.insert(list, {
						part = other,
						low = offset[axis] - size[axis] / 2,
						high = offset[axis] + size[axis] / 2,
						aligned = relative.XVector.X >= SQUARE and relative.YVector.Y >= SQUARE and relative.ZVector.Z >= SQUARE,
					})
				end
			end
		end
	end
	return byAxis
end

-- The stack through `root` along one axis: every candidate that lies face on face with what
-- is stacked so far. Returns its members in their order and its ends, or nil for none.
local function stackOf(root, axis, candidates)
	local half = root.Size[axis] / 2
	local members = { { part = root, low = -half, high = half, aligned = true } }
	local low, high = -half, half
	local grew = true
	while grew do
		grew = false
		for position = #candidates, 1, -1 do
			local candidate = candidates[position]
			if math.abs(candidate.low - high) <= FLUSH then
				high = candidate.high
				table.insert(members, candidate)
				table.remove(candidates, position)
				grew = true
			elseif math.abs(candidate.high - low) <= FLUSH then
				low = candidate.low
				table.insert(members, candidate)
				table.remove(candidates, position)
				grew = true
			end
		end
	end
	if #members < 2 then
		return nil
	end
	table.sort(members, function(first, second)
		return first.low < second.low
	end)
	return members, low, high
end

-- A part of `others` that lies on an end of the stack from `low` to `high` along `axis` of
-- `root` as its skin: { part, low, high, aligned, skin }, or nil.
local function skinOn(root, axis, low, high, others, taken)
	local frame = root.CFrame
	local own = root.Size
	for _, other in ipairs(others) do
		if not taken[other] then
			local relative = frame:ToObjectSpace(other.CFrame)
			local size = sizeAlong(relative, other.Size)
			if size then
				local offset = relative.Position
				local from = offset[axis] - size[axis] / 2
				local to = offset[axis] + size[axis] / 2
				if math.abs(from - high) <= FLUSH or math.abs(to - low) <= FLUSH then
					local cover = 1
					local narrow = math.huge
					for _, name in ipairs(AXES) do
						if name ~= axis then
							local shared = math.min(offset[name] + size[name] / 2, own[name] / 2) - math.max(offset[name] - size[name] / 2, -own[name] / 2)
							cover *= math.max(shared, 0) / own[name]
							narrow = math.min(narrow, size[name])
						end
					end
					if cover >= SKIN_COVER and size[axis] <= narrow * SKIN_THIN then
						return { part = other, low = from, high = to, aligned = false, skin = true }
					end
				end
			end
		end
	end
	return nil
end

local function stacked(root, axis, members, low, high)
	local middle = (low + high) / 2
	local frame = root.CFrame * CFrame.new(along(axis, middle))
	local size = withAxis(root.Size, axis, high - low)
	local layers = table.create(#members)
	for position, member in ipairs(members) do
		local from = member.low - middle
		local to = member.high - middle
		layers[position] = {
			part = member.part,
			low = from,
			high = to,
			aligned = member.aligned,
			skin = member.skin,
			slice = {
				part = member.part,
				frame = frame * CFrame.new(along(axis, (from + to) / 2)),
				size = withAxis(size, axis, to - from),
				plain = not member.aligned,
			},
		}
	end
	return { part = root, frame = frame, size = size, axis = axis, layers = layers }
end

-- Adds the skin that lies on the stack, when one does; returns the stack's ends with it.
local function withSkin(root, axis, members, low, high, others, skins)
	local skin = skinOn(root, axis, low, high, others, skins)
	if not skin then
		return false, low, high
	end
	skins[skin.part] = true
	table.insert(members, skin)
	table.sort(members, function(first, second)
		return first.low < second.low
	end)
	return true, math.min(low, skin.low), math.max(high, skin.high)
end

function Layers.grounds(parts, others)
	local grounds = table.create(#parts)
	local taken = {}
	local skins = {}
	local looks = #parts > 1 and #parts <= MOST_BLOCKS
	local skinned = others ~= nil and #others > 0 and #parts <= MOST_BLOCKS
	for _, root in ipairs(parts) do
		if not taken[root] then
			taken[root] = true
			local ground = nil
			if looks then
				local byAxis = inLine(root, parts, taken)
				for _, axis in ipairs(AXES) do
					local candidates = byAxis[axis]
					if candidates and not ground then
						local members, low, high = stackOf(root, axis, candidates)
						if members then
							for _, member in ipairs(members) do
								taken[member.part] = true
							end
							if skinned then
								local _
								_, low, high = withSkin(root, axis, members, low, high, others, skins)
							end
							ground = stacked(root, axis, members, low, high)
						end
					end
				end
			end
			-- A block by itself may still lie under a skin, along any of its axes.
			if not ground and skinned then
				for _, axis in ipairs(AXES) do
					if not ground then
						local half = root.Size[axis] / 2
						local members = { { part = root, low = -half, high = half, aligned = true } }
						local found, low, high = withSkin(root, axis, members, -half, half, others, skins)
						if found then
							ground = stacked(root, axis, members, low, high)
						end
					end
				end
			end
			table.insert(grounds, ground or { part = root, frame = root.CFrame, size = root.Size })
		end
	end
	return grounds, skins
end

function Layers.inPatch(ground, centre, size)
	local axis = ground.axis
	local low = centre[axis] - size[axis] / 2
	local high = centre[axis] + size[axis] / 2
	local shares = {}
	for index, layer in ipairs(ground.layers) do
		local from = math.max(low, layer.low)
		local to = math.min(high, layer.high)
		if to - from > THIN then
			table.insert(shares, {
				index = index,
				offset = along(axis, (from + to) / 2 - centre[axis]),
				size = withAxis(size, axis, to - from),
				skin = layer.skin and layer.part or nil,
			})
		end
	end
	return shares
end

function Layers.clip(ground, layer, rectangles, face)
	if face.axis == ground.axis then
		return rectangles
	end
	local uAxis = Sites.faceAxes(face.axis)
	local middle = (layer.low + layer.high) / 2
	local clipped = {}
	for _, rectangle in ipairs(rectangles) do
		local minU, minV, maxU, maxV = rectangle.minU, rectangle.minV, rectangle.maxU, rectangle.maxV
		if uAxis == ground.axis then
			minU = math.max(minU, layer.low) - middle
			maxU = math.min(maxU, layer.high) - middle
		else
			minV = math.max(minV, layer.low) - middle
			maxV = math.min(maxV, layer.high) - middle
		end
		if maxU - minU > THIN and maxV - minV > THIN then
			table.insert(clipped, { minU = minU, minV = minV, maxU = maxU, maxV = maxV })
		end
	end
	return clipped
end

return Layers

--[[
	Momentum  -  the velocity a mesh part-icle's own motion gives its copy at this moment, for
	the moment the copy is handed to the Reactor code (Reactor/HandOver).

	A play moves its copy in keyframe steps and keeps no velocity: its motion is Speed along a
	direction, Acceleration, Drag, the Displacement graphs, a Timescale. So the velocity is
	measured, with the play's own update. One step tells how fast the play's time runs against
	real time. The play is then set exactly on its keyframe and stepped exactly one keyframe
	on: the way its copy goes, over the real time that keyframe stands for, is its velocity.
	The copy is put back where it stood.

	Momentum.of(particle, pData, now) -> Vector3, studs per second of real time
	    particle: the engine, whose UpdatePart is called. Zero for a play whose time stands
	    still, that is at the end of its life, or that a collision has stopped.
	Mutates: the play (it is stepped on, and its clock set on a keyframe) and its copy's look
	(up to two steps of its graphs); the copy's CFrame is as it was afterwards. Only for a
	play whose own motion ends here.
	Cross-file: reads and writes what UpdatePart keeps (Update.luau): _effectiveElapsed and
	AccumulatedDT (its clock, and the time gathered since its last keyframe), CurrentStep, and
	_lastEffectiveDt, the play's own time one call took. A keyframe that starts on a keyframe
	and ends on the next is the one stretch that both of UpdatePart's ways of moving agree on:
	its closed forms move by keyframes, its loops by the time gathered.
	_postUpdateCF (Engine.luau) is the pose of the last keyframe without the overlays laid
	over it since (Orientation, Z-Offset).
]]

local Momentum = {}

local ZERO = Vector3.new(0, 0, 0)
local TINY = 1e-6
-- How far past a keyframe the measuring step ends, as a share of it: on the keyframe itself a
-- rounding could leave the play one short.
local PAST = 1e-6

function Momentum.of(particle, pData, now)
	local visual = pData.VisualPart
	local shown = visual.CFrame
	local keyframeSeconds = pData.LifeTime / math.max(pData.TotalKeyFrames, 1)
	local velocity = ZERO

	local step = pData.CurrentStep
	particle:UpdatePart(pData, keyframeSeconds, now)
	local timescale = (pData._lastEffectiveDt or 0) / keyframeSeconds
	if math.abs(timescale) > TINY then
		local from = visual.CFrame.Position
		if pData.CurrentStep == step then
			from = (pData._postUpdateCF or shown).Position
		end
		-- A play in reverse steps back: floor() then needs the step to end short of the keyframe.
		local direction = math.sign(timescale)
		step = pData.CurrentStep
		pData._effectiveElapsed = step * keyframeSeconds
		pData.AccumulatedDT = 0
		local wanted = direction * keyframeSeconds * (1 + direction * PAST)
		particle:UpdatePart(pData, wanted / timescale, now)
		local took = pData._lastEffectiveDt or 0
		if pData.CurrentStep ~= step and math.abs(took) > TINY then
			velocity = (visual.CFrame.Position - from) * (timescale / took)
		end
	end
	visual.CFrame = shown
	return velocity
end

return Momentum

--[[
	Owned  -  what the entry of a Reactor does differently when its reactor is a COPY the
	runtime made: the emitted copy of a mesh part-icle that a Force has reached
	(Reactor/HandOver). Such an entry has an owner:
	  { copy, particle, source, settings, velocity, whole, context, entry, leaving, released }
	  copy       the emitted copy: the entry's reactor. The runtime's own; never pooled again.
	  particle   the copy's own play (its pData): off the engine's list since the hand-over,
	             and ended here when the owner is gone
	  source     the transformed item the copy was emitted from
	  settings   the Reactor settings read from that item's config at the emit
	  velocity   the copy's own velocity at the hand-over
	  whole      true for a copy that is never cut (a Matte's shape: a window, not a thing)
	  context    what the entry's play is registered with: the part-icle's own play token
	  entry      nil while the engine cuts the copy
	  leaving    true once the cap has sent it away (Reactor/HandOver)

	A piece that is a whole part of the copy is marked own: Reactor/Display then moves that
	part itself in place of a stand-in, so what is linked to the copy goes along (its nested
	part-icles, its emitters and trails, a Matte's twin). A copy that is in pieces is hidden
	where it was reached, and what drew on it is switched off.
	Nothing of a copy stands: it is carried by nothing. So the moment its entry is made every
	piece is let go at the copy's own velocity, and what a Force throws is thrown on top.

	Owned.mark(pieces, owner)        before the play is made: own pieces, none fixed
	Owned.adopt(entry, owner)        when the entry is made (Reactor/Entries): ties the two,
	                                 and lets every piece go
	Owned.spent(entry) -> boolean    an owned entry whose play has nothing left to show
	Owned.gone(self, owner, natural)
	    The end of an owner: its copy is destroyed and the copy's own play ended through the
	    engine's helpers. natural = true fires OnDeath and OnDestruction, as for a play that
	    ends by itself; a stop from outside (Disable, Stop Emits, Deactivate) passes false.
	    Harmless with no owner, and when called again.
	Mutates: the copy (a CLONE its own play made), never anything of the user's.
	Cross-file: Particle._reacted (Reactor/HandOver) lists the owners; gone takes one out.
	Reactor/Recarve leaves a piece marked uncut alone.
]]

local Display = require(script.Parent.Display)

local Owned = {}

function Owned.mark(pieces, owner)
	for _, piece in ipairs(pieces) do
		if not piece.shard and not piece.blockSize then
			piece.own = true
		end
		piece.fixed = nil
		piece.partStands = nil
		if owner.whole then
			piece.uncut = true
		end
	end
end

function Owned.adopt(entry, owner)
	entry.owner = owner
	owner.entry = entry
	local play = entry.play
	local pieces = play.pieces
	-- Every piece goes at once: there is nothing to hold another up.
	play.settings.Collapse = false
	local wholeCopy = #pieces == 1 and pieces[1].own == true and pieces[1].part == owner.copy
	if not wholeCopy then
		Display.quiet(owner.copy)
		local nested = owner.particle._nestedAlive
		if nested then
			nested[1] = false
		end
	end
	-- Play:place shows every piece now; a placed piece that is pushed flies at once.
	play:place()
	for index in ipairs(pieces) do
		play:_push(index, owner.velocity)
	end
	-- It was never stood up anywhere: a Return ends with the play restored and done.
	play.placed = false
end

function Owned.spent(entry)
	return entry.owner ~= nil and entry.play.awake <= 0
end

function Owned.gone(self, owner, natural)
	if not owner or owner.released then
		return
	end
	owner.released = true
	local listed = table.find(self._reacted, owner)
	if listed then
		table.remove(self._reacted, listed)
	end
	local particle = owner.particle
	local copy = owner.copy
	if natural then
		self:_fireOnDeath(particle)
		self:_fireOnDestruction(particle, copy)
	end
	self:_releaseOrDestroy(particle, copy)
	self:_reclaimPData(particle)
end

return Owned

--[[
	Patches  -  the engine's cut of the patches of a ground (Reactor/Wounds). A patch is not a
	part of the place: it is a rectangle of a ground's face, through the ground. So each is cut
	from a template, a plain block of the patch's size that is never put into the world, by the
	cut cracked ground always gets (Reactor/Shards: the crust off its base, the crust in rings
	around the hit).

	A shard's box is its place in the template's own space, so it does not matter where the
	template stands: Reactor/Wounds stands the pieces where the patch is.

	A whole square (job.whole) is the same cut every time for one size, Range and variant, so
	its shards are kept and the next such crack is answered at once, in the frame of its
	Force. Kept shards are templates only: every wound copies its own stand-ins from them
	(Reactor/Display), so any number of open wounds share one kept cut. The least recently
	used go when more than KEPT are held; a wound that still uses them holds on to them.

	Patches.cut(jobs, done)
	    jobs: { { size, hit, reach, count, seed, face, line, whole, variant }, ... }, or for a
	    rectangle a blade carves { size, count, seed, face, bladeFrame, bladeSize, slash, mode,
	    stands }, which Reactor/Shards hands to Reactor/Carve
	    (Reactor/Footprint.job: hit and line in the template's space, face = { axis, side }; a
	    job with a line is split along it, Reactor/Fissure). done(sets) is called when every
	    job is answered, sets[position] the shards of that job (Reactor/Shards) or false when
	    it asks for fewer than two pieces or the engine gave none. With every job kept, done is
	    called before cut returns; otherwise a few frames later.
	Patches.kept() -> how many cuts are held
	Patches.forget()  drops them all
]]

local Shards = require(script.Parent.Shards)

-- The kept cuts held at most.
local KEPT = 12

local Patches = {}

-- key -> { shards, used }: the cuts of whole squares, and when each was last asked for.
local kept = {}
local held = 0
local uses = 0

local function keyOf(job)
	local size = job.size
	local key = string.format("%.2f,%.2f,%.2f|%d|%.2f|%s%d|%d", size.X, size.Y, size.Z, job.count, job.reach, job.face.axis, job.face.side, job.variant)
	-- A stacked ground's cut is of its layers: where each lies in the patch.
	for _, share in ipairs(job.layers or {}) do
		key ..= string.format("|%d:%.2f,%.2f,%.2f:%.2f,%.2f,%.2f", share.index, share.offset.X, share.offset.Y, share.offset.Z, share.size.X, share.size.Y, share.size.Z)
	end
	return key
end

local function remember(key, shards)
	uses += 1
	if not kept[key] then
		held += 1
	end
	kept[key] = { shards = shards, used = uses }
	while held > KEPT do
		local oldest, least = nil, math.huge
		for name, entry in pairs(kept) do
			if entry.used < least then
				oldest, least = name, entry.used
			end
		end
		kept[oldest] = nil
		held -= 1
	end
end

function Patches.cut(jobs, done)
	local sets = table.create(#jobs, false)
	local cuts = {}
	for position, job in ipairs(jobs) do
		local key = nil
		if job.whole then
			key = keyOf(job)
		end
		local known = key and kept[key]
		if known then
			uses += 1
			known.used = uses
			sets[position] = known.shards
		elseif job.count >= 2 then
			local template = Instance.new("Part")
			template.Anchored = true
			template.Size = job.size
			-- A kept cut is drawn from its variant alone, so every Force of that size gets it.
			local seed = job.seed
			if key then
				seed = (job.variant + 1) * 104729
			end
			table.insert(cuts, {
				part = template,
				key = Shards.key(template, job.count, seed, job.hit, job.reach, false),
				count = job.count,
				seed = seed,
				hit = job.hit,
				reach = job.reach,
				face = job.face,
				line = job.line,
				bladeFrame = job.bladeFrame,
				bladeSize = job.bladeSize,
				ribbon = job.ribbon,
				ribbonFrame = job.ribbonFrame,
				always = job.always,
				slash = job.slash,
				mode = job.mode,
				stands = job.stands,
				layers = job.layers,
				-- Where the patch stands in the world: a skin is cut where it lies (Reactor/LayerCuts).
				place = job.frame,
				loose = true,
				position = position,
				keep = key,
			})
		end
	end
	Shards.prepare(cuts, function()
		for _, cut in ipairs(cuts) do
			local shards = Shards.get(cut.part, cut.key) or false
			sets[cut.position] = shards
			if cut.keep and shards then
				remember(cut.keep, shards)
			end
			cut.part:Destroy()
		end
		done(sets)
	end)
end

function Patches.kept()
	return held
end

function Patches.forget()
	kept = {}
	held = 0
end

return Patches

--[[
	Pieces  -  the parts of a Reactor that can be pushed, as records for Reactor/Play:
	{ part, rest (its CFrame now), halfExt, size, reach }.
	A part whose shape lies off its CFrame (a union made by GeometryService keeps the CFrame of
	the part it was made of) rests where its shape is: its record carries standOffset, where
	the part sits in that frame, as a shard's does, and box, that frame in the part's space.
	A Model has every BasePart under it; a Reactor that is one part has itself and every
	BasePart under it (Modules/Scatter places copies there). A transformed item inside (an
