	emitter with its own RenderTemplate) keeps to itself and is skipped with everything under
	it. Read each time a play starts, so hand edits are picked up.

	With Break = "Blocks" a part is cut into about `pieceCount` blocks (fewer for a very small
	part: Reactor/Sites.count). A plain block-shaped Part is cut here, by arithmetic
	(Reactor/Dice.cut): one record per block, with the same part, blockSize (the block's own
	size), and siblings, one list shared by all the blocks of that part, holding their places in
	the returned array. Any other part is cut by the engine around an even grid of points, and
	its blocks come as shards do (below); one the caller has no shards for stays one piece.
	The cut is the same every time for the same Reactor: each part draws from its own seed.

	With Break = "Shards" a part gives one record per shard the caller has for it:
	shardsOf(part) -> { { template, box, size, standOffset, fixed }, ... } (Reactor/Shards) or
	nil for a part that moves whole. A record's rest is the shard's own box, in the world; it
	carries shard (the template its stand-in is copied from), standOffset and siblings as a
	block does, box (the shard's box in the part's space) and siteIndex and sites (the point it
	was cut around, as its place among the points of the cut; Reactor/Recut finds by them the
	piece a point falls in). Of a part cut as cracked ground (the set has a strike), a base
	shard's record is fixed, and every other record carries strike = { origin, normal, reach,
	crust } in the world, one table for the whole part (Reactor/Crack reads it).
	Of a part carved by a blade (Reactor/Carve: the set has a slash) every record carries
	slash = { origin, normal, heading, kerf } in the world, one table for the whole part, and
	its shard's side (1 or -1) or bit mark (Reactor/Slash reads them). Such a set stands in
	for its part whatever the Break, and may be one record: the part with a slot in it. A bit
	carries `under` as well, how far its top lies under the top of the space it was cut in:
	Reactor/Play starts its flight over that, since a part with a slot stays solid. Every
	record of a set whose side is fixed (the part stands, with a slot) carries partStands,
	which is how Reactor/Display knows to leave that part solid while it is hidden.

	Pieces.parts(reactor) -> the parts collect reads, in its order: the Reactor itself when it
	is a part, then every BasePart under it outside transformed items.
	Pieces.isPlainBlock(part) -> true for a Part whose Shape is Block and that carries no mesh:
	the one kind Break = "Blocks" cuts without the engine.

	Pieces.ofShard(part, rest, shard) -> the record of one shard standing at `rest`, without the
	marks of its set (siblings, strike, sites): Reactor/Recut makes the pieces of a later cut by it.
	Pieces.ofSet(pieces, part, frame, shards, siblings, cut) -> siblings
	    Adds one record per shard of a set to `pieces`, standing where the space the set was cut
	    in stands (`frame`). siblings: the list the records join, when the set shows together
	    with others; made when nil. cut = { size, face = { axis, side } } when that space is not
	    the part itself but a patch of it (Reactor/Wounds): every record carries it, and one
	    whose box meets a side of the patch is marked atEdge (Reactor/Crack leaves it at rest
	    beyond the rim, so the patch's outline never shows against the ground around it).
	Pieces.touchesSide(box, halfExt, cut) -> whether a box of the patch's space meets its side
	Pieces.reachesFace(box, halfExt, cut) -> whether it comes up to the patch's struck face: a
	    piece of the crust's lower layer mostly does not, and is marked atFace when it does
	    (Reactor/Display gives the ground's Textures to those pieces alone)
	Pieces.ofBlock(part, rest, size) -> the record of one uncut block of a part

	Pieces.carry(pieces, own, origin, fullPose) moves the records of a Reactor that is emitted
	somewhere else (EmitAt, an event) to that place: the parts themselves stay where they are.
]]

local Dice = require(script.Parent.Dice)
local Sites = require(script.Parent.Sites)
local Fissure = require(script.Parent.Fissure)

local Pieces = {}

-- size: the edge of a cube of the volume, what a Force's Size Response goes by.
-- reach: the longest edge.
local function record(part, rest, size)
	return {
		part = part,
		rest = rest,
		halfExt = size / 2,
		size = (size.X * size.Y * size.Z) ^ (1 / 3),
		reach = math.max(size.X, size.Y, size.Z),
	}
end

-- A shape this far off its part's CFrame is told apart from one around it.
local OFF_CENTRE = 0.01

-- The record of a part that moves whole. Its box is where its shape is, which for a result of
-- the engine's solid modelling need not be around its CFrame (measured in Studio, 2026-10-13:
-- 3 studs off for a union of a 12-stud and a 10-stud block).
local function whole(part)
	local extents = part.ExtentsCFrame
	if (extents.Position - part.CFrame.Position).Magnitude < OFF_CENTRE then
		return record(part, part.CFrame, part.Size)
	end
	local piece = record(part, extents, part.ExtentsSize)
	piece.standOffset = extents:ToObjectSpace(part.CFrame)
	-- Reactor/Recarve cuts a whole part in the part's own space: where its box lies in it.
	piece.box = part.CFrame:ToObjectSpace(extents)
	return piece
end

-- A plain box: a Part whose Shape is Block and that carries no mesh of its own.
function Pieces.isPlainBlock(part)
	if part.ClassName ~= "Part" or part.Shape ~= Enum.PartType.Block then
		return false
	end
	for _, child in ipairs(part:GetChildren()) do
		if child:IsA("DataModelMesh") then
			return false
		end
	end
	return true
end

-- One whole block of a part, standing at `rest`: what Reactor/Display draws as a box of that
-- size in the part's look.
function Pieces.ofBlock(part, rest, size)
	local piece = record(part, rest, size)
	piece.blockSize = size
	return piece
end

-- looks: the layers of a stacked ground (Reactor/Layers), for a shard cut from one: each of
-- its fragments is drawn in the look of its own layer's part.
function Pieces.ofShard(part, rest, shard, looks)
	local piece = record(part, rest, shard.size)
	piece.shard = shard.template
	piece.standOffset = shard.standOffset
	piece.box = shard.box
	piece.siteIndex = shard.siteIndex
	if looks and shard.layer then
		piece.looks = looks
		piece.part = looks[shard.layer].part
		piece.plain = not looks[shard.layer].aligned
		piece.skin = looks[shard.layer].skin
		if shard.parts then
			local layered = table.create(#shard.parts)
			for position, fragment in ipairs(shard.parts) do
				local look = looks[fragment.layer]
				layered[position] = {
					shard = fragment.template,
					layer = fragment.layer,
					part = look.part,
					plain = not look.aligned,
					skin = look.skin,
					standOffset = fragment.standOffset,
					offset = fragment.offset,
					halfExt = fragment.size / 2,
				}
			end
			piece.layered = layered
		end
	end
	return piece
end

-- A box this near a side of its patch meets it.
local EDGE_SLACK = 0.05

-- How far a box of half-lengths `half` at `frame` reaches up from its middle.
local function halfHeight(frame, half)
	return math.abs(frame.XVector.Y) * half.X + math.abs(frame.YVector.Y) * half.Y + math.abs(frame.ZVector.Y) * half.Z
end

function Pieces.touchesSide(box, halfExt, cut)
	local alongX = box:VectorToWorldSpace(Vector3.new(halfExt.X, 0, 0))
	local alongY = box:VectorToWorldSpace(Vector3.new(0, halfExt.Y, 0))
	local alongZ = box:VectorToWorldSpace(Vector3.new(0, 0, halfExt.Z))
	local uAxis, vAxis = Sites.faceAxes(cut.face.axis)
	for _, axis in ipairs({ uAxis, vAxis }) do
		local reach = math.abs(alongX[axis]) + math.abs(alongY[axis]) + math.abs(alongZ[axis])
		if math.abs(box.Position[axis]) + reach > cut.size[axis] / 2 - EDGE_SLACK then
			return true
		end
	end
	return false
end

function Pieces.reachesFace(box, halfExt, cut)
	local axis = cut.face.axis
	local alongX = box:VectorToWorldSpace(Vector3.new(halfExt.X, 0, 0))
	local alongY = box:VectorToWorldSpace(Vector3.new(0, halfExt.Y, 0))
	local alongZ = box:VectorToWorldSpace(Vector3.new(0, 0, halfExt.Z))
	local reach = math.abs(alongX[axis]) + math.abs(alongY[axis]) + math.abs(alongZ[axis])
	return box.Position[axis] * cut.face.side + reach > cut.size[axis] / 2 - EDGE_SLACK
end

-- How far the top of a piece lies under the top of the box `size` at `frame` it was cut out
-- of: debris of something that still stands starts its flight that much higher (Play:_surfaced).
function Pieces.underTop(frame, size, piece)
	local top = frame.Position.Y + halfHeight(frame, size / 2)
	return math.max(top - piece.rest.Position.Y - halfHeight(piece.rest, piece.halfExt), 0)
end

function Pieces.ofSet(pieces, part, frame, shards, siblings, cut, looks)
	local strike = nil
	if shards.strike then
		strike = {
			origin = frame:PointToWorldSpace(shards.strike.origin),
			normal = frame:VectorToWorldSpace(shards.strike.normal),
			reach = shards.strike.reach,
			crust = shards.strike.crust,
		}
		-- A split's path (Reactor/Fissure), out of the cut's space into the world.
		if shards.strike.path then
			strike.path = Fissure.moved(shards.strike.path, frame, false)
		end
	end
	local slash = nil
	if shards.slash then
		slash = {
			origin = frame:PointToWorldSpace(shards.slash.origin),
			normal = frame:VectorToWorldSpace(shards.slash.normal),
			heading = frame:VectorToWorldSpace(shards.slash.heading),
			kerf = shards.slash.kerf,
		}
	end
	local partStands = nil
	if slash then
		for _, shard in ipairs(shards) do
			if shard.fixed then
				partStands = true
			end
		end
	end
	siblings = siblings or table.create(#shards)
	for _, shard in ipairs(shards) do
		local piece = Pieces.ofShard(part, frame * shard.box, shard, looks)
		piece.siblings = siblings
		piece.cut = cut
		piece.slash = slash
		piece.partStands = partStands
		piece.baked = shard.baked
		piece.side = shard.side
		piece.bit = shard.bit
		if shard.bit then
			local size = part.Size
			if cut then
				size = cut.size
			end
			piece.under = Pieces.underTop(frame, size, piece)
		end
		if shard.fixed then
			piece.fixed = true
			-- What a blade left of a ground's patch is the ground's own surface there.
			if slash and cut and Pieces.reachesFace(shard.box, piece.halfExt, cut) then
				piece.atFace = true
			end
		else
			piece.strike = strike
			piece.sites = shards.sites
			if cut and Pieces.touchesSide(shard.box, piece.halfExt, cut) then
				piece.atEdge = true
			end
			if cut and Pieces.reachesFace(shard.box, piece.halfExt, cut) then
				piece.atFace = true
			end
		end
		table.insert(pieces, piece)
		table.insert(siblings, #pieces)
	end
	return siblings
end

-- One record per shard of a part, or false when the caller has none for it.
local function addShards(pieces, part, shardsOf)
	local shards = shardsOf and shardsOf(part) or nil
	if not shards or #shards == 0 or (#shards < 2 and not shards.slash) then
		return false
	end
	Pieces.ofSet(pieces, part, part.CFrame, shards)
	return true
end

local function add(pieces, part, breakMode, pieceCount, shardsOf)
	local plainBlock = breakMode == "Blocks" and Pieces.isPlainBlock(part)
	-- What the engine cut of a part stands in for it: its shards, the blocks of a part that
	-- is no plain box, or what a blade left of it, whatever the Break.
	if addShards(pieces, part, shardsOf) then
		return
	end
	if not plainBlock then
		table.insert(pieces, whole(part))
		return
	end
	local blocks = Dice.cut(part.Size, Sites.count(part.Size, pieceCount), Sites.sequence(#pieces * 7919 + 13))
	if #blocks == 1 then
		table.insert(pieces, record(part, part.CFrame, part.Size))
		return
	end
	local siblings = table.create(#blocks)
	for _, block in ipairs(blocks) do
		local piece = record(part, part.CFrame * CFrame.new(block.offset.X, block.offset.Y, block.offset.Z), block.size)
		piece.blockSize = block.size
		piece.siblings = siblings
		table.insert(pieces, piece)
		table.insert(siblings, #pieces)
	end
end

local function visit(parent, parts)
	for _, child in ipairs(parent:GetChildren()) do
		if not child:GetAttribute("Transformed") then
			if child:IsA("BasePart") and not child:IsA("Terrain") then
				table.insert(parts, child)
			end
			visit(child, parts)
		end
	end
end

function Pieces.parts(reactor)
	local parts = {}
	if reactor:IsA("BasePart") then
		table.insert(parts, reactor)
	end
	visit(reactor, parts)
	return parts
end

-- Rewrites every rest pose for a Reactor whose frame is `own` and that is emitted at `origin`.
-- A full pose brings the layout into the origin's frame; otherwise it is only moved there and
-- every piece keeps its rotation.
function Pieces.carry(pieces, own, origin, fullPose)
	-- A strike is shared by the pieces of its crack, a slash by those of its cut: each is
	-- moved once.
	local strikes = {}
	local slashes = {}
	for _, piece in ipairs(pieces) do
		if piece.strike then
			strikes[piece.strike] = true
		end
		if piece.slash then
			slashes[piece.slash] = true
		end
	end
	if fullPose then
		for _, piece in ipairs(pieces) do
			piece.rest = origin * own:ToObjectSpace(piece.rest)
		end
		for strike in pairs(strikes) do
			strike.origin = origin:PointToWorldSpace(own:PointToObjectSpace(strike.origin))
			strike.normal = origin:VectorToWorldSpace(own:VectorToObjectSpace(strike.normal))
			if strike.path then
				strike.path = Fissure.moved(Fissure.moved(strike.path, own, true), origin, false)
			end
		end
		for slash in pairs(slashes) do
			slash.origin = origin:PointToWorldSpace(own:PointToObjectSpace(slash.origin))
			slash.normal = origin:VectorToWorldSpace(own:VectorToObjectSpace(slash.normal))
			slash.heading = origin:VectorToWorldSpace(own:VectorToObjectSpace(slash.heading))
		end
		return
	end
	local shift = origin.Position - own.Position
	for _, piece in ipairs(pieces) do
		piece.rest = piece.rest + shift
	end
	for strike in pairs(strikes) do
		strike.origin = strike.origin + shift
		if strike.path then
			strike.path = Fissure.moved(strike.path, CFrame.new(shift), false)
		end
	end
	for slash in pairs(slashes) do
		slash.origin = slash.origin + shift
	end
end

-- leftOut(part) -> true for a part that gives no records: a ground, whose cracks are
-- wounds of their own (Reactor/Wounds).
function Pieces.collect(reactor, breakMode, pieceCount, shardsOf, leftOut)
	local pieces = {}
	for _, part in ipairs(Pieces.parts(reactor)) do
		if not (leftOut and leftOut(part)) then
			add(pieces, part, breakMode, pieceCount or 50, shardsOf)
		end
	end
	return pieces
end

return Pieces

--[[
	Play  -  one disturbed Reactor: which pieces are out of place, on what paths, and what happens
	once they have all come to rest (the Fade and the Return are Reactor/After). Logic only: instances are reached through `display`
	(Reactor/Display in the runtime, a recorder in the tests) and the world through `castRay`, so
	all of it runs under the luau CLI. What Forces do to a play (watch, strike, kickAgain and
	the kicks themselves) is Reactor/Follow, mixed in below.

	A piece is { rest = CFrame, halfExt = Vector3, size = number, reach = number }.
	States: RESTING (never pushed: the original stands, the play shows nothing for it), FLYING
	(on a path), LANDED (its path ended; it lies where it fell), GONE (sunk away or lost), DRIVEN
	(carried by a Continuous Force: Reactor/Driven steps it live until no Force holds it).

	A pushed piece flies a path from Rocks/Trajectory: a plain arc at once, replaced by the whole
	built path (bounces, roll-out, rest pose) within the per-frame build budget. A push on a piece
	already out of place rebuilds its path from where it is and how fast it goes. The plain arc
	knows no ground: whoever takes a piece's place and speed from its flight (a second push, a
	flow that takes it up: Reactor/Driven) has the path built first (Play:_buildPath), or a
	long frame would put the piece half a second down the arc, under the ground.

	A Force's strength is a distance: how far, in studs, it throws a piece (Fields.throwSpeed
	turns it into a speed under the piece's own gravity). Hold is a distance too: a throw no
	longer than Hold leaves the piece standing.

	With settings.Collapse, a piece left standing with no chain of standing neighbours to
	something that carries it (Reactor/Support) is let go and falls. The graph is built the first
	time a piece of the play wakes.

	Cracked ground (Reactor/Crack): a piece that is fixed (the base under the crust) is never
	pushed, by a Force or by a collapse. A crust piece (it carries a strike) that an Impulse
	reaches and does not throw is stood a little out of place instead: sunk and tipped in the
	crater, heaved on the rim, moved by a hair beyond; outside the crater no Force throws it.
	Such a piece stays RESTING. A Continuous Force cracks nothing. A later Impulse elsewhere on
	the same ground cracks it again (Reactor/Recut): pieces are added to the play while it runs,
	and a piece that was cut again is retired (piece.retired, GONE for good).
	A part carved by a Force's blade (Reactor/Carve) is Reactor/Slash's to show and let go; a
	side that slides off flies a path led by a slide, kept when its flight is built.

	settings: Hold, HoldSpread, Collapse, isAnchored(index) (asked once per piece when Collapse
	is on), After ("Stay" | "Fade" | "Return"), AfterDelay, AfterTime, closes (a wound of a
	ground: a Fade ends with the ground grown back and the play done, Reactor/After.close),
	MaxPieces, MaxAirTime (seconds a piece may fly: its path looks for ground that long, and
	one still in the air after it is taken away; never less than a second),
	wakeBudget (stand-ins made per frame), buildBudget (paths built per frame), and
	the functions rollGravity(),
	rollBounciness(), rollFriction(), rollTumble() (radians per second) and random() (0 to 1).
	display: wake(index) shows a stand-in for a piece, hides the original and returns how many
	stand-ins it made (a block brings its siblings); move(indices, frames, count) places stand-ins; drop(index) removes one for good; restore(index) removes it
	and shows the original again.

	A play can be placed (Play:place): every piece is given its stand-in at once and stands at
	rest, for a Reactor emitted somewhere other than where its parts are. Nothing moves until a
	Force pushes; a pushed piece then goes at once, its stand-in being there already, and a
	Return ends with the Reactor standing at that place again.

	step(dt) returns "active" while anything moves or is still to come, or a Force it follows
	is still alive, "dormant" when the pieces lie where they fell and nothing more happens
	without a new Force, and "done" when every piece is back at rest and the play can be thrown
	away. The wait before a Fade or a Return (AfterDelay) counts from the moment nothing moves
	any more: a Force that is merely alive does not hold it up, one that may yet move a piece
	does (play.held, Reactor/Follow). play.busy says whether this step found anything moving.
]]

local Trajectory = require(script.Parent.Parent.Rocks.Trajectory)
local Driven = require(script.Parent.Driven)
local Support = require(script.Parent.Support)
local After = require(script.Parent.After)
local Crack = require(script.Parent.Crack)
local Follow = require(script.Parent.Follow)

local RESTING = 0
local FLYING = 1
local LANDED = 2
local GONE = 3
local DRIVEN = Driven.STATE

local ZERO = Vector3.new(0, 0, 0)
local UP = Vector3.new(0, 1, 0)
local TINY = 1e-4
-- The least a play's Max Air Time counts as.
local LEAST_AIR_TIME = 1
-- How far above a surface a piece buried past its middle starts its flight.
local SURFACE_MARGIN = 0.02

local Play = {}
Play.__index = Play
-- watch, strike, kickAgain, _takeTime, _applyImpulse and _followForces: what Forces do to a play.
for name, method in pairs(Follow.methods) do
	Play[name] = method
end

function Play.new(pieces, settings, display, castRay)
	local self = setmetatable({}, Play)
	self.pieces = pieces
	self.settings = settings
	self.display = display
	self.castRay = castRay
	-- A piece whose built path meets no ground within this many seconds is taken away then.
	self.airTime = math.max(settings.MaxAirTime, LEAST_AIR_TIME)
	-- Rocks/Trajectory.build's rules for a piece: it leaves walls, it starts where it stood, on
	-- the ground or sunk into it, which a Rocks chunk does not, ground is looked for all
	-- through its air time, and a roll that runs off an edge falls on.
	self.pathRules = { offWalls = true, fromRest = true, airTime = self.airTime, offEdges = true }
	self.clock = 0
	self.state = table.create(#pieces, RESTING)
	-- Per piece, set at its first launch.
	self.path = {}
	self.pathStart = {}
	self.pathBuilt = {}
	self.gravity = {}
	self.bounciness = {}
	self.friction = {}
	self.lastFrame = {}
	self.landedAfter = {}
	self.holdOf = {}
	-- Reactor/Support's graph, and whether pieces have left since it was last walked.
	self.support = nil
	self.supportStale = false
	-- record -> the pieces it has already reached.
	self.kicks = {}
	self.flying = {}
	-- The pieces a Continuous Force carries, and their live state (Reactor/Driven).
	self.driven = {}
	-- index -> the way a Continuous Force carried the piece (Reactor/Driven).
	self.track = {}
	self.drivePosition = {}
	self.driveRotation = {}
	self.driveVelocity = {}
	self.driveSpin = {}
	self.pendingWake = {}
	self.pendingPush = {}
	-- Cracked ground (Reactor/Crack): the pieces queued or stood out of place, and their poses.
	self.cracked = {}
	self.crackPower = {}
	self.crackFrame = {}
	self.pendingCrack = {}
	-- record -> true while a later crack of its own is being cut (Reactor/Recrack): until it
	-- is in, that Force leaves the standing crust alone, and then kicks it late (kickAgain).
	-- "all" while a blade's later cut is being made (Reactor/Recarve): it leaves every piece.
	self.recracking = {}
	self.buildQueue = {}
	self.moveIndices = {}
	self.moveFrames = {}
	self.moveCount = 0
	-- Pieces with a stand-in, and pieces whose original is hidden (a faded piece is still hidden).
	self.awake = 0
	self.hidden = 0
	-- True once Play:place has stood every piece up as a stand-in.
	self.placed = false
	self.phase = "live"
	self.phaseTime = 0
	self.idleFor = 0
	-- held: a Force that is still alive may yet move a piece (Reactor/Follow). busy: something
	-- moves, is still to come or is on its way back; Reactor/Wounds holds a group's wait by it.
	self.held = false
	self.busy = false
	-- The time sources of the Forces that have moved a piece of this play (Force/Registry:
	-- record.time, a Container's, and record.ownTime, the Force's own Timescale). Reactor/init
	-- steps the play by the slowest of them.
	self.times = {}
	return self
end

-- Where a piece is for a Force. Cracked ground is asked at rest, however a crack has stood it;
-- any other piece that stands out of place (the pieces of a cut piece) where it stands.
function Play:_position(index)
	if self.state[index] == RESTING then
		local piece = self.pieces[index]
		return ((not piece.strike and self.crackFrame[index]) or piece.rest).Position
	end
	return self.lastFrame[index].Position
end

local function randomAxis(random)
	local axis = Vector3.new(random() * 2 - 1, random() * 2 - 1, random() * 2 - 1)
	if axis.Magnitude < TINY then
		return UP
	end
	return axis.Unit
end

-- A piece's own Hold: the Reactor's, spread by HoldSpread, rolled the first time it is asked for.
function Play:_holdOf(index)
	local hold = self.holdOf[index]
	if hold == nil then
		local settings = self.settings
		hold = settings.Hold * (1 + settings.HoldSpread * (settings.random() * 2 - 1))
		self.holdOf[index] = hold
	end
	return hold
end

-- A piece's own gravity, bounciness and friction, rolled the first time they are asked for.
function Play:_rolled(index)
	local settings = self.settings
	if self.gravity[index] == nil then
		self.gravity[index] = settings.rollGravity()
		self.bounciness[index] = settings.rollBounciness()
		self.friction[index] = settings.rollFriction()
	end
	return self.gravity[index]
end

-- Puts a piece on a plain arc from `frame` and queues the whole path for building.
function Play:_launch(index, frame, velocity, spin)
	local settings = self.settings
	-- Only a flight that starts where a Force let the piece go has that Force's way before it.
	local track = self.track[index]
	if track and not track.kept then
		self.track[index] = nil
	elseif track then
		track.kept = nil
	end
	self:_rolled(index)
	if spin.Magnitude < TINY then
		spin = randomAxis(settings.random) * settings.rollTumble()
	end
	self.path[index] = Trajectory.ballistic(frame.Position, velocity, frame.Rotation, spin)
	self.pathStart[index] = self.clock
	self.pathBuilt[index] = false
	self.lastFrame[index] = frame
	table.insert(self.buildQueue, index)
	if self.state[index] ~= FLYING then
		self.state[index] = FLYING
		table.insert(self.flying, index)
	end
end

-- Where a resting piece starts its flight: from `stood` when it stands out of place (a crack
-- sank it, Reactor/Crack), else from its rest. One buried past its middle starts just above
-- the surface it lies in: a ray cast from inside the ground does not find it, and a flight
-- begun in there never lands. A piece of cracked ground's lower layer lies wholly under that
-- surface (Reactor/Crack.buried), and so may a bit of what a blade took out of a part
-- (piece.under, Reactor/Pieces).
function Play:_surfaced(index, stood)
	local piece = self.pieces[index]
	local rest = stood or piece.rest
	local reach = Support.worldHalf(piece).Y + SURFACE_MARGIN + Crack.buried(piece, rest.Position) + (piece.under or 0)
	local over = self.castRay(rest.Position + UP * reach, UP * -reach)
	if not over then
		return rest
	end
	return rest + UP * (over.Position.Y - rest.Position.Y + SURFACE_MARGIN)
end

-- A push on one piece. A resting piece waits for its stand-in; a moving one is re-launched now.
function Play:_push(index, push)
	local state = self.state[index]
	if state == GONE or self.pieces[index].fixed then
		return
	end
	if state == RESTING then
		if self.placed then
			-- Its stand-in stands there already: it goes now, and counts against no cap.
			self:_launch(index, self:_surfaced(index, self.crackFrame[index]), push, ZERO)
			self.supportStale = true
			return
		end
		if self.pendingPush[index] then
			self.pendingPush[index] += push
			return
		end
		if self.awake + #self.pendingWake >= self.settings.MaxPieces then
			return
		end
		self.pendingPush[index] = push
		table.insert(self.pendingWake, index)
		return
	end
	if state == DRIVEN then
		self.driveVelocity[index] += push
		return
	end
	self:_buildPath(index)
	local elapsed = self.clock - self.pathStart[index]
	local gravity = self.gravity[index]
	local frame = Trajectory.evaluate(self.path[index], elapsed, gravity)
	local velocity, spin = Trajectory.velocity(self.path[index], elapsed, gravity)
	self:_launch(index, frame, velocity + push, spin)
end

-- Stand-ins for the pieces waiting to move, until the frame's budget of new stand-ins is spent.
function Play:_wakePending()
	local pending = self.pendingWake
	local budget = self.settings.wakeBudget
	local taken = 0
	local made = 0
	while taken < #pending and made < budget do
		taken += 1
		local index = pending[taken]
		local push = self.pendingPush[index]
		self.pendingPush[index] = nil
		made += self.display.wake(index) or 1
		self.awake += 1
		self.hidden += 1
		-- A cracked piece flies from where it was stood, or from the surface over that.
		self:_launch(index, self:_surfaced(index, self.crackFrame[index]), push, ZERO)
	end
	if taken == 0 then
		return
	end
	self.supportStale = true
	local remaining = {}
	for position = taken + 1, #pending do
		table.insert(remaining, pending[position])
	end
	self.pendingWake = remaining
end

-- Lets go of every standing piece that has lost its last chain to something that carries it.
-- Those wake over the next frames like any other, and may bring more down in their turn.
function Play:_collapse()
	self.supportStale = false
	local settings = self.settings
	if not settings.Collapse then
		return
	end
	if not self.support then
		self.support = Support.build(self.pieces, settings.isAnchored)
	end
	local fallen = Support.unsupported(self.support, function(index)
		return self.state[index] == RESTING and self.pendingPush[index] == nil
	end)
	for _, index in ipairs(fallen) do
		self:_push(index, ZERO)
	end
end

-- The whole path of one flying piece in place of its plain arc, now, whatever the budget.
-- Nothing to do for a piece whose path is built or that does not fly.
function Play:_buildPath(index)
	if self.state[index] ~= FLYING or self.pathBuilt[index] then
		return
	end
	-- The flight is the last stretch of an unbuilt path: a slide may lead it.
	local plain = self.path[index]
	local start = plain.segs[#plain.segs]
	local built = Trajectory.build(start.p0, start.v0, start.rot0, start.w, self.pieces[index].halfExt, 1,
		self.gravity[index], self.bounciness[index], self.friction[index], self.castRay, self.pathRules)
	if plain.lead then
		built = Trajectory.led(plain.lead, built)
	end
	self.path[index] = built
	self.pathBuilt[index] = true
end

-- Whole paths in place of plain arcs, as many as the frame's budget allows.
function Play:_buildPaths()
	local queue = self.buildQueue
	local taken = math.min(#queue, self.settings.buildBudget)
	if taken == 0 then
		return
	end
	for position = 1, taken do
		self:_buildPath(queue[position])
	end
	local remaining = {}
	for position = taken + 1, #queue do
		table.insert(remaining, queue[position])
	end
	self.buildQueue = remaining
end

-- The poses of this frame are gathered in the move lists (flying pieces, then driven ones) and
-- handed to the display in one go. The lists are cut to `count`: a display may pass
-- them straight to BulkMoveTo.
function Play:_flush(count)
	local indices = self.moveIndices
	local frames = self.moveFrames
	for position = count + 1, self.moveCount do
		indices[position] = nil
		frames[position] = nil
	end
	self.moveCount = count
	if count > 0 then
		self.display.move(indices, frames, count)
	end
end

-- Returns how many poses it put in the move lists.
function Play:_moveFlying()
	local flying = self.flying
	local count = 0
	local position = 1
	while position <= #flying do
		local index = flying[position]
		-- A piece a Continuous Force took over is dropped from the list here.
		if self.state[index] ~= FLYING then
			local last = #flying
			flying[position] = flying[last]
			flying[last] = nil
			continue
		end
		local path = self.path[index]
		local elapsed = self.clock - self.pathStart[index]
		-- A lost piece leaves before it is listed: the display moves every piece it is handed,
		-- and one whose stand-in is gone stops the whole move (Reactor/Display.move).
		if self.pathBuilt[index] and path.restT == math.huge and elapsed > self.airTime then
			local last = #flying
			flying[position] = flying[last]
			flying[last] = nil
			self.state[index] = GONE
			self.display.drop(index)
			self.awake -= 1
			continue
		end
		local frame = Trajectory.evaluate(path, elapsed, self.gravity[index])
		self.lastFrame[index] = frame
		count += 1
		self.moveIndices[count] = index
		self.moveFrames[count] = frame

		if self.pathBuilt[index] and elapsed >= path.restT then
			local last = #flying
			flying[position] = flying[last]
			flying[last] = nil
			self.state[index] = LANDED
			self.landedAfter[index] = path.restT
		else
			position += 1
		end
	end
	return count
end

function Play:step(dt)
	self.clock += dt
	self.busy = true
	if self.phase == "fading" then
		return After.fade(self, dt)
	elseif self.phase == "returning" then
		return After.back(self, dt)
	elseif self.phase == "closing" then
		return After.close(self, dt)
	end

	self:_followForces()
	self:_wakePending()
	if self.supportStale then
		self:_collapse()
	end
	self:_buildPaths()
	self:_flush(Crack.settle(self, Driven.step(self, dt, self:_moveFlying())))

	self.busy = #self.flying > 0 or #self.driven > 0 or #self.pendingWake > 0 or #self.pendingCrack > 0 or next(self.recracking) ~= nil or self.held
	if self.busy then
		self.idleFor = 0
		return "active"
	end
	-- A Force that is still alive keeps the play at work, so it may yet be pushed, but the
	-- wait below runs on: it counts from the moment the pieces lay still (Reactor/Follow).
	local followed = next(self.kicks) ~= nil
	if self.hidden == 0 then
		return if followed then "active" else "done"
	end
	local after = self.settings.After
	-- Something to fade or to bring back: what has landed and, for a Return, what is cracked.
	local settles = self.awake > 0 and After.anyLanded(self)
	if after == "Return" and next(self.crackFrame) ~= nil then
		settles = true
	end
	-- A wound gives its ground back whatever was moved in it (After.close).
	if self.settings.closes then
		settles = true
	end
	if after == "Stay" or not settles then
		return if followed then "active" else "dormant"
	end
	self.idleFor += dt
	if self.idleFor >= self.settings.AfterDelay then
		self.phaseTime = 0
		self.phase = After.begin(self)
	end
	return "active"
end

-- Stands the whole Reactor up as stand-ins, the originals hidden: for a play whose rest poses
-- are somewhere other than the parts (Reactor/Pieces.carry). Nothing is let go: a piece stays
-- where it stands until a Force pushes it or it loses its support. Called once, on a new play.
function Play:place()
	if self.placed then
		return
	end
	self.placed = true
	for index in ipairs(self.pieces) do
		self.display.wake(index)
		self.awake += 1
		self.hidden += 1
	end
end

-- Everything back: stand-ins removed, originals shown, the play as new. A piece that was cut
-- again stays out of it: its pieces stand for it.
function Play:restore()
	for index, piece in ipairs(self.pieces) do
		if self.state[index] ~= RESTING or self.placed or self.crackFrame[index] then
			self.display.restore(index)
			self.state[index] = RESTING
			if piece.retired then
				self.state[index] = GONE
			end
		end
	end
	self.placed = false
	self.flying = {}
	self.driven = {}
	self.track = {}
	self.pendingWake = {}
	self.pendingPush = {}
	self.cracked = {}
	self.crackPower = {}
	self.crackFrame = {}
	self.pendingCrack = {}
	self.buildQueue = {}
	self.kicks = {}
	self:_flush(0)
	self.awake = 0
	self.hidden = 0
	self.phase = "live"
	self.phaseTime = 0
	self.idleFor = 0
end

Play.RESTING = RESTING
Play.FLYING = FLYING
Play.LANDED = LANDED
Play.GONE = GONE
Play.DRIVEN = DRIVEN

return Play

--[[
	Reach  -  whether a Force reaches a part-icle that may react (Reactor/HandOver). Numbers only:
	a place, a size, a Hold. These are a Reactor piece's own rules (Reactor/Follow,
	Reactor/Driven), asked of one thing that is not a piece yet: inside the field's shape,
	behind its front, and moved by it more than the Hold. Nothing here makes a table.
	Reactor/HandOver asks only inside a ball round the shape.

	Reach.moved(record, position, extent, hold, age) -> whether the record's Force moves it now
	    extent  the part-icle's Size; a Force's Size Response goes by the cube of its volume
	    hold    the throw, in studs, it shrugs off (an Impulse), or the speed (a Continuous Force)
	    age     seconds since the part-icle was emitted
	Reach.inBlade(record, position, radius, age) -> whether the box of a Linear record, grown by
	    the radius, holds the place and its front has come that far: the first test for a blade
	    (Reactor/Blade.touches decides)

	A part-icle emitted where an Impulse's front has already passed is left alone: the blast
	went by before it was there. A Force that is itself on its way (record.moving, Force/init)
	reaches whatever it comes to.
	Cross-file: the two formulas are Follow's (throw against Hold) and Driven's (speed against
	Hold), without a kick's Variation: a part-icle is asked every frame, and a roll a frame
	would let it through in the end.
]]

local Fields = require(script.Parent.Parent.Force.Fields)

local Reach = {}

-- Whether an Impulse's front had passed a place `distance` along its way before a part-icle
-- `age` seconds old was emitted there.
local function passedBefore(record, distance, age)
	if record.actsAs ~= "Impulse" or record.moving then
		return false
	end
	local ageThen = record.age - age
	if ageThen <= 0 then
		return false
	end
	if record.travelSpeed <= 0 then
		return true
	end
	return record.travelSpeed * ageThen >= distance
end

function Reach.moved(record, position, extent, hold, age)
	local strength = record.strength
	local direction, distance, distance01 = Fields.sample(record.field, position, strength < 0)
	if not direction or distance > record.front then
		return false
	end
	if passedBefore(record, distance, age) then
		return false
	end
	local size = (extent.X * extent.Y * extent.Z) ^ (1 / 3)
	local moves = math.abs(strength) * Fields.kept(record.falloff, distance01) * Fields.sizeShare(size, record.sizeResponse)
	return moves > hold
end

function Reach.inBlade(record, position, radius, age)
	local field = record.field
	local point = field.origin:PointToObjectSpace(position)
	local forward = -point.Z
	if forward > field.range + radius or forward < field.inner - radius then
		return false
	end
	if math.abs(point.X) > field.halfWidth + radius or math.abs(point.Y) > field.halfHeight + radius then
		return false
	end
	if forward - radius > record.front then
		return false
	end
	return not passedBefore(record, forward, age)
end

return Reach

--[[
	Recarve  -  a blade through a Reactor that is out of place already. A part is carved for
	the first Force that cuts it (Reactor/CutPlan, Reactor/Carve); every cutting Force after it
	cuts the PIECES its blade touches, as often as Forces come, while the play has room for
	more (its Max Pieces).

	A piece is cut where it is: standing in its part, stood out of place, lying where it fell
	or in the air. The blade is taken into the piece's own space, the engine cuts the piece's
	own shard there (a whole part is cut as a part is, a block of Reactor/Dice as a box of its
	size), and the results stand in for the piece exactly where it is when they come: a
	standing piece's as standing pieces, a lying piece's as lying ones (LANDED, on a path that
	only lies there, so a Fade sinks them and a Return takes them home), a flying piece's in
	flight, at the speed and spin it had. The piece itself leaves the play for good
	(piece.retired), as one cut again by a crack does (Reactor/Recut).

	A ground's gash is cut again the same way (Reactor/Wounds asks for every open wound a
	later blade crosses): what the first blade left of a patch stands, so what the next one
	leaves of it stands too, and still shows the ground's own surface. A PART with a slot in
	it stands only while it is in one piece: a later blade that parts it gives two ordinary
	sides, which Reactor/Slash lets go by its own rules, so a shape cut out of it comes loose.

	What stands is cut before the debris that lies about, and is cut even when the play has
	no room left; a cut whose debris or breaking has no room is made as Halves.

	Not cut again: a piece carried by a Continuous Force, cracked ground and the base under
	its crust (Reactor/Crack: a gash stops at an open crack), the debris of a Band (litter:
	cutting it would cost a cut a bit and show nothing), a piece whose longest edge is under
	LEAST_PIECE, and the pieces of this Force's own cut.

	The cut takes a few frames. Until it is in, its Force leaves the whole play alone
	(play.recracking[record] = "all") and then kicks late (Play:kickAgain), which also lets
	the new sides go (Reactor/Slash). A second request waits for the first.

	Recarve.request(entry, record, kicked, isCurrent, revive)
	    entry: Reactor/Entries', with play, pieceCount and breaks (whether the Reactor's Break
	    gives a part pieces of its own, which Cut = Pieces breaks the sides into). Keeps
	    entry.carves (the requests waiting) and entry.carved (the Forces that have asked: one
	    cut a Force). kicked, isCurrent, revive: as Reactor/Recrack.request takes them.
	Recarve.plan(play, blade, record, pieceCount) -> { blade, record, jobs }
	    jobs: Reactor/Carve's, each with the index of the piece it cuts; nearest the Force first.
	Recarve.apply(play, plan, results) -> the places of the new pieces in play.pieces
]]

local Trajectory = require(script.Parent.Parent.Rocks.Trajectory)
local Blade = require(script.Parent.Blade)
local Pieces = require(script.Parent.Pieces)
local Shards = require(script.Parent.Shards)
local Sites = require(script.Parent.Sites)
local Carve = require(script.Parent.Carve)

local RESTING = 0
local FLYING = 1
local LANDED = 2
local GONE = 3

local IDENTITY = CFrame.new(0, 0, 0)
local UP = Vector3.new(0, 1, 0)
local TINY = 1e-6
-- A piece whose longest edge is under this many studs is not cut again.
local LEAST_PIECE = 1
-- Pieces cut for one Force.
local MOST_JOBS = 64
-- A point a side breaks around keeps this far inside the piece's box.
local INSET = 0.9
-- Debris of a kerf: about one bit for this many studs square of the piece's face (Reactor/Carve).
local BIT_AREA = 9
local LEAST_BITS = 3

local Recarve = {}

-- Where a piece is now.
local function poseOf(play, index)
	if play.state[index] == RESTING then
		return play.crackFrame[index] or play.pieces[index].rest
	end
	return play.lastFrame[index]
end

local function carvable(play, index, record)
	local piece = play.pieces[index]
	local state = play.state[index]
	if state ~= RESTING and state ~= LANDED and state ~= FLYING then
		return false
	end
	-- A Matte's shape that has reacted is a window, never cut (Reactor/Owned).
	if piece.retired or piece.bit or piece.uncut or play.pendingPush[index] ~= nil or piece.reach < LEAST_PIECE then
		return false
	end
	-- Cracked ground and the base under its crust are Reactor/Crack's.
	if piece.strike or (piece.fixed and not piece.slash) then
		return false
	end
	if piece.slash and piece.slash.by == record then
		return false
	end
	return piece.shard ~= nil or piece.blockSize ~= nil or Shards.cuttable(piece.part)
end

-- How many pieces a job is expected to add to the play.
local function growth(piece, mode, count)
	if mode == "Pieces" then
		return math.max(count, 1)
	elseif mode == "Band" then
		local size = piece.halfExt * 2
		local longest = math.max(size.X, size.Y, size.Z)
		local middling = size.X + size.Y + size.Z - longest - math.min(size.X, size.Y, size.Z)
		return 1 + math.clamp(math.round(longest * middling / BIT_AREA), LEAST_BITS, Carve.MOST_BITS)
	end
	return 1
end

-- The cut of one piece by the blade, in the piece's own space.
local function jobFor(play, index, blade, record, pieceCount)
	local piece = play.pieces[index]
	local box = piece.box or IDENTITY
	-- The space the piece's box is told in, where what the engine cuts lies: a shard's
	-- template where it was cut, a whole part where it is, a block at the origin.
	local space = IDENTITY
	if piece.shard then
		space = piece.shard.ExtentsCFrame * box:Inverse()
	elseif not piece.blockSize then
		space = piece.part.CFrame
	end
	-- The world as it is now, seen from that space: the blade goes where the piece has gone.
	local inSpace = box * poseOf(play, index):Inverse()
	local mode = record.cut.mode
	local seed = Sites.seedAt(blade.origin) + index
	-- Asked with the whole part: all its pieces are cut by the same ribbon of a jagged blade.
	local ribbon, ribbonFrame = Blade.ribbonFor(blade, piece.part.CFrame, piece.part.Size, inSpace)
	local count = 0
	local points = nil
	if mode == "Pieces" and pieceCount >= 2 then
		local size = piece.halfExt * 2
		local whole = piece.part.Size
		local share = size.X * size.Y * size.Z / math.max(whole.X * whole.Y * whole.Z, TINY)
		count = math.round(math.min(pieceCount * share, Sites.MAX))
		if count >= 2 then
			local random = Sites.sequence(seed)
			points = table.create(count)
			for position = 1, count do
				local inBox = Vector3.new((random() - 0.5) * size.X, (random() - 0.5) * size.Y, (random() - 0.5) * size.Z) * INSET
				points[position] = box:PointToWorldSpace(inBox)
			end
		else
			count = 0
		end
	end
	return {
		index = index,
		part = piece.part,
		template = piece.shard,
		blockSize = piece.blockSize,
		baked = piece.baked,
		frame = space,
		bladeFrame = inSpace * blade.frame,
		bladeSize = blade.size,
		ribbon = ribbon,
		ribbonFrame = ribbonFrame,
		slash = {
			origin = inSpace:PointToWorldSpace(blade.origin),
			normal = inSpace:VectorToWorldSpace(blade.normal),
			heading = inSpace:VectorToWorldSpace(blade.heading),
			kerf = blade.kerf,
		},
		mode = mode,
		count = count,
		points = points,
		seed = seed,
		-- A ground's patch stands however it is cut; a part does while it is in one piece.
		stands = piece.fixed == true and piece.cut ~= nil,
	}
end

function Recarve.plan(play, blade, record, pieceCount)
	local live = 0
	local touched = {}
	for index, piece in ipairs(play.pieces) do
		if play.state[index] ~= GONE then
			live += 1
		end
		if carvable(play, index, record) then
			local pose = poseOf(play, index)
			if Blade.touches(blade, pose, piece.halfExt * 2) then
				table.insert(touched, { index = index, fixed = piece.fixed == true, away = (pose.Position - blade.origin).Magnitude })
			end
		end
	end
	table.sort(touched, function(first, second)
		if first.fixed ~= second.fixed then
			return first.fixed
		end
		return first.away < second.away
	end)
	local settings = play.settings
	local room = (settings.MostPieces or settings.MaxPieces) - live
	-- Debris and breaking are made within Max Pieces itself; the bare cut within the room a
	-- wound's later cracks have (Reactor/WoundBudget).
	local spare = settings.MaxPieces - live
	local jobs = {}
	for _, entry in ipairs(touched) do
		if #jobs >= MOST_JOBS then
			break
		end
		local job = jobFor(play, entry.index, blade, record, pieceCount)
		local grows = growth(play.pieces[entry.index], job.mode, job.count)
		if grows > math.min(room, spare) then
			job.mode = "Halves"
			job.count = 0
			job.points = nil
			grows = 1
		end
		if grows <= room or entry.fixed then
			room -= grows
			table.insert(jobs, job)
		end
	end
	return { blade = blade, record = record, jobs = jobs }
end

local function discard(shards)
	for _, shard in ipairs(shards or {}) do
		shard.template:Destroy()
	end
end

-- Puts the results of one job in the place of the piece it cut.
local function replace(play, plan, job, shards, taken, movedIndices, movedFrames)
	local index = job.index
	local leaf = play.pieces[index]
	local box = leaf.box or IDENTITY
	local stood = play.crackFrame[index]
	local lying = nil
	local lyingOn = UP
	local flying = nil
	local velocity, spin = nil, nil
	if play.state[index] == LANDED then
		lying = play.lastFrame[index]
		lyingOn = play.path[index].restNormal or UP
	elseif play.state[index] == FLYING then
		local elapsed = play.clock - play.pathStart[index]
		flying = Trajectory.evaluate(play.path[index], elapsed, play.gravity[index])
		velocity, spin = Trajectory.velocity(play.path[index], elapsed, play.gravity[index])
	end
	local siblings = leaf.siblings
	if siblings then
		local place = table.find(siblings, index)
		if place then
			table.remove(siblings, place)
		end
	else
		siblings = {}
	end
	-- A ground's patch stands however it is cut; a part with a slot while it is in one piece.
	local sides = 0
	for _, shard in ipairs(shards) do
		if not shard.bit then
			sides += 1
		end
	end
	local standsOn = leaf.fixed == true and (leaf.cut ~= nil or sides <= 1)
	-- Where the leaf's part, or its ground's patch, stands, and how large that is.
	local space = leaf.rest * box:Inverse()
	local wholeSize = leaf.part.Size
	if leaf.cut then
		wholeSize = leaf.cut.size
	end
	-- One cut, one table: Reactor/Slash lets the sides of each piece go by it.
	local blade = plan.blade
	local slash = { origin = blade.origin, normal = blade.normal, heading = blade.heading, kerf = blade.kerf, by = plan.record }
	local shown = nil
	for _, shard in ipairs(shards) do
		local rest = leaf.rest * box:ToObjectSpace(shard.box)
		local piece = Pieces.ofShard(leaf.part, rest, shard)
		piece.siblings = siblings
		piece.slash = slash
		piece.side = shard.side
		piece.bit = shard.bit
		piece.baked = shard.baked
		-- A part that is parted stands no longer: its sides are ordinary pieces, and the
		-- hidden part itself leaves the play's rays when one of them wakes (Reactor/Entries).
		if standsOn then
			piece.partStands = leaf.partStands
			piece.fixed = not shard.bit or nil
		end
		-- A patch's pieces stay its patch's: Reactor/Display lays the ground's Texture by it.
		piece.cut = leaf.cut
		if leaf.cut and piece.fixed and Pieces.reachesFace(shard.box, piece.halfExt, leaf.cut) then
			piece.atFace = true
		end
		if standsOn and shard.bit then
			piece.under = Pieces.underTop(space, wholeSize, piece)
		end
		table.insert(play.pieces, piece)
		local child = #play.pieces
		table.insert(siblings, child)
		table.insert(taken, child)
		shown = shown or child
		play.state[child] = RESTING
		local now = nil
		if lying then
			now = lying * leaf.rest:ToObjectSpace(rest)
			play.state[child] = LANDED
			play.path[child] = Trajectory.lying(now, lyingOn)
			play.pathStart[child] = play.clock
			play.pathBuilt[child] = true
			play.lastFrame[child] = now
			play.landedAfter[child] = 0
			play:_rolled(child)
			play.awake += 1
		elseif flying then
			now = flying * leaf.rest:ToObjectSpace(rest)
			play:_launch(child, now, velocity, spin)
			play.awake += 1
		elseif stood and not (standsOn and shard.bit) then
			-- Debris of something fixed keeps no pose of its own: it starts on top (Play:_surfaced).
			now = stood * leaf.rest:ToObjectSpace(rest)
			play.crackFrame[child] = now
		end
		if now then
			table.insert(movedIndices, child)
			table.insert(movedFrames, now)
		end
	end
	leaf.retired = true
	play.state[index] = GONE
	play.cracked[index] = nil
	play.crackFrame[index] = nil
	play.display.drop(index)
	if lying or flying then
		play.awake -= 1
	elseif not stood then
		-- The part is hidden for as long as its pieces stand in for it: that counts once.
		play.hidden += 1
	end
	-- Waking one piece shows every piece of its part that has no stand-in yet (Reactor/Display).
	if shown then
		play.display.wake(shown)
	end
end

function Recarve.apply(play, plan, results)
	local taken = {}
	local movedIndices = {}
	local movedFrames = {}
	for position, job in ipairs(plan.jobs) do
		local shards = results[position]
		if shards and #shards >= 1 and carvable(play, job.index, plan.record) then
			replace(play, plan, job, shards, taken, movedIndices, movedFrames)
		else
			discard(shards or nil)
		end
	end
	if #movedIndices > 0 then
		play.display.move(movedIndices, movedFrames, #movedIndices)
	end
	-- Reactor/Support's graph names pieces by their place in the list, which has grown.
	play.support = nil
	return taken
end

local function takeNext(entry, isCurrent, revive)
	local request = entry.carves[1]
	if not request then
		return
	end
	local play = entry.play
	local record = request.record

	-- The Force left the play alone while its cut was made (Play.recracking): it kicks now,
	-- and Reactor/Slash lets go of the sides it finds for this Force.
	local function finish(indices)
		table.remove(entry.carves, 1)
		play.recracking[record] = nil
		if play.slashed then
			play.slashed[record] = nil
		end
		play:kickAgain(record, request.kicked, indices or {})
		revive()
		takeNext(entry, isCurrent, revive)
	end

	local blade = Blade.of(record.field, record.cut)
	if play.phase ~= "live" or not blade then
		finish(nil)
		return
	end
	local pieceCount = 0
	if entry.breaks then
		pieceCount = entry.pieceCount
	end
	local plan = Recarve.plan(play, blade, record, pieceCount)
	if #plan.jobs == 0 then
		finish(nil)
		return
	end
	Shards.recut(plan.jobs, function(results)
		if not isCurrent() or play.phase ~= "live" then
			for _, shards in ipairs(results) do
				discard(shards or nil)
			end
			if isCurrent() then
				finish(nil)
			else
				table.clear(entry.carves)
			end
			return
		end
		finish(Recarve.apply(play, plan, results))
	end)
end

function Recarve.request(entry, record, kicked, isCurrent, revive)
	if not kicked or not record.cut then
		return
	end
	if not entry.carved then
		entry.carved = setmetatable({}, { __mode = "k" })
		entry.carves = {}
	end
	if entry.carved[record] then
		return
	end
	entry.carved[record] = true
	table.insert(entry.carves, { record = record, kicked = kicked })
	entry.play.recracking[record] = "all"
	if #entry.carves == 1 then
		takeNext(entry, isCurrent, revive)
	end
end

return Recarve

--[[
	Recrack  -  the later cracks of one Reactor's play, taken one after another.

	Reactor/init asks for one each time an Impulse reaches a Reactor that is out of place
	already (Recrack.request). Reactor/Recut plans it, Reactor/Shards cuts the pieces, which
	takes a few frames, Recut puts them into the play, and the Force that asked is then given
	to the new pieces late (Play:kickAgain), as a Reactor's first cut answers its Force late.
	A second request waits for the first: it is planned on the pieces the first one left.

	One Force cracks one place once: asked again where it last cracked, it is given nothing
	(Reactor/Entries asks for every Force a Reactor is told of, and is told again of one that
	has moved). Another Force at that place cracks the ground again: its rings are laid from
	other numbers, so the pieces that stand there are cut finer and moved on.

	Recrack.request(entry, record, kicked, isCurrent, revive)
	    entry: Reactor/init's, with play, pieceCount (the Reactor's Pieces) and cracks (the
	    requests waiting, oldest first); a wound of Reactor/Wounds has that shape. Recrack keeps
	    two fields of its own on it: places (record -> where it last cracked) and taken (the
	    cracks planned so far). kicked: the record's own list of the pieces it has
	    kicked in this play (Play.kicks[record], or what Play:strike returned for an Impulse that
	    is over); nil asks for nothing. isCurrent() -> whether the entry is still its Reactor's:
	    a Reactor put back while a cut runs gets nothing. revive(): the play has work again.
	Recrack.opened(entry, records, hit)
	    The entry's first cut was made around `hit`: the first Impulse of `records` that stands
	    there has cracked that place, and asks for nothing more at it.
]]

local Recut = require(script.Parent.Recut)
local Shards = require(script.Parent.Shards)
local Sites = require(script.Parent.Sites)

-- A Force within this many studs of where it last cracked is at that place still.
local SAME_PLACE = 1
-- Keeps the rings of one crack apart from those of the crack before it at the same place.
local SEED_STEP = 104729

local Recrack = {}

-- record -> where it last cracked this entry's ground; a record that is over is forgotten.
local function placesOf(entry)
	if not entry.places then
		entry.places = setmetatable({}, { __mode = "k" })
	end
	return entry.places
end

local function takeNext(entry, isCurrent, revive)
	local request = entry.cracks[1]
	if not request then
		return
	end
	local play = entry.play
	local record = request.record

	-- The Force left the standing crust alone while its crack was cut (Play.recracking): it
	-- kicks now, the new pieces and those that joined (`indices`) included.
	local function finish(indices)
		table.remove(entry.cracks, 1)
		play.recracking[record] = nil
		play:kickAgain(record, request.kicked, indices or {})
		revive()
		takeNext(entry, isCurrent, revive)
	end

	if play.phase ~= "live" then
		finish(nil)
		return
	end
	local hit = record.field.origin.Position
	-- A Force may name the pieces of its own crack (record.pieces, Force/Registry).
	entry.taken = (entry.taken or 0) + 1
	local seed = Sites.seedAt(hit) + entry.taken * SEED_STEP
	local plan = Recut.plan(play, hit, record.field.range, record.pieces or entry.pieceCount, seed, record.field)
	if not plan then
		finish(nil)
		return
	end
	-- The strikes are this Force's: Reactor/Crack tells by that which pieces its split reaches.
	for _, strike in ipairs(plan.strikes) do
		strike.by = record
	end
	if #plan.jobs == 0 then
		finish(Recut.apply(play, plan, {}))
		return
	end
	Shards.recut(plan.jobs, function(results)
		if not isCurrent() then
			table.clear(entry.cracks)
			return
		end
		if play.phase ~= "live" then
			finish(nil)
			return
		end
		finish(Recut.apply(play, plan, results))
	end)
end

function Recrack.request(entry, record, kicked, isCurrent, revive)
	if not kicked then
		return
	end
	local places = placesOf(entry)
	local hit = record.field.origin.Position
	local last = places[record]
	if last and (last - hit).Magnitude < SAME_PLACE then
		return
	end
	places[record] = hit
	table.insert(entry.cracks, { record = record, kicked = kicked })
	entry.play.recracking[record] = true
	if #entry.cracks == 1 then
		takeNext(entry, isCurrent, revive)
	end
end

function Recrack.opened(entry, records, hit)
	for _, record in ipairs(records) do
		local stands = record.field.origin.Position
		if record.actsAs == "Impulse" and (stands - hit).Magnitude < SAME_PLACE then
			placesOf(entry)[record] = stands
			return
		end
	end
end

return Recrack

--[[
	Recut  -  a later crack in ground that is cracked already (Shard Pattern "Cracks"). Part of
	Reactor/Play, split out for size: the functions that take a play read and write its own
	tables. Maths on Vector3 and CFrame values; the engine's cut itself is Reactor/Shards.recut.

	A part keeps its first cut for as long as its play lasts. A later Impulse on the same face
	gets rings of its own (Reactor/Sites.cracks around its own hit), at the place of an earlier
	hit as anywhere else: that place is then cracked finer and deeper. Every crust piece that
	still stands and that two or more of those points fall in is cut again around them: it
	leaves the play, its pieces take its place and carry a strike of their own, so the crater,
	the rim and the hairlines are measured from the new hit. A standing piece within the new
	reach that is not cut joins the new crack as it is. Pieces already thrown are left alone,
	and so is the base.

	Cracks pile up: a piece keeps what earlier cracks did to it, and the new crack moves it on
	from where it stands (Reactor/Crack.pose), so the new crater, rim and hairlines all show.

	A crack is never refused for want of room in the play's Max Pieces: its pieces are then cut
	around fewer points, the ones nearest the hit first, and a piece with no room at all joins
	the crack whole. A piece wider than the new crack's crater (Reactor/Crack.outsizes) has
	more room: whole it could not sink into that crater, and the crack would not show there,
	so it is still cut until the play holds PLATE_ROOM times its Max Pieces
	(play.settings.MostPieces when whoever owns the play counts over several plays, as
	Reactor/Wounds does). Past that it joins whole too, and is moved by a hair.

	Which piece a point falls in is the engine's own rule: the nearest point of a cut owns the
	space. A piece of a part's first cut carries that cut's points (sites) and its own place
	among them (siteIndex). A piece that was cut again carries the points of that cut
	(cutPoints) and the pieces it gave, by their place among those points (children).

	Recut.plan(play, hit, reach, count, seed, field) -> plan or nil
	    hit: where the Force is, in the world. reach: its Range. count: the points a part is
	    cut around (the Reactor's Pieces). seed: the rings' numbers; Reactor/Recrack gives
	    every crack its own, or a second hit at one place would lay the first one's points
	    again and cut nothing. field: the Force's (Force/Fields); a Linear one that lies along
	    the struck face splits the ground along its path (Reactor/Fissure), drawn from the
	    place alone so it is one path across every ground and wound it crosses
	    (Reactor/Footprint draws the same). nil when nothing standing is within the crack.
	    plan.jobs: { { index, template, points, strike, within, always }, ... }: each piece to
	    cut, the fragment it is drawn from, and the points in the part's own space. within: the
	    piece lies inside the new reach, so it joins the new crack whole if the engine refuses
	    the cut. always: the piece is wider than the crater, and has the larger room.
	Recut.PLATE_ROOM: how many times Max Pieces a play may hold through the cutting of such
	    pieces.
	    plan.joins: { { index, strike }, ... }: the pieces that join the new crack uncut. A
	    joined piece is marked piece.joined (Reactor/Crack reads it).
	    plan.strikes: every strike the plan made, one a ground: the caller marks whose they are.
	Recut.apply(play, plan, results) -> indices
	    results[position]: the shards the engine gave for plan.jobs[position] (Reactor/Shards),
	    or false. Returns every piece the new crack made or took over: the Force that made it
	    has passed them by, and Play:kickAgain gives them its kick.
]]

local Sites = require(script.Parent.Sites)
local Pieces = require(script.Parent.Pieces)
local Fissure = require(script.Parent.Fissure)
local Crack = require(script.Parent.Crack)

local RESTING = 0
local GONE = 3

-- Two unit normals with at least this dot product face the same way.
local SAME_FACE = 0.99
-- A piece whose longest edge is under this many studs is not cut again.
local LEAST_RECUT = 1.5

local Recut = {}

Recut.PLATE_ROOM = 1.5

-- Where a piece's part stands for the play: where it is, or where the Reactor was stood up.
local function partFrame(piece)
	return piece.rest * piece.box:Inverse()
end

local function stands(play, index)
	local piece = play.pieces[index]
	return play.state[index] == RESTING and play.pendingPush[index] == nil and not piece.retired and not piece.fixed
end

-- The place in `points` of the one nearest to `point`.
local function nearest(points, point)
	local best = nil
	local least = math.huge
	for index, candidate in ipairs(points) do
		local distance = (candidate - point).Magnitude
		if distance < least then
			least = distance
			best = index
		end
	end
	return best
end

-- The piece of a part's crust a point of the part's space falls in today, or nil where the
-- first cut gave no piece. Walks from the first cut down through every later one.
local function ownerOf(play, ground, point)
	local index = ground.pieceOf[nearest(ground.sites, point)]
	while index do
		local piece = play.pieces[index]
		if not piece.retired then
			return index
		end
		index = piece.children[nearest(piece.cutPoints, point)]
	end
	return nil
end

-- Every cracked ground of the play: its frame, its size, its first cut and its strikes. A
-- ground is a part, or one patch of a part (piece.cut, Reactor/Pieces.ofSet): the space one
-- first cut was made in.
local function grounds(play)
	local bySpace = {}
	local ordered = {}
	local live = 0
	for index, piece in ipairs(play.pieces) do
		if not piece.retired then
			live += 1
		end
		if piece.box and piece.siteIndex and not piece.fixed then
			local space = piece.cut or piece.part
			local ground = bySpace[space]
			if not ground then
				local size = piece.part.Size
				if piece.cut then
					size = piece.cut.size
				end
				ground = { size = size, face = piece.cut and piece.cut.face, frame = partFrame(piece), pieceOf = {}, strikes = {}, pieces = {} }
				bySpace[space] = ground
				table.insert(ordered, ground)
			end
			table.insert(ground.pieces, index)
			if piece.sites then
				ground.sites = piece.sites
				ground.pieceOf[piece.siteIndex] = index
			end
			if piece.strike and not table.find(ground.strikes, piece.strike) then
				table.insert(ground.strikes, piece.strike)
			end
		end
	end
	return ordered, live
end

-- Whether a crack comes near enough to a part to cut any of it: a round one by where its Force
-- is, a split by its path.
local function comesNear(size, hitInPart, reach, line)
	if not line then
		return (hitInPart - Sites.hitIn(size, hitInPart)).Magnitude <= reach * Sites.RUN_ON
	end
	for _, point in ipairs(line.path.points) do
		if (point - Sites.hitIn(size, point)).Magnitude <= line.reach * Sites.RUN_ON then
			return true
		end
	end
	return false
end

-- The new crack of one part: its jobs and joins are added to the plan. crack = { hit, reach,
-- count, seed, field } (Recut.plan's own arguments), position: the part's place among the
-- play's grounds.
local function planGround(play, ground, crack, position, plan)
	if not ground.sites or #ground.strikes == 0 then
		return
	end
	local frame = ground.frame
	local size = ground.size
	local hit, reach = crack.hit, crack.reach
	local hitInPart = frame:PointToObjectSpace(hit)
	local points = Sites.count(size, crack.count)
	local first = ground.strikes[1]
	local normal = frame:VectorToObjectSpace(first.normal)
	local line = nil
	if crack.field then
		line = Fissure.of(crack.field, frame, frame:PointToObjectSpace(first.origin), normal, Sites.sequence(Sites.seedAt(hit)))
	end
	if points < 2 or not comesNear(size, hitInPart, reach, line) then
		return
	end
	if line then
		-- One layout for the whole split: every ground of the play keeps its part of it.
		line.seed = crack.seed
	end
	-- The crust keeps the thickness of the part's first cut: the new points are laid in it.
	local random = Sites.sequence(crack.seed + position * 7919)
	local offsets, cut = Sites.cracks(size, points, hitInPart, reach, random, { face = ground.face, crust = first.crust, line = line })
	if cut.normal:Dot(normal) < SAME_FACE then
		return
	end
	local origin = frame:PointToWorldSpace(cut.origin)
	local strike = { origin = origin, normal = first.normal, reach = cut.reach, crust = first.crust }
	if cut.path then
		strike.path = Fissure.moved(cut.path, frame, false)
	end
	table.insert(plan.strikes, strike)

	local byPiece = {}
	for _, point in ipairs(offsets) do
		local owner = ownerOf(play, ground, point)
		if owner and stands(play, owner) then
			local list = byPiece[owner]
			if not list then
				list = {}
				byPiece[owner] = list
			end
			table.insert(list, point)
		end
	end

	for _, index in ipairs(ground.pieces) do
		if stands(play, index) then
			local piece = play.pieces[index]
			local within = Crack.shareAt(strike, piece.rest.Position) <= 1
			local list = byPiece[index]
			if list and #list >= 2 and piece.reach >= LEAST_RECUT then
				table.insert(plan.jobs, { index = index, template = piece.shard, layered = piece.layered, points = list, strike = strike, within = within, always = Crack.outsizes(piece, strike) })
			elseif within then
				table.insert(plan.joins, { index = index, strike = strike })
			end
		end
	end
end

-- Holds a plan to the room the budget has left: `room` pieces more for a piece that fits the
-- crater, `plateRoom` for one wider than it. Reactor/Sites.cracks lays its points from the
-- hit outward, so the ones dropped are the farthest.
local function fit(plan, room, plateRoom)
	local jobs = {}
	for _, job in ipairs(plan.jobs) do
		local points = job.points
		local allowed = room
		if job.always then
			allowed = plateRoom
		end
		for position = #points, math.max(allowed + 2, 1), -1 do
			points[position] = nil
		end
		if #points >= 2 then
			room -= #points - 1
			plateRoom -= #points - 1
			table.insert(jobs, job)
		elseif job.within then
			table.insert(plan.joins, { index = job.index, strike = job.strike })
		end
	end
	plan.jobs = jobs
end

function Recut.plan(play, hit, reach, count, seed, field)
	local ordered, live = grounds(play)
	local plan = { jobs = {}, joins = {}, strikes = {} }
	local crack = { hit = hit, reach = reach, count = count, seed = seed, field = field }
	for position, ground in ipairs(ordered) do
		planGround(play, ground, crack, position, plan)
	end
	if #plan.jobs == 0 and #plan.joins == 0 then
		return nil
	end
	local settings = play.settings
	local most = settings.MostPieces or settings.MaxPieces * Recut.PLATE_ROOM
	fit(plan, settings.MaxPieces - live, most - live)
	return plan
end

-- Takes one cut piece out of the play and puts its pieces in. Mutates the play's own tables.
-- A piece that was stood out of place hands that place on: its pieces stand where it stood
-- until the new crack moves them. The new pieces are added to `taken`, and those that stand
-- out of place to the two move lists.
local function replace(play, job, shards, taken, movedIndices, movedFrames)
	local leaf = play.pieces[job.index]
	local siblings = leaf.siblings
	local place = table.find(siblings, job.index)
	if place then
		table.remove(siblings, place)
	end
	local stood = play.crackFrame[job.index]
	local children = {}
	local shown = nil
	for _, shard in ipairs(shards) do
		local rest = leaf.rest * leaf.box:ToObjectSpace(shard.box)
		local piece = Pieces.ofShard(leaf.part, rest, shard, leaf.looks)
		piece.siblings = siblings
		piece.strike = job.strike
		-- A fragment of a fragment whose colours are in its geometry has them there too.
		piece.baked = leaf.baked
		piece.cut = leaf.cut
		if leaf.cut and Pieces.touchesSide(shard.box, piece.halfExt, leaf.cut) then
			piece.atEdge = true
		end
		if leaf.cut and Pieces.reachesFace(shard.box, piece.halfExt, leaf.cut) then
			piece.atFace = true
		end
		table.insert(play.pieces, piece)
		local index = #play.pieces
		play.state[index] = RESTING
		table.insert(siblings, index)
		table.insert(taken, index)
		if shard.siteIndex then
			children[shard.siteIndex] = index
		end
		shown = shown or index
		if stood then
			local frame = stood * leaf.rest:ToObjectSpace(rest)
			play.crackFrame[index] = frame
			table.insert(movedIndices, index)
			table.insert(movedFrames, frame)
		end
	end
	leaf.retired = true
	leaf.children = children
	leaf.cutPoints = job.points
	play.state[job.index] = GONE
	play.cracked[job.index] = nil
	play.crackFrame[job.index] = nil
	play.display.drop(job.index)
	-- The part is hidden for as long as its cut pieces stand in for it: that counts once.
	if not stood then
		play.hidden += 1
	end
	-- Waking one piece shows every piece of its part that has no stand-in yet (Reactor/Display).
	play.display.wake(shown)
end

function Recut.apply(play, plan, results)
	local taken = {}
	local movedIndices = {}
	local movedFrames = {}
	local function join(index, strike)
		if not stands(play, index) then
			return
		end
		local piece = play.pieces[index]
		piece.strike = strike
		piece.joined = true
		play.cracked[index] = nil
		table.insert(taken, index)
	end
	for position, job in ipairs(plan.jobs) do
		local shards = results[position]
		if shards and #shards >= 2 and stands(play, job.index) then
			replace(play, job, shards, taken, movedIndices, movedFrames)
		elseif job.within then
			join(job.index, job.strike)
		end
	end
	for _, joined in ipairs(plan.joins) do
		join(joined.index, joined.strike)
	end
	if #movedIndices > 0 then
		play.display.move(movedIndices, movedFrames, #movedIndices)
	end
	-- Reactor/Support's graph names pieces by their place in the list, which has grown.
	play.support = nil
	return taken
end

return Recut

--[[
	Refusals  -  what the engine has said, this session, of the meshes it was asked to cut.

	A mesh that is not a closed solid is refused by every call of the engine's solid modelling
	(Fragment, Subtract, Intersect, Union: "Non-manifold mesh part"), whatever the part's size
	and the points. That refusal takes about half a second whenever the engine was not asked
	about the mesh in the two seconds before, and a millisecond otherwise (measured in Studio,
	2026-10-13). So a refusal is kept by mesh for the session, and a mesh is asked about ahead
	of the Force that would cut it (Refusals.judge): a part of a refused mesh moves whole at
	once, with no wait for the engine.
	A mesh is named by its MeshId or, for a mesh part made of an EditableMesh, by that mesh,
	which its copies share (measured). A plugin cannot read a mesh it does not own, so a mesh
	cannot be closed here either.

	Refusals.refused(part) -> boolean   a mesh part whose mesh the engine refused as not solid
	Refusals.notSolid(reason) -> boolean   whether an engine's reason is that refusal
	Refusals.cut(part)                  the engine cut a part: its mesh is one it cuts
	Refusals.refuse(part, reason)       a cut the engine refused, with its reason: kept when
	                                    the mesh itself is the reason, and told (below)
	Refusals.explain(part)              tells why a part that was to be cut moves whole, when
	                                    its mesh was refused
	Refusals.judge(part, fragment, done)
	    Asks the engine, once a mesh a session, whether it cuts a mesh part at all: a cut in
	    two of a copy kept out of the world, by fragment(part, points) -> fragments | nil,
	    reason (Reactor/Shards'). Calls done() when the engine's word is in: at once for a
	    mesh already asked about and for a part that is no mesh part. Returns at once.

	Told: one line in the Output (Log.warn) for each mesh, or part without one, a session.
]]

local Log = require(script.Parent.Parent.Log)

-- Probes of a mesh running at once.
local JUDGES = 2
-- The engine's word for a mesh that is not a closed solid.
local NOT_SOLID = "manifold"

local Refusals = {}

-- mesh -> the engine's reason once it refused the mesh as not solid, true once it cut it, the
-- list of who waits while it is being asked. Weak keys: an EditableMesh goes with its last
-- part; a MeshId, a string, stays.
local verdicts = setmetatable({}, { __mode = "k" })
-- The meshes, and the parts that have no mesh, whose refusal has been told.
local told = setmetatable({}, { __mode = "k" })
-- The parts whose meshes wait to be asked about, and how many probes run.
local waiting = {}
local judges = 0

local function contentObject(part)
	return part.MeshContent.Object
end

-- What names a mesh part's mesh, or nil for any other part.
local function meshOf(part)
	if not part:IsA("MeshPart") then
		return nil
	end
	local id = part.MeshId
	if id ~= nil and id ~= "" then
		return id
	end
	local ok, object = pcall(contentObject, part)
	if ok then
		return object
	end
	return nil
end

local function notSolid(reason)
	return string.find(reason, NOT_SOLID, 1, true) ~= nil
end
Refusals.notSolid = notSolid

local function tell(part, reason)
	local key = meshOf(part) or part
	if told[key] then
		return
	end
	told[key] = true
	local hint = ""
	if notSolid(reason) then
		hint = " A mesh must be a closed solid to be cut."
	end
	Log.warn(string.format("[Part-Icles] Reactor: the engine will not cut %s (%s), so it moves whole.%s", part:GetFullName(), reason, hint))
end

-- Keeps the engine's word on a mesh and answers who waited for it. A refusal stays.
local function settle(mesh, verdict)
	local before = verdicts[mesh]
	if type(before) == "string" then
		return
	end
	verdicts[mesh] = verdict
	if type(before) == "table" then
		for _, done in ipairs(before) do
			done()
		end
	end
end

function Refusals.refused(part)
	local mesh = meshOf(part)
	return mesh ~= nil and type(verdicts[mesh]) == "string"
end

function Refusals.cut(part)
	local mesh = meshOf(part)
	if mesh then
		settle(mesh, true)
	end
end

function Refusals.refuse(part, reason)
	local mesh = meshOf(part)
	if mesh and notSolid(reason) then
		settle(mesh, reason)
	end
	tell(part, reason)
end

function Refusals.explain(part)
	local mesh = meshOf(part)
	local reason = mesh and verdicts[mesh]
	if type(reason) == "string" then
		tell(part, reason)
	end
end

-- Asks the engine about the meshes that wait, one after another. Yields.
local function judgeWaiting(fragment)
	while #waiting > 0 do
		local part = table.remove(waiting, 1)
		local mesh = meshOf(part)
		local copy = Instance.fromExisting(part)
		copy.Archivable = true
		copy.Anchored = true
		local frame = copy.CFrame
		local reach = copy.Size / 4
		local fragments, reason = fragment(copy, { frame:PointToWorldSpace(reach), frame:PointToWorldSpace(-reach) })
		copy:Destroy()
		for _, entry in ipairs(fragments or {}) do
			entry.Instance:Destroy()
		end
		if mesh then
			if reason and notSolid(reason) then
				settle(mesh, reason)
			else
				settle(mesh, true)
			end
		end
	end
	judges -= 1
end

function Refusals.judge(part, fragment, done)
	local mesh = meshOf(part)
	local verdict = nil
	if mesh then
		verdict = verdicts[mesh]
	end
	if type(verdict) == "table" then
		if done then
			table.insert(verdict, done)
		end
		return
	end
	if not mesh or verdict ~= nil then
		if done then
			done()
		end
		return
	end
	verdicts[mesh] = { done }
	table.insert(waiting, part)
	if judges < JUDGES then
		judges += 1
		task.spawn(judgeWaiting, fragment)
	end
end

return Refusals

--[[
	Ribbon  -  the cutter of a jagged blade (Reactor/Blade.ribbon): a thin box swept through
	the ribbon's frames (GeometryService:SweepPartAsync joins every two of them up), which is
	the blade's own box bent along a zig-zag. It is made ONCE for a Force and a way of the
	blade and kept out of the world; Reactor/Carve sets a copy of it where the blade stands
	for each thing it cuts. So everything one Force cuts is cut along the very same surface,
	and a jagged cut costs one engine call more than a clean one, whatever it cuts.

	Measured in Studio (2026-10-11): a sweep takes about a millisecond a joint while the box
	is short, and six times that for a box 500 studs long. So the box is swept short and the
	ribbon stretched along its straight way afterwards (a MeshPart's Size scales its shape,
	and the ribbon stands square to the space it was made in). A subtraction with the cutter
	takes as long as one with a box.

	Ribbon.cutter(ribbon) -> the cutter (a MeshPart, never parented), or nil when the engine
	    refuses. Yields the first time a Force's ribbon is asked for. The cutter is made in
	    the blade's own space: at blade.frame * cutter.CFrame it lies where the blade stands.
]]

local GeometryService = game:GetService("GeometryService")
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")

local Ribbon = {}

-- A Force's cut table (Force/init: record.cut) -> { [lengthwise] = { cutter, making } }. The
-- keys are weak: a cutter goes with its Force.
local made = setmetatable({}, { __mode = "k" })

local function sweep(ribbon)
	local tool = Instance.new("Part")
	tool.Anchored = true
	tool.Size = ribbon.tool
	local ok, swept = pcall(function()
		return GeometryService:SweepPartAsync(tool, ribbon.frames)
	end)
	tool:Destroy()
	if not ok or typeof(swept) ~= "Instance" then
		return nil
	end
	local size = swept.Size
	local stretched = { X = size.X, Y = size.Y, Z = size.Z }
	stretched[ribbon.straight] = ribbon.length
	swept.Size = Vector3.new(stretched.X, stretched.Y, stretched.Z)
	return swept
end

function Ribbon.cutter(ribbon)
	local ofForce = made[ribbon.key]
	if not ofForce then
		ofForce = {}
		made[ribbon.key] = ofForce
	end
	local entry = ofForce[ribbon.lengthwise]
	if not entry then
		entry = { making = true }
		ofForce[ribbon.lengthwise] = entry
		entry.cutter = sweep(ribbon)
		entry.making = false
	end
	-- Asked for again while it is being made: every cut of the Force waits for the one cutter.
	while entry.making do
		RunService.Heartbeat:Wait()
	end
	return entry.cutter
end

return Ribbon

--[[
	Shards  -  what a part breaks into with Break = "Shards": real fragments, cut by the engine
	(GeometryService:FragmentAsync) around points of ours (Reactor/Sites) and kept OUT of the
	world as templates. Reactor/Display copies its stand-ins from them; the part itself is read
	and never changed. Break = "Blocks" comes here as well for a part that is not a plain box:
	cut around an even grid of points (Reactor/Dice.centres), its fragments are cubes.

	The cut yields (about 30 ms for 50 shards of a plain part, measured in Studio), and a play
	needs its pieces up front. So shards are cut ahead and kept per part under a key that names
	everything the cut depends on; Reactor/init asks for them and, when they are not there yet,
	has them cut and lets the Reactor answer its Force a few frames late.

	Shards.cuttable(part) -> boolean      a Part, wedge, MeshPart or union that draws its own
	                                      shape; a Part carrying a mesh, a truss and Terrain are
	                                      not, nor a mesh the engine has refused (below)
	Shards.refused(part), Shards.explain(part), Shards.judge(part, done)
