	    Reactor/Refusals' own, with this module's cut as the probe: whether a mesh part's mesh
	    was refused as not a closed solid, the line that says so, and the question asked ahead
	    (done() is called once the engine's word on the part's mesh is in).
	Shards.key(part, count, seed, hit, reach, grid) -> string
	Shards.get(part, key) -> shards | false | nil
	    shards: { { template, box, size, standOffset, fixed, siteIndex, baked }, ... }
	        template     the fragment, a MeshPart with no parent
	        box          the shard's own box as a frame in the PART's space; size its extents
	        standOffset  where the template sits in that box's frame: a stand-in at frame F of
	                     the piece has CFrame F * standOffset
	        fixed        true for the base under cracked ground: it never moves
	        siteIndex    the place, among the points of its cut, of the point it was cut around
	        baked        true when its colours are in its geometry: Reactor/Display then leaves
	                     its Color as it came (bakesColours, below)
	    shards.sites     the points of the cut, in the part's space
	    shards.strike    for cracked ground, Sites.cracks' strike, in the part's space
	    Cracked ground is cut twice: the part into its crust and its base (two points, a flat
	    face between), then the crust alone into its pieces. The base is one shard.
	    false: the engine refused the part, or gave fewer than two shards; it moves whole.
	    A refusal is told once a session for each mesh or part, with the engine's own reason,
	    and one of a mesh that is not a closed solid is kept for the session
	    (Reactor/Refusals): no part of that mesh is cuttable from then on.
	    nil: not cut under that key yet.
	    A part carved by a blade (a job with bladeFrame) is Reactor/Carve's to cut: its set has
	    a slash, its shards a side or a bit mark, and it may be ONE shard, the part with a slot.
	Shards.prepare(jobs, done)
	    jobs: { { part, key, count, seed, hit, reach, grid, face, line, loose }, ... }. Cuts them, a few at a time,
	    and calls done() once all are kept. Returns at once. No hit: Sites.even. A hit (a point of
	    the part's box): Sites.aroundHit. A hit and a reach: Sites.cracks, the hit as it is.
	    grid = true: Dice.centres, for blocks. face: the face Sites.cracks is to crack.
	    line: the split of a Linear Force (Reactor/Fissure.of, in the part's space, with its
	    seed), which Sites.cracks then lays its places along.
	    loose = true: the part is a template kept out of the world (Reactor/Patches), which
	    whoever asked must hold on to until done() has read its set.
	Shards.recut(jobs, done)
	    jobs: { { template, points }, ... } (Reactor/Recut's): cuts each template, a fragment of an
	    earlier cut, around its points, which are in the space of the part it came from. Calls
	    done(results) with the shards of each job, or false, in the jobs' order. Returns at once.
	    These are a play's own and are not kept. A job with a bladeFrame (Reactor/Recarve's) is
	    a piece cut again by a blade: Reactor/Carve's to cut.

	Kept sets are held by the part alone (weak keys): they go when the part does, and a part
	cut again under another key drops its old set. Nothing here is saved with the place: the
	engine does not keep fragments across sessions, so they are cut again in each.
]]

local GeometryService = game:GetService("GeometryService")
local Refusals = require(script.Parent.Refusals)
local Sites = require(script.Parent.Sites)
local Dice = require(script.Parent.Dice)
local Carve = require(script.Parent.Carve)
local LayerCuts = require(script.Parent.LayerCuts)

-- Cuts running at once.
local WORKERS = 4
-- A hit is the same hit within this many studs: the key rounds to it.
local HIT_STEP = 0.5

local Shards = {}

-- part -> { key = string, shards = table or false }
local kept = setmetatable({}, { __mode = "k" })

-- Whether the engine's fragments of a part come back with its colours in their geometry. Those
-- of a union that shows its own parts' colours do (UsePartColor off, as Studio's Union leaves
-- it): white MeshParts whose outer faces carry each part's colour and whose cut faces the
-- union's own. Given the union's Color as well they show it twice, too dark (measured in
-- Studio, 2026-10-13). Fragments of a mesh part, a plain part and a union that uses its part
-- colour come back in that one Color.
local function bakesColours(part)
	return part:IsA("PartOperation") and not part.UsePartColor
end

Shards.refused = Refusals.refused
Shards.explain = Refusals.explain

function Shards.cuttable(part)
	if part:IsA("MeshPart") then
		return not Refusals.refused(part)
	end
	if part:IsA("PartOperation") then
		return true
	end
	if part:IsA("Part") or part:IsA("WedgePart") or part:IsA("CornerWedgePart") then
		-- A Part that carries a mesh draws the mesh, which is not what the engine would cut.
		return part:FindFirstChildWhichIsA("DataModelMesh") == nil
	end
	return false
end

function Shards.key(part, count, seed, hit, reach, grid, line)
	local size = part.Size
	local shape = part.ClassName
	if part:IsA("MeshPart") then
		shape ..= part.MeshId
	elseif part:IsA("Part") then
		shape ..= part.Shape.Name
	elseif bakesColours(part) then
		-- A union cut while it showed its parts' colours is no cut for one that uses its own.
		shape ..= ":baked"
	end
	local where = "even"
	if hit then
		where = string.format("%d,%d,%d", math.round(hit.X / HIT_STEP), math.round(hit.Y / HIT_STEP), math.round(hit.Z / HIT_STEP))
	end
	if reach then
		where = string.format("cracks:%s:%d", where, math.round(reach / HIT_STEP))
	end
	if line then
		-- A split is its path's two ends, its reach and the numbers it wanders by.
		local points = line.path.points
		local first, last = points[1], points[#points]
		where = string.format("%s:split:%d,%d,%d:%d,%d,%d:%.2f:%d", where,
			math.round(first.X / HIT_STEP), math.round(first.Y / HIT_STEP), math.round(first.Z / HIT_STEP),
			math.round(last.X / HIT_STEP), math.round(last.Y / HIT_STEP), math.round(last.Z / HIT_STEP), line.reach, line.seed or 0)
	end
	if grid then
		where = "blocks"
	end
	return string.format("%s|%.3f,%.3f,%.3f|%d|%d|%s", shape, size.X, size.Y, size.Z, count, seed, where)
end

function Shards.get(part, key)
	local set = kept[part]
	if set and set.key == key then
		return set.shards
	end
	return nil
end

-- The engine's fragments of `part` around world points, or nil and the engine's reason.
-- Yields. A wedge is refused as it is and accepted as a union of itself alone.
local function fragment(part, points)
	local ok, result = pcall(function()
		return GeometryService:FragmentAsync(part, points)
	end)
	if ok and type(result) == "table" then
		return result
	end
	local reason = nil
	if not ok then
		reason = tostring(result)
	end
	local united, union = pcall(function()
		return GeometryService:UnionAsync(part, {})
	end)
	local solid = united and type(union) == "table" and union[1] or nil
	if not solid then
		return nil, reason
	end
	ok, result = pcall(function()
		return GeometryService:FragmentAsync(solid, points)
	end)
	solid:Destroy()
	if ok and type(result) == "table" then
		return result
	end
	return nil, reason
end

-- A fragment as a shard of the part whose frame is `frame`.
local function shardOf(template, frame, fixed, siteIndex)
	local extents = template.ExtentsCFrame
	return {
		template = template,
		box = frame:ToObjectSpace(extents),
		size = template.ExtentsSize,
		standOffset = extents:ToObjectSpace(template.CFrame),
		fixed = fixed,
		siteIndex = siteIndex,
	}
end

-- A copy of a part the engine takes as it is: Archivable, and out of the world.
local function solidCopy(part)
	local copy = Instance.fromExisting(part)
	copy.Archivable = true
	copy.Anchored = true
	return copy
end

-- What of the box of `template` lies inside `part`: the engine's intersection of a plain
-- white box of that frame and size with the part, which keeps the box's frame. into: what
-- takes the part's place to the template's space, when the template does not stand where it
-- is cut from (a patch's stands at the world's origin); nil for one that does. nil when they
-- share nothing or the engine refuses. Yields.
local function clip(template, part, into)
	local other = solidCopy(part)
	if into then
		other.CFrame = into * part.CFrame
	end
	-- White, as every source of a cut is: the faces the part gives carry its colour in their
	-- geometry, and a stand-in is given its part's colour on top.
	other.Color = Color3.new(1, 1, 1)
	if other:IsA("PartOperation") then
		other.UsePartColor = true
	end
	local box = Instance.new("Part")
	box.Anchored = true
	box.Size = template.Size
	box.CFrame = template.CFrame
	box.Color = Color3.new(1, 1, 1)
	local ok, result = pcall(function()
		return GeometryService:IntersectAsync(box, { other })
	end)
	box:Destroy()
	other:Destroy()
	if not ok or type(result) ~= "table" or not result[1] then
		return nil
	end
	for position = 2, #result do
		result[position]:Destroy()
	end
	return result[1]
end

LayerCuts.use(fragment, shardOf, clip)

-- The engine's first intersection with a part's shape takes most of a second, every later
-- one a frame (measured in Studio, 2026-10-13: 667 ms, then 17). A skin is asked about once,
-- ahead of its first crack (Reactor/Entries.prepare). Returns at once.
local warmed = setmetatable({}, { __mode = "k" })
function Shards.warm(part)
	if warmed[part] then
		return
	end
	warmed[part] = true
	task.spawn(function()
		local probe = Instance.new("Part")
		probe.Size = Vector3.new(1, 1, 1)
		probe.CFrame = part.CFrame
		local made = clip(probe, part, nil)
		probe:Destroy()
		if made then
			made:Destroy()
		end
	end)
end

-- `part` with boxes taken out of it ({ { frame, size }, ... }): one new part that keeps the
-- part's frame and look, out of the world, or nil when nothing is left or the engine
-- refuses. Yields. Reactor/SkinDisplay draws what is intact of a skin with it.
function Shards.without(part, boxes)
	local source = solidCopy(part)
	local cutters = table.create(#boxes)
	for position, box in ipairs(boxes) do
		local cutter = Instance.new("Part")
		cutter.Anchored = true
		cutter.Size = box.size
		cutter.CFrame = box.frame
		cutters[position] = cutter
	end
	local ok, result = pcall(function()
		return GeometryService:SubtractAsync(source, cutters, { SplitApart = false })
	end)
	source:Destroy()
	for _, cutter in ipairs(cutters) do
		cutter:Destroy()
	end
	if not ok or type(result) ~= "table" or not result[1] then
		return nil
	end
	for position = 2, #result do
		result[position]:Destroy()
	end
	return result[1]
end

-- What the engine is given to cut of a part. It refuses one that is not Archivable (measured
-- in Studio, 2026-10-13: at once, "CSG: Part is not archivable"), and every copy the runtime
-- emits is not; Reactor/HandOver makes Reactors of those. Such a part is cut as a copy of
-- itself that is Archivable and kept out of the world. The second value is true for a copy
-- made here, which whoever asked destroys.
local function archivable(part)
	if part.Archivable then
		return part, false
	end
	local copy = Instance.fromExisting(part)
	copy.Archivable = true
	return copy, true
end

-- Cuts one job and returns its shards, or false. Yields.
local function cut(job)
	local part = job.part
	if not part.Parent and not job.loose then
		return false
	end
	-- A patch of a stacked ground (Reactor/Layers): one that lies in a single layer is cut as
	-- any patch and its shards marked with that layer.
	local shares = job.layers
	local stacked = shares ~= nil and #shares > 1
	if job.bladeFrame then
		if stacked then
			return LayerCuts.carve(job, part.CFrame, Carve.cut)
		end
		-- Only a mesh's own refusal is kept and told; any other failed carve moves whole in silence.
		local carved, refusal = Carve.cut(job, fragment, shardOf)
		if refusal and Refusals.notSolid(refusal) and not job.loose then
			Refusals.refuse(part, refusal)
		end
		if carved and shares then
			LayerCuts.stamp(carved, shares[1])
		end
		return carved
	end
	local frame = part.CFrame
	local whole, madeHere = archivable(part)
	local random = Sites.sequence(job.seed)
	local offsets
	local strike, split = nil, nil
	if job.grid then
		offsets = Dice.centres(part.Size, job.count)
	elseif job.reach then
		-- A ground's patch (loose) is always cut: one left whole could never crack again.
		offsets, strike, split = Sites.cracks(part.Size, job.count, job.hit, job.reach, random, { face = job.face, fill = job.loose == true, line = job.line })
	elseif job.hit then
		offsets = Sites.aroundHit(part.Size, job.count, job.hit, random)
	else
		offsets = Sites.even(part.Size, job.count, random)
	end
	local points = table.create(#offsets)
	for index, offset in ipairs(offsets) do
		points[index] = frame:PointToWorldSpace(offset)
	end

	if stacked then
		local layered = LayerCuts.cut(job, whole, frame, points, split)
		if madeHere then
			whole:Destroy()
		end
		if layered then
			layered.sites = offsets
			layered.strike = strike
		end
		return layered
	end

	-- Cracked ground: the crust is cut off its base first, and only the crust into pieces.
	-- A fragment's Index is the place of its point among those the cut was given.
	local source = whole
	local crust, base = nil, nil
	if split then
		local halves = fragment(whole, { frame:PointToWorldSpace(split.inCrust), frame:PointToWorldSpace(split.inBase) })
		if halves and #halves == 2 then
			for _, entry in ipairs(halves) do
				if entry.Index == 1 then
					crust = entry.Instance
				else
					base = entry.Instance
				end
			end
		end
		if crust and base then
			source = crust
		else
			base = nil
		end
	end

	local fragments, reason = fragment(source, points)
	if crust then
		crust:Destroy()
	end
	if madeHere then
		whole:Destroy()
	end
	if not fragments or #fragments < 2 then
		if base then
			base:Destroy()
		end
		if reason and not job.loose then
			Refusals.refuse(part, reason)
		end
		return false
	end
	Refusals.cut(part)
	local shards = table.create(#fragments + 1)
	for _, entry in ipairs(fragments) do
		table.insert(shards, shardOf(entry.Instance, frame, false, entry.Index))
	end
	if base then
		table.insert(shards, shardOf(base, frame, true, nil))
	end
	if bakesColours(part) then
		for _, shard in ipairs(shards) do
			shard.baked = true
		end
	end
	if shares then
		LayerCuts.stamp(shards, shares[1])
	end
	shards.sites = offsets
	shards.strike = strike
	return shards
end

-- Cuts one fragment of an earlier cut again and returns its shards, or false. Yields. A
-- fragment keeps the frame of the part it was cut from, which is the frame its points are in.
local function cutAgain(job)
	if job.bladeFrame then
		local carved, refusal = Carve.cut(job, fragment, shardOf)
		-- A whole part cut again is cut as itself: its mesh may be what the engine refuses.
		if refusal and Refusals.notSolid(refusal) and job.part and not job.template and not job.blockSize then
			Refusals.refuse(job.part, refusal)
		end
		return carved
	end
	if job.layered then
		return LayerCuts.cutAgain(job)
	end
	local template = job.template
	local frame = template.CFrame
	local points = table.create(#job.points)
	for index, offset in ipairs(job.points) do
		points[index] = frame:PointToWorldSpace(offset)
	end
	local fragments = fragment(template, points)
	if not fragments or #fragments < 2 then
		return false
	end
	local shards = table.create(#fragments)
	for _, entry in ipairs(fragments) do
		table.insert(shards, shardOf(entry.Instance, frame, false, entry.Index))
	end
	return shards
end

function Shards.judge(part, done)
	Refusals.judge(part, fragment, done)
end

function Shards.prepare(jobs, done)
	local total = #jobs
	if total == 0 then
		done()
		return
	end
	local taken = 0
	local finished = 0
	local function work()
		while taken < total do
			taken += 1
			local job = jobs[taken]
			local ok, shards = pcall(cut, job)
			kept[job.part] = { key = job.key, shards = ok and shards or false }
			finished += 1
		end
		if finished == total and done then
			local callback = done
			done = nil
			callback()
		end
	end
	for _ = 1, math.min(WORKERS, total) do
		task.spawn(work)
	end
end

function Shards.recut(jobs, done)
	local total = #jobs
	local results = table.create(total, false)
	if total == 0 then
		done(results)
		return
	end
	local taken = 0
	local finished = 0
	local function work()
		while taken < total do
			taken += 1
			local position = taken
			local ok, shards = pcall(cutAgain, jobs[position])
			results[position] = ok and shards or false
			finished += 1
		end
		if finished == total and done then
			local callback = done
			done = nil
			callback(results)
		end
	end
	for _ = 1, math.min(WORKERS, total) do
		task.spawn(work)
	end
end

return Shards

--[[
	Sites  -  the points a part is broken around with Break = "Shards". The engine cuts one shard
	per point: the part of the solid that is nearer to that point than to any other (a Voronoi
	cell). So the number of points is the number of shards, and where the points are thick the
	shards are small. Numbers only, no instances.

	Sites.count(size, pieces) -> how many points a part of `size` gets
	    `pieces` held to Sites.MAX, and to fewer for a part too small to give that many shards
	    of LEAST_VOLUME each. Under 2 the part is not cut.
	Sites.even(size, count, random) -> { Vector3 }
	    anywhere in the part's box: shards of about one size.
	Sites.aroundHit(size, count, hit, random) -> { Vector3 }
	    NEAR_SHARE of the points near `hit`, the rest anywhere: small shards where the part was
	    struck, large ones away from it.
	Sites.hitIn(size, point) -> the point of the part's box nearest to `point`
	Sites.face(size, point) -> axis ("X" | "Y" | "Z"), side (1 | -1)
	    the face of the part's box that lies nearest to `point`: the one a Force there strikes.
	    Of faces about as near, the largest: a slab struck beside its edge cracks in its top.
	Sites.faceAxes(axis) -> the two axes a face normal to `axis` lies in: its u and its v
	Sites.underFace(size, axis, side, u, v, depth) -> the point of the part at (u, v) of a face,
	    `depth` under it
	Sites.alongFace(axis, u, v, normal) -> the vector with `u` and `v` along the face's two axes
	    and `normal` along `axis`
	Sites.probes(size, axis, side, u, v, reach) -> { Vector3 }: places just under a face, at
	    (u, v) and on three rings around it out to `reach`, to ask a Force's field at
	Sites.cracks(size, count, hit, reach, random, options) -> { Vector3 }, strike, split
	    cracked ground: the points of a crust under the struck face, in rings around the hit
	    (rubble at the hit, cracks running out from it that fork, long pieces past the reach).
	    `count` is how many places the rings lay. A crust of LEAST_LAYERED studs or more is cut
	    in two layers: every place gives two points, one high in the crust and one low, a little
	    apart to either side, so a piece's sides are stepped and not one upright wall. The
	    places are then held to half of Sites.MAX, and the points are about twice `count`.
	    strike = { origin, normal, reach, crust }: the hit laid onto the struck face, that face's
	    outward normal, how far the rings go (`reach`, drawn in when the face is smaller) and
	    how thick the crust is.
	    split = { inCrust, inBase }: two points, one over the other; cut around them alone, the
	    part falls into the crust and the base under it, with a flat face between. The other
	    points are then for the crust only. nil for a part too thin for both: it is cut straight
	    through, and its crust is all of it.
	    `hit` may lie outside the part: a part beside the one struck gets the outer rings.
	    options (all optional):
	      face = { axis, side } names the face to crack; without it, Sites.face(size, hit). A
	        patch of a ground (Reactor/Wounds) names its ground's face: a narrow patch of a
	        thick ground has a side larger than its top.
	      fill: the face is cut whatever the rings give it. A patch beside the hit that gets
	        fewer than two of their places has `count` of them, two at least, spread over it
	        (beside a split, whose count is not the patch's own, just two).
	        Reactor/Shards asks it for a ground's patches; Reactor/Recut never does, since a
	        later crack cuts only where its rings fall.
	      crust: the thickness to lay the points in, for a part that is cut already
	        (Reactor/Recut: a later crack keeps the first cut's crust).
	      line = { path, reach, seed }: a split along a Linear Force (Reactor/Fissure.of, in
	        the part's space). The places are laid along the path and not in rings, `reach` is
	        the line's own, the crust is as thick as for a round crack as wide as the path is
	        long, and the strike carries the path. `count` is then the places of the WHOLE
	        split, laid once, and the part keeps those that fall in it: a part the path only
	        crosses gets that stretch's places and no more. With a seed the places are drawn
	        from it, so every part one split crosses takes its places from one layout.
	Sites.LAYERS: the most points one place gives (2).
	Sites.RUN_ON: how many times the reach the outermost cracks run to; a part farther from
	    the hit than that gets none of them.
	Sites.sequence(seed) -> random: numbers from 0 to 1, the same for the same seed
	Sites.seedAt(point) -> a seed that is the same for the same place: a Force emitted again
	    where it was cuts ground that is whole as it did (a later crack of ground that is
	    cracked adds a step of its own, Reactor/Recrack)
	Points and `hit` are offsets in the part's own space; points keep a little inside the box.
	`random` gives 0 to 1; the same sequence gives the same points. A point that falls outside
	the solid itself (the corner of a ball's box) cuts no shard, so a round part gives a few
	fewer than asked.
]]

local Fissure = require(script.Parent.Fissure)

local Sites = {}

Sites.MAX = 240
Sites.LAYERS = 2
-- The average shard is never smaller than this, in cubic studs: a half-stud cube.
local LEAST_VOLUME = 0.125
-- Points stay within this share of the box, clear of its faces.
local INSET = 0.95
-- aroundHit: the share of the points gathered near the hit, how far from it they reach as a
-- share of the part's longest edge, and how strongly they crowd toward it (under 1 crowds).
local NEAR_SHARE = 0.7
local NEAR_REACH = 0.4
local CROWDING = 0.6

local AXES = { "X", "Y", "Z" }
local SIDES = { 1, -1 }
-- face: a face this much farther off than the nearest still counts as near as it.
local FACE_SLACK = 0.25
-- cracks: the share of the crust's points that is rubble right at the hit, and how far out it
-- lies (share of the reach).
local RUBBLE_SHARE = 0.1
local RUBBLE_REACH = 0.12
-- Bands crowd toward the hit: band i of n ends at (i / n) ^ BAND_CROWDING of the reach.
local BAND_CROWDING = 1.3
-- A crack forks where its piece would be this many times wider than deep.
local FORK_AT = 2.4
-- How unevenly the cracks leave the hit (share of their even spacing), and how far a piece's
-- point strays across its band (share of the band's depth).
local UNEVEN = 0.3
local ACROSS = 0.3
-- Past the reach the cracks run on as long pieces, to this many times the reach.
local RUN_ON = 1.9
Sites.RUN_ON = RUN_ON
local MOST_BANDS = 14
-- The crust is this share of the reach thick, never under LEAST_CRUST studs nor over
-- CRUST_SHARE of the part; a part that leaves no room for that has no base.
local CRUST_REACH_SHARE = 0.075
local LEAST_CRUST = 0.5
local CRUST_SHARE = 0.45
-- A crust this thick is cut in two layers; a thinner one would give flakes.
local LEAST_LAYERED = 1
-- How deep each layer's points lie, as shares of the crust.
local UPPER = 0.28
local LOWER = 0.72
-- How far the two points of one place stand to either side of it, as a share of the way to
-- the nearest other place.
local STAGGER = 0.3

function Sites.sequence(seed)
	local state = seed % 2147483647
	return function()
		state = (state * 48271 + 11) % 2147483647
		return state / 2147483647
	end
end

function Sites.seedAt(point)
	return math.floor(math.abs(point.X * 31.7 + point.Y * 57.3 + point.Z * 17.1) * 1000) % 2147483646 + 1
end

function Sites.count(size, pieces)
	local wanted = math.floor(math.min(pieces, Sites.MAX))
	local room = math.floor(size.X * size.Y * size.Z / LEAST_VOLUME)
	return math.max(math.min(wanted, room), 0)
end

local function anywhere(size, random)
	return Vector3.new((random() - 0.5) * size.X, (random() - 0.5) * size.Y, (random() - 0.5) * size.Z) * INSET
end

function Sites.even(size, count, random)
	local points = table.create(count)
	for index = 1, count do
		points[index] = anywhere(size, random)
	end
	return points
end

function Sites.hitIn(size, point)
	local half = size / 2
	return Vector3.new(math.clamp(point.X, -half.X, half.X), math.clamp(point.Y, -half.Y, half.Y), math.clamp(point.Z, -half.Z, half.Z))
end

function Sites.aroundHit(size, count, hit, random)
	local points = table.create(count)
	local reach = math.max(size.X, size.Y, size.Z) * NEAR_REACH
	local near = math.floor(count * NEAR_SHARE)
	for index = 1, count do
		if index > near then
			points[index] = anywhere(size, random)
		else
			local direction = Vector3.new(random() - 0.5, random() - 0.5, random() - 0.5)
			if direction.Magnitude < 1e-4 then
				direction = Vector3.new(0, 1, 0)
			end
			local offset = hit + direction.Unit * (reach * random() ^ CROWDING)
			points[index] = Sites.hitIn(size, offset) * INSET
		end
	end
	return points
end

-- How far `point` lies from the face of the box across `axis` on `side`, as a rectangle.
local function faceDistance(size, point, axis, side)
	local squared = (point[axis] - side * size[axis] / 2) ^ 2
	for _, other in ipairs(AXES) do
		if other ~= axis then
			local past = math.max(math.abs(point[other]) - size[other] / 2, 0)
			squared += past * past
		end
	end
	return math.sqrt(squared)
end

function Sites.face(size, point)
	local bestAxis, bestSide = "Y", 1
	local least, bestArea = math.huge, 0
	for _, axis in ipairs(AXES) do
		local area = size.X * size.Y * size.Z / size[axis]
		for _, side in ipairs(SIDES) do
			local distance = faceDistance(size, point, axis, side)
			local clearlyNearer = distance < least * (1 - FACE_SLACK)
			local asNearAndLarger = distance <= least * (1 + FACE_SLACK) and area > bestArea
			if clearlyNearer or asNearAndLarger then
				bestAxis, bestSide = axis, side
				least, bestArea = distance, area
			end
		end
	end
	return bestAxis, bestSide
end

-- The two axes a face normal to `axis` lies in.
local function faceAxes(axis)
	if axis == "X" then
		return "Y", "Z"
	elseif axis == "Y" then
		return "X", "Z"
	end
	return "X", "Y"
end

-- A point of the part from its place (u, v) in a face and its depth under that face.
local function underFace(size, axis, side, u, v, depth)
	local along = side * (size[axis] / 2 - depth)
	if axis == "X" then
		return Vector3.new(along, u, v)
	elseif axis == "Y" then
		return Vector3.new(u, along, v)
	end
	return Vector3.new(u, v, along)
end

-- The angle after `angle` in a ring of angles that goes once round.
local function nextIn(angles, index)
	local following = angles[index % #angles + 1]
	if following <= angles[index] then
		following += 2 * math.pi
	end
	return following
end

-- The ring's places (u, v) around (hitU, hitV), for `count` points. inside(u, v) keeps a place.
local function rings(count, hitU, hitV, reach, random, inside)
	local places = {}
	local function add(u, v)
		-- A place outside the part cuts nothing: it is left out, never pushed onto the edge.
		if inside(u, v) then
			table.insert(places, { u, v })
		end
	end

	local rubble = math.floor(count * RUBBLE_SHARE)
	for _ = 1, rubble do
		local angle = random() * 2 * math.pi
		local radius = reach * RUBBLE_REACH * math.sqrt(random())
		add(hitU + math.cos(angle) * radius, hitV + math.sin(angle) * radius)
	end

	-- More cracks leave the hit the more pieces there are to make.
	local cracksAtHit = math.clamp(math.round(math.sqrt(count) * 0.9), 6, 16) + math.floor(random() * 3)
	local angles = {}
	local turn = random() * 2 * math.pi
	for index = 1, cracksAtHit do
		angles[index] = turn + (index - 1 + (random() - 0.5) * 2 * UNEVEN) / cracksAtHit * 2 * math.pi
	end

	local function edges(band, bands)
		local inner = reach * (RUBBLE_REACH + (1 - RUBBLE_REACH) * ((band - 1) / bands) ^ BAND_CROWDING)
		local outer = reach * (RUBBLE_REACH + (1 - RUBBLE_REACH) * (band / bands) ^ BAND_CROWDING)
		return inner, outer
	end
	-- The points `bands` bands take, forks counted in, with the long pieces past the reach.
	local function cost(bands)
		local total = 0
		local across = cracksAtHit
		for band = 1, bands do
			local inner, outer = edges(band, bands)
			if math.pi * (inner + outer) / across > FORK_AT * (outer - inner) then
				across *= 2
			end
			total += across
		end
		return total + across
	end
	local bands = 1
	while bands < MOST_BANDS and cost(bands + 1) <= count - rubble do
		bands += 1
	end

	for band = 1, bands + 1 do
		local inner, outer = edges(math.min(band, bands), bands)
		if band > bands then
			inner = reach
			outer = reach * RUN_ON
		end
		local depth = outer - inner
		if band <= bands and math.pi * (inner + outer) / #angles > FORK_AT * depth then
			local forked = {}
			for index, angle in ipairs(angles) do
				table.insert(forked, angle)
				table.insert(forked, angle + (nextIn(angles, index) - angle) * (0.5 + (random() - 0.5) * 0.3))
			end
			angles = forked
		end
		for index, angle in ipairs(angles) do
			-- A piece's point sits midway between its two cracks.
			local along = (angle + nextIn(angles, index)) / 2
			local radius = (inner + outer) / 2 + (random() - 0.5) * 2 * ACROSS * depth
			add(hitU + math.cos(along) * radius, hitV + math.sin(along) * radius)
		end
	end
	return places
end

-- About `count` places (two or more asked) spread over a face of half-lengths halfU and halfV:
-- a grid of cells about as wide as they are long, each place off its cell's middle by up to
-- SPREAD_JITTER of the cell.
local SPREAD_JITTER = 0.25
local function spread(count, halfU, halfV, random)
	local columns = math.clamp(math.round(math.sqrt(count * halfU / halfV)), 1, count)
	local rows = math.max(math.round(count / columns), 1)
	local places = {}
	for row = 1, rows do
		for column = 1, columns do
			local u = (2 * (column - 0.5 + (random() - 0.5) * 2 * SPREAD_JITTER) / columns - 1) * halfU * INSET
			local v = (2 * (row - 0.5 + (random() - 0.5) * 2 * SPREAD_JITTER) / rows - 1) * halfV * INSET
			table.insert(places, { u, v })
		end
	end
	return places
end

-- The points of a crust for its places: one at the crust's middle for each, or, in a crust
-- thick enough, a high one and a low one staggered to either side. lay(u, v, depth) -> Vector3.
local function layered(places, crust, halfU, halfV, random, lay)
	local points = {}
	if crust < LEAST_LAYERED then
		for _, place in ipairs(places) do
			table.insert(points, lay(place[1], place[2], crust / 2))
		end
		return points
	end
	local limitU, limitV = halfU * INSET, halfV * INSET
	for index, place in ipairs(places) do
		local gap = 2 * math.max(halfU, halfV)
		for other, candidate in ipairs(places) do
			if other ~= index then
				gap = math.min(gap, math.sqrt((candidate[1] - place[1]) ^ 2 + (candidate[2] - place[2]) ^ 2))
			end
		end
		local angle = random() * 2 * math.pi
		local du = math.cos(angle) * gap * STAGGER
		local dv = math.sin(angle) * gap * STAGGER
		table.insert(points, lay(math.clamp(place[1] + du, -limitU, limitU), math.clamp(place[2] + dv, -limitV, limitV), crust * UPPER))
		table.insert(points, lay(math.clamp(place[1] - du, -limitU, limitU), math.clamp(place[2] - dv, -limitV, limitV), crust * LOWER))
	end
	return points
end

Sites.faceAxes = faceAxes
Sites.underFace = underFace

function Sites.alongFace(axis, u, v, normal)
	if axis == "X" then
		return Vector3.new(normal, u, v)
	elseif axis == "Y" then
		return Vector3.new(u, normal, v)
	end
	return Vector3.new(u, v, normal)
end

-- How far under the face a probe lies.
local PROBE_DEPTH = 0.5

function Sites.probes(size, axis, side, u, v, reach)
	local points = { underFace(size, axis, side, u, v, PROBE_DEPTH) }
	for ring = 1, 3 do
		local radius = reach * ring * 0.3
		for step = 1, 8 do
			local angle = step / 8 * 2 * math.pi
			table.insert(points, underFace(size, axis, side, u + math.cos(angle) * radius, v + math.sin(angle) * radius, PROBE_DEPTH))
		end
	end
	return points
end

function Sites.cracks(size, count, hit, reach, random, options)
	local face = options and options.face
	local fill = options and options.fill
	local line = options and options.line
	local axis, side = Sites.face(size, hit)
	if face then
		axis, side = face.axis, face.side
	end
	local uAxis, vAxis = faceAxes(axis)
	local halfU, halfV = size[uAxis] / 2, size[vAxis] / 2
	local hitU, hitV = hit[uAxis], hit[vAxis]
	local function inside(u, v)
		return math.abs(u) < halfU * INSET and math.abs(v) < halfV * INSET
	end

	local crustReach = reach
	if line then
		reach = line.reach
		crustReach = line.path.length
		-- The crust is cut off its base under the split's middle.
		local middle = Fissure.at(line.path, 0.5)
		hitU, hitV = middle[uAxis], middle[vAxis]
	else
		-- The rings are drawn in to the face: none of the points is spent beyond its far corner.
		local farthest = math.sqrt((math.abs(hitU) + halfU) ^ 2 + (math.abs(hitV) + halfV) ^ 2)
		reach = math.min(reach, farthest / 1.2)
		crustReach = reach
	end

	local thickness = size[axis]
	local crust = math.min(math.max(crustReach * CRUST_REACH_SHARE, LEAST_CRUST), thickness * CRUST_SHARE)
	if options and options.crust then
		crust = options.crust
	end
	local split = nil
	if crust >= LEAST_CRUST then
		-- One point in the crust and one under it, in line: the cut between them is flat.
		local apart = math.min(crust, thickness - crust) / 2
		local u = math.clamp(hitU, -halfU * INSET, halfU * INSET)
		local v = math.clamp(hitV, -halfV * INSET, halfV * INSET)
		split = {
			inCrust = underFace(size, axis, side, u, v, crust - apart),
			inBase = underFace(size, axis, side, u, v, crust + apart),
		}
	else
		crust = thickness
	end
	if crust >= LEAST_LAYERED then
		count = math.min(count, Sites.MAX // Sites.LAYERS)
	end

	local seed = math.floor(random() * 2147483645) + 1
	local places = {}
	local spare = count
	if line then
		local along = Fissure.places(count, line.path, reach, RUN_ON, Sites.sequence(line.seed or seed), function(position)
			return inside(position[uAxis], position[vAxis])
		end)
		for index, position in ipairs(along) do
			places[index] = { position[uAxis], position[vAxis] }
		end
		spare = 2
	else
		-- Places that fall outside the part are lost (a hit near an edge loses many): the rings
		-- are drawn again for more, from the same numbers, until about as many are kept as asked.
		places = rings(count, hitU, hitV, reach, Sites.sequence(seed), inside)
		local asked = count
		for _ = 1, 16 do
			if #places >= count * 0.95 then
				break
			end
			asked = math.ceil(asked * 1.12)
			local more = rings(asked, hitU, hitV, reach, Sites.sequence(seed), inside)
			if #more > count then
				break
			end
			places = more
		end
	end
	if fill and #places < 2 then
		places = spread(math.max(spare, 2), halfU, halfV, Sites.sequence(seed))
	end
	local points = layered(places, crust, halfU, halfV, Sites.sequence(seed + 7), function(u, v, depth)
		return underFace(size, axis, side, u, v, depth)
	end)

	local strike = {
		origin = underFace(size, axis, side, hitU, hitV, 0),
		normal = underFace(Vector3.new(2, 2, 2), axis, side, 0, 0, 0),
		reach = reach,
		crust = crust,
	}
	if line then
		strike.path = line.path
	end
	return points, strike, split
end

return Sites

--[[
	SkinDisplay  -  what is left intact of a skin (Reactor/Layers: a thin mesh part or union
	lying on a ground) while that ground has open cracks: a copy of the skin with the wounds
	taken out of it, while the skin itself is hidden. A skin has any outline, so the rest of
	it cannot be drawn as boxes (Reactor/GroundDisplay).

	The copy is the engine's (Reactor/Shards.without, handed in), which YIELDS for a frame or
	more, and a draw must not leave a frame with ground that is intact and not drawn. So
	until the new copy is there the last one stays, and when a wound has closed the skin
	itself is shown again beside it: for those frames grass lies over an open wound, never a
	hole over ground that is whole.

	The skin is LIVE user content: it is written by Reactor/Display's hide and show alone.
	The copies are not saved (Archivable off, under the runtime's folder, marked
	_PartIcleEmit) and nothing collides with them.

	SkinDisplay.new(folder, onServer, without) -> skins
	skins.draw(ground, layer, rectangles, face)
	    ground: a stacked ground; layer: its skin's layer; rectangles: the intact rest of the
	    ground's face `face` (Reactor/Ground), or nil: the skin is whole again.
	skins.clear()   every skin whole again
	SkinDisplay.holes(size, rectangles, face) -> { { minU, minV, maxU, maxV }, ... }
	    What of the face of a box of that size the rectangles leave open. Maths only.
]]

local Display = require(script.Parent.Display)
local Index = require(script.Parent.Index)
local Sites = require(script.Parent.Sites)

-- Two edges this near are one.
local SAME = 0.01
-- A cutter reaches this far past the ground along the struck face's axis, to both sides.
local THROUGH = 4

local SkinDisplay = {}

local function edgesOf(low, high, rectangles, fromKey, toKey)
	local edges = { low, high }
	for _, rectangle in ipairs(rectangles) do
		table.insert(edges, math.clamp(rectangle[fromKey], low, high))
		table.insert(edges, math.clamp(rectangle[toKey], low, high))
	end
	table.sort(edges)
	local distinct = { edges[1] }
	for position = 2, #edges do
		if edges[position] - distinct[#distinct] > SAME then
			table.insert(distinct, edges[position])
		end
	end
	return distinct
end

function SkinDisplay.holes(size, rectangles, face)
	local uAxis, vAxis = Sites.faceAxes(face.axis)
	local us = edgesOf(-size[uAxis] / 2, size[uAxis] / 2, rectangles, "minU", "maxU")
	local vs = edgesOf(-size[vAxis] / 2, size[vAxis] / 2, rectangles, "minV", "maxV")
	local holes = {}
	for row = 1, #vs - 1 do
		local v = (vs[row] + vs[row + 1]) / 2
		-- The open cells of a row that lie side by side are one hole.
		local run = nil
		for column = 1, #us - 1 do
			local u = (us[column] + us[column + 1]) / 2
			local covered = false
			for _, rectangle in ipairs(rectangles) do
				if u > rectangle.minU and u < rectangle.maxU and v > rectangle.minV and v < rectangle.maxV then
					covered = true
					break
				end
			end
			if covered then
				run = nil
			elseif run then
				run.maxU = us[column + 1]
			else
				run = { minU = us[column], minV = vs[row], maxU = us[column + 1], maxV = vs[row + 1] }
				table.insert(holes, run)
			end
		end
	end
	return holes
end

-- Whether every hole of `before` is still open in `now`.
local function stillOpen(before, now)
	for _, hole in ipairs(before) do
		local u = (hole.minU + hole.maxU) / 2
		local v = (hole.minV + hole.maxV) / 2
		local open = false
		for _, other in ipairs(now) do
			-- A hole's middle may lie on the line between two of the new ones.
			if u >= other.minU and u <= other.maxU and v >= other.minV and v <= other.maxV then
				open = true
				break
			end
		end
		if not open then
			return false
		end
	end
	return true
end

function SkinDisplay.new(folder, onServer, without)
	-- part -> { copy, kept (what Display.show puts back), holes, version }
	local drawn = {}
	local skins = {}

	local function whole(part)
		local state = drawn[part]
		if not state then
			return
		end
		drawn[part] = nil
		if state.copy then
			state.copy:Destroy()
		end
		if state.kept then
			Display.show(part, onServer, state.kept)
		end
	end

	-- The engine's copy as what is drawn of the skin.
	local function dress(copy, part)
		copy.Name = "SkinRest"
		copy.Archivable = false
		copy.Anchored = true
		copy.CanCollide = false
		copy.CanQuery = false
		copy.CanTouch = false
		copy.Locked = true
		if copy:IsA("PartOperation") and part:IsA("PartOperation") then
			copy.UsePartColor = part.UsePartColor
		end
		-- On a server the skin is hidden through its own Transparency, which the copy took.
		copy.Transparency = Display.ownTransparency(part)
		Index.unmark(copy)
		copy:SetAttribute("_PartIcleEmit", true)
	end

	function skins.draw(ground, layer, rectangles, face)
		local part = layer.part
		local holes = rectangles and SkinDisplay.holes(ground.size, rectangles, face) or {}
		if #holes == 0 then
			whole(part)
			return
		end
		local state = drawn[part]
		if not state then
			state = { copy = nil, kept = nil, holes = {}, version = 0 }
			drawn[part] = state
		end
		-- A wound has closed: the skin itself covers its place until the new copy is there.
		if state.kept and not stillOpen(state.holes, holes) then
			Display.show(part, onServer, state.kept)
			state.kept = nil
		end
		state.holes = holes
		state.version += 1
		local version = state.version
		local boxes = table.create(#holes)
		local through = ground.size[face.axis] + 2 * THROUGH
		for position, hole in ipairs(holes) do
			local centre = Sites.alongFace(face.axis, (hole.minU + hole.maxU) / 2, (hole.minV + hole.maxV) / 2, 0)
			boxes[position] = {
				frame = ground.frame * CFrame.new(centre.X, centre.Y, centre.Z),
				size = Sites.alongFace(face.axis, hole.maxU - hole.minU, hole.maxV - hole.minV, through),
			}
		end
		task.spawn(function()
			local copy = without(part, boxes)
			if drawn[part] ~= state or state.version ~= version then
				if copy then
					copy:Destroy()
				end
				return
			end
			-- The engine gave nothing: what is drawn stays, the last copy or the skin itself.
			if not copy then
				return
			end
			dress(copy, part)
			copy.Parent = folder
			if state.copy then
				state.copy:Destroy()
			end
			state.copy = copy
			-- Hidden last, so the copy is there in the frame the skin goes.
			if not state.kept then
				state.kept = Display.hide(part, onServer, true)
			end
		end)
	end

	function skins.clear()
		for part in pairs(table.clone(drawn)) do
			whole(part)
		end
	end

	return skins
end

return SkinDisplay

--[[
	Slash  -  what the sides of a cut do. Part of Reactor/Play, split out for size: the
	functions take a play and read and write its own tables. Maths on Vector3 and CFrame
	values, no instances.

	A Linear Force with a Cut (Force/init: record.cut = { mode, pushAlong, pushApart }) carves
	the parts its blade touches (Reactor/Carve). A carved piece carries
	piece.slash = { origin, normal, heading, kerf, by } in the world, one table for the pieces
	of one part, `by` the Force the cut was made for (Reactor/Entries stamps it), and
	piece.side (1 or -1: its side of the cut) or piece.bit (debris of what the blade took out).

	The first time that Force reaches the play its cuts show (waking one piece shows its whole
	part, Reactor/Display) and their sides are let go:
	  The side that lies on top of a sloping cut is loose. With no Push Apart it drops onto the
	    cut and slides down it under its own weight, then falls: a path led by a slide
	    (Rocks/Trajectory.slide). Push Along sends it off along the Force's heading as it
	    slides; a level cut with no push only closes. With a Push Apart it is thrown clear at
	    once, as any piece is thrown.
	  The side under it is carried, and no push moves it. Reactor/Support lets it fall when
	    nothing carries it.
	  Of an upright cut neither side lies on the other: both stand unless a push throws them,
	    each to its own side of the cut.
	  A lone side (the blade ended inside the part) is the part with a slot in it: it stands.
	The pushes are distances, as a Force's Strength is (Force/Fields.throwSpeed).
	Bits are thrown by the Force's Strength as its front reaches them, whatever the Reactor's
	Hold: they are loose already.

	A side that stands is kept as a piece of cracked ground is, RESTING with
	play.crackFrame[index] at the pose it stands in: a Return and a restore then know its
	stand-in. A bit is not: it starts its flight as any buried piece does (Play:_surfaced).
	The pieces of a piece that was cut again (Reactor/Recarve) stand where that piece stood,
	which need not be where it rests, so everything here goes by where a side stands now.
	Sides that lie where their piece fell, or fly as it flew, slide nowhere: a push throws
	them, each to its own side of the cut, and without one they go on as they were.

	A slide stops where the world is in its way (one ray along it): the low end of a side that
	is in pieces meets the ground before the rest is over the edge.

	Slash.kick(play, record, kicked)
	    Called by Play:_applyImpulse with every Impulse it applies. `kicked` is that Force's
	    list of the pieces it has kicked: the sides and the bits it lets go are added to it.
]]

local Trajectory = require(script.Parent.Parent.Rocks.Trajectory)
local Fields = require(script.Parent.Parent.Force.Fields)
local Blade = require(script.Parent.Blade)

local RESTING = 0
local FLYING = 1
local LANDED = 2

local ZERO = Vector3.new(0, 0, 0)
local UP = Vector3.new(0, 1, 0)
local TINY = 1e-4
-- A push under this many studs is no push.
local LEAST_PUSH = 0.05
-- The friction of a fresh cut: its loose side slides on any slope steeper than about 5 degrees.
local SLIDE_FRICTION = 0.08
-- An acceleration under this many studs per second squared is no slide.
local LEAST_SLIDE = 1
-- No slide lasts longer than this many seconds.
local MOST_SLIDE = 4
-- The share of its tumble a side takes with it over the edge.
local TIP_SHARE = 0.5
-- A bit strays sideways by up to this share of its speed.
local BIT_STRAY = 0.35
-- Halvings that find when a slide has gone a given way.
local TIME_STEPS = 16

local Slash = {}

-- Where a side stands: where its cut was shown, which is its rest pose unless the piece it was
-- cut from stood out of place.
local function stoodAt(play, index)
	return play.crackFrame[index] or play.pieces[index].rest
end

-- How far a box of half-lengths `half`, standing at `stood`, reaches from its middle along a unit direction.
local function reachAlong(stood, half, direction)
	return math.abs(stood.XVector:Dot(direction)) * half.X + math.abs(stood.YVector:Dot(direction)) * half.Y + math.abs(stood.ZVector:Dot(direction)) * half.Z
end

-- How far the pieces reach past their common middle along a unit direction: the way their
-- middle has to go before it is over the edge.
local function overhang(play, indices, direction)
	local total = 0
	local farthest = -math.huge
	for _, index in ipairs(indices) do
		local stood = stoodAt(play, index)
		local along = stood.Position:Dot(direction)
		total += along
		farthest = math.max(farthest, along + reachAlong(stood, play.pieces[index].halfExt, direction))
	end
	return farthest - total / #indices
end

-- Where a slide is `time` seconds in, from where it began.
local function slid(velocity, acceleration, settle, settleTime, time)
	local settled = math.min(time / settleTime, 1)
	return velocity * time + acceleration * (0.5 * time * time) + settle * (settled * settled)
end

-- The seconds a piece may slide before the world is in its way: `duration`, or less. One ray
-- along the whole slide finds the surface; the piece then slides until its box, as it stands,
-- touches that surface's plane.
local function clearFor(play, index, velocity, acceleration, settle, settleTime, duration)
	local stood = stoodAt(play, index)
	local half = play.pieces[index].halfExt
	local start = stood.Position
	local travel = slid(velocity, acceleration, settle, settleTime, duration)
	local distance = travel.Magnitude
	if distance < TINY then
		return duration
	end
	local direction = travel / distance
	local hit = play.castRay(start, direction * (distance + reachAlong(stood, half, direction)))
	if not hit then
		return duration
	end
	local normal = hit.Normal
	local seat = hit.Position:Dot(normal) + reachAlong(stood, half, normal)
	local function clear(time)
		return (start + slid(velocity, acceleration, settle, settleTime, time)):Dot(normal) >= seat
	end
	if clear(duration) then
		return duration
	end
	local low, high = 0, duration
	for _ = 1, TIME_STEPS do
		local middle = (low + high) / 2
		if clear(middle) then
			low = middle
		else
			high = middle
		end
	end
	return low
end

-- Puts a standing carved piece on a path of its own. Its stand-in is there already.
local function launch(play, index, path, built)
	play.display.wake(index)
	play.awake += 1
	play.hidden += 1
	play.path[index] = path
	play.pathStart[index] = play.clock
	play.pathBuilt[index] = built
	play.lastFrame[index] = stoodAt(play, index)
	if not built then
		table.insert(play.buildQueue, index)
	end
	play.state[index] = FLYING
	table.insert(play.flying, index)
	play.supportStale = true
end

-- The loose side of a sloping cut, with no Push Apart: `along` is the speed its Push Along
-- gives it. All its pieces take one slide, so a side that is in pieces leaves as one.
local function slideOff(play, indices, slash, downhill, sine, cosine, along)
	local gravity = play:_rolled(indices[1])
	local accel = gravity * (sine - SLIDE_FRICTION * cosine)
	-- It falls onto the cut first: the kerf, straight down.
	local drop = slash.kerf / math.max(cosine, TINY)
	local settle = UP * -drop
	local settleTime = math.sqrt(2 * drop / math.max(gravity, TINY))
	local slides = downhill ~= nil and accel > LEAST_SLIDE
	if not slides and along <= 0 then
		for _, index in ipairs(indices) do
			play:_rolled(index)
			local stood = stoodAt(play, index)
			local lead = Trajectory.slide(stood.Position, ZERO, stood.Rotation, ZERO, settleTime, settle, settleTime)
			launch(play, index, Trajectory.settled(lead, UP), true)
		end
		return
	end

	local velocity = slash.heading * along
	local acceleration = ZERO
	local duration = MOST_SLIDE
	if slides then
		acceleration = downhill * accel
		local length = overhang(play, indices, downhill)
		local start = velocity:Dot(downhill)
		duration = math.min(duration, (-start + math.sqrt(start * start + 2 * accel * length)) / accel)
	end
	if along > 0 then
		duration = math.min(duration, overhang(play, indices, slash.heading) / along)
	end
	for _, index in ipairs(indices) do
		play:_rolled(index)
		local stood = stoodAt(play, index)
		local own = clearFor(play, index, velocity, acceleration, settle, settleTime, duration)
		local lead = Trajectory.slide(stood.Position, velocity, stood.Rotation, acceleration, own, settle, settleTime)
		local finish = stood.Position + slid(velocity, acceleration, settle, settleTime, own)
		local leave = velocity + acceleration * own
		-- Over the edge it tips forward, about the level axis across the way it leaves.
		local level = Vector3.new(leave.X, 0, leave.Z)
		local spin = ZERO
		if level.Magnitude > TINY then
			spin = UP:Cross(level.Unit) * (play.settings.rollTumble() * TIP_SHARE)
		end
		launch(play, index, Trajectory.led(lead, Trajectory.ballistic(finish, leave, stood.Rotation, spin)), false)
	end
end

-- Lets go of the sides of one part's cut. group = { slash, sides = { [1], [-1] }, first }.
local function release(play, group, cut)
	local slash = group.slash
	local sides = group.sides
	-- A blade that ended inside the part left it in one piece: nothing is let go.
	if #sides[1] == 0 or #sides[-1] == 0 then
		return
	end
	local gravity = play:_rolled(group.first)
	local along = 0
	if cut.pushAlong > LEAST_PUSH then
		along = Fields.throwSpeed(cut.pushAlong, gravity)
	end
	local apart = 0
	if cut.pushApart > LEAST_PUSH then
		apart = Fields.throwSpeed(cut.pushApart, gravity)
	end
	local over, downhill, sine, cosine = Blade.slope(slash)
	if over == 0 then
		if along > 0 or apart > 0 then
			for side = -1, 1, 2 do
				for _, index in ipairs(sides[side]) do
					play:_push(index, slash.heading * along + slash.normal * (side * apart))
				end
			end
		end
		return
	end
	local loose = sides[over]
	if apart > 0 then
		for _, index in ipairs(loose) do
			play:_push(index, slash.heading * along + slash.normal * (over * apart))
		end
		return
	end
	slideOff(play, loose, slash, downhill, sine, cosine, along)
end

-- The sides of a cut that lie where their piece fell or fly as it flew: a push throws each to
-- its own side.
local function throwLoose(play, record, kicked)
	local cut = record.cut
	for index, piece in ipairs(play.pieces) do
		local slash = piece.slash
		local state = play.state[index]
		if slash and slash.by == record and piece.side and (state == LANDED or state == FLYING) and not kicked[index] then
			kicked[index] = true
			local gravity = play:_rolled(index)
			local push = ZERO
			if cut.pushAlong > LEAST_PUSH then
				push += slash.heading * Fields.throwSpeed(cut.pushAlong, gravity)
			end
			if cut.pushApart > LEAST_PUSH then
				push += slash.normal * (piece.side * Fields.throwSpeed(cut.pushApart, gravity))
			end
			if push.Magnitude > TINY then
				play:_push(index, push)
				play:_takeTime(record)
			end
		end
	end
end

-- Shows every part this Force cut and lets its sides go.
local function letGo(play, record, kicked)
	throwLoose(play, record, kicked)
	local groups = {}
	local ordered = {}
	for index, piece in ipairs(play.pieces) do
		local slash = piece.slash
		if slash and slash.by == record and play.state[index] == RESTING and not play.pendingPush[index] then
			local group = groups[slash]
			if not group then
				group = { slash = slash, sides = { [1] = {}, [-1] = {} }, first = index }
				groups[slash] = group
				table.insert(ordered, group)
			end
			if piece.side then
				play.crackFrame[index] = stoodAt(play, index)
				kicked[index] = true
				-- A fixed side stands whatever the cut: a part with a slot, or a ground's patch.
				if not piece.fixed then
					table.insert(group.sides[piece.side], index)
				end
			end
		end
	end
	for _, group in ipairs(ordered) do
		play.display.wake(group.first)
		play.hidden += 1
		release(play, group, record.cut)
	end
	if #ordered > 0 then
		play:_takeTime(record)
	end
end

-- The bits the Force's front has reached go, along the way it heads.
local function throwBits(play, record, kicked)
	local field = record.field
	local strength = record.strength
	local heading = Fields.heading(field, strength < 0)
	local origin = field.origin.Position
	local axis = field.origin.LookVector
	local random = play.settings.random
	for index, piece in ipairs(play.pieces) do
		local slash = piece.slash
		local state = play.state[index]
		if piece.bit and slash.by == record and not kicked[index] and (state == RESTING or state == LANDED or state == FLYING) and not play.pendingPush[index] then
			local distance = math.clamp((play:_position(index) - origin):Dot(axis), field.inner, field.range)
			if distance <= record.front then
				kicked[index] = true
				local spread = 1 + record.variation * (random() * 2 - 1)
				local throw = strength * Fields.kept(record.falloff, distance / field.range) * spread
				local speed = Fields.throwSpeed(throw, play:_rolled(index))
				local stray = slash.normal * ((random() * 2 - 1) * BIT_STRAY * speed)
				play:_push(index, heading * speed + stray)
			end
		end
	end
end

function Slash.kick(play, record, kicked)
	if not record.cut then
		return
	end
	local shown = play.slashed
	if not shown then
		shown = setmetatable({}, { __mode = "k" })
		play.slashed = shown
	end
	if not shown[record] then
		shown[record] = true
		letGo(play, record, kicked)
	end
	throwBits(play, record, kicked)
end

return Slash

--[[
	Support  -  which pieces of a Reactor hold each other up, so that a piece left with nothing
	under or beside it can fall. Numbers only, no instances.

	Two pieces are neighbours when their boxes meet face to face: world-axis boxes around each
	piece at rest, no farther apart than a small margin along one axis and overlapping by a good
	part of the smaller box along the other two. Boxes that only meet at an edge or a corner do
	not hold each other. The two sides of a blade's cut hold each other across its kerf
	(piece.slash, Reactor/Carve). A piece is anchored when the caller says so (Reactor/init:
	something that is not the Reactor lies right under it). A piece is supported when a chain of
	neighbours that are still standing leads from it to a standing anchored piece.

	Support.build(pieces, isAnchored) -> graph, with graph.supported[index] true for every piece
	that is supported while everything stands. A piece that floats from the start (a lamp hung in
	mid-air) is not, and is never made to fall.
	Support.unsupported(graph, isStanding) -> the pieces that were supported at rest, still stand,
	and have lost their last chain to an anchor.
]]

local Support = {}

-- How far apart two boxes may be and still count as touching, in studs.
local TOUCH_MARGIN = 0.15
-- Along the two axes of a shared face, the boxes must overlap by this share of the smaller one.
local FACE_SHARE = 0.25
-- The grid the boxes are sorted into, so that only pieces near each other are compared.
local LEAST_CELL = 2

-- Half the size of the world-axis box around a piece at rest.
function Support.worldHalf(piece)
	local rest = piece.rest
	local half = piece.halfExt
	local right, up, back = rest.XVector, rest.YVector, rest.ZVector
	return Vector3.new(
		math.abs(right.X) * half.X + math.abs(up.X) * half.Y + math.abs(back.X) * half.Z,
		math.abs(right.Y) * half.X + math.abs(up.Y) * half.Y + math.abs(back.Y) * half.Z,
		math.abs(right.Z) * half.X + math.abs(up.Z) * half.Y + math.abs(back.Z) * half.Z
	)
end

-- Along one axis: 2 when the boxes overlap deeply enough to share a face across it, 1 when
-- they at least touch, 0 when they are apart.
local function contact(offset, firstHalf, secondHalf)
	local overlap = firstHalf + secondHalf - math.abs(offset)
	if overlap >= FACE_SHARE * 2 * math.min(firstHalf, secondHalf) then
		return 2
	elseif overlap >= -TOUCH_MARGIN then
		return 1
	end
	return 0
end

-- Face to face: touching along every axis and overlapping deeply along at least two.
function Support.touching(firstCentre, firstHalf, secondCentre, secondHalf)
	local alongX = contact(firstCentre.X - secondCentre.X, firstHalf.X, secondHalf.X)
	local alongY = contact(firstCentre.Y - secondCentre.Y, firstHalf.Y, secondHalf.Y)
	local alongZ = contact(firstCentre.Z - secondCentre.Z, firstHalf.Z, secondHalf.Z)
	if alongX == 0 or alongY == 0 or alongZ == 0 then
		return false
	end
	return alongX + alongY + alongZ >= 5
end

-- Every piece reachable from the standing anchored ones through standing neighbours.
local function reached(graph, isStanding)
	local seen = {}
	local queue = {}
	for index in pairs(graph.anchored) do
		if isStanding(index) then
			seen[index] = true
			table.insert(queue, index)
		end
	end
	local head = 1
	while head <= #queue do
		local index = queue[head]
		head += 1
		for _, neighbour in ipairs(graph.neighbours[index]) do
			if not seen[neighbour] and isStanding(neighbour) then
				seen[neighbour] = true
				table.insert(queue, neighbour)
			end
		end
	end
	return seen
end

function Support.build(pieces, isAnchored)
	local count = #pieces
	local centres = table.create(count)
	local halves = table.create(count)
	local cell = LEAST_CELL
	for index, piece in ipairs(pieces) do
		centres[index] = piece.rest.Position
		local half = Support.worldHalf(piece)
		-- The sides of a blade's cut (Reactor/Carve) stand a kerf apart and still hold each
		-- other: each box reaches half the kerf across the cut.
		local slash = piece.slash
		if slash then
			local normal = slash.normal
			half += Vector3.new(math.abs(normal.X), math.abs(normal.Y), math.abs(normal.Z)) * (slash.kerf / 2)
		end
		halves[index] = half
		cell = math.max(cell, half.X * 2, half.Y * 2, half.Z * 2)
	end

	-- A box is listed in every cell it reaches into; two boxes are compared once, in the first
	-- cell they share.
	local cells = {}
	local neighbours = table.create(count)
	local paired = {}
	for index = 1, count do
		neighbours[index] = {}
		local centre, half = centres[index], halves[index]
		for x = math.floor((centre.X - half.X - TOUCH_MARGIN) / cell), math.floor((centre.X + half.X + TOUCH_MARGIN) / cell) do
			for y = math.floor((centre.Y - half.Y - TOUCH_MARGIN) / cell), math.floor((centre.Y + half.Y + TOUCH_MARGIN) / cell) do
				for z = math.floor((centre.Z - half.Z - TOUCH_MARGIN) / cell), math.floor((centre.Z + half.Z + TOUCH_MARGIN) / cell) do
					local key = x .. "," .. y .. "," .. z
					local members = cells[key]
					if not members then
						members = {}
						cells[key] = members
					end
					for _, other in ipairs(members) do
						local pair = other * (count + 1) + index
						if not paired[pair] then
							paired[pair] = true
							if Support.touching(centre, half, centres[other], halves[other]) then
								table.insert(neighbours[index], other)
								table.insert(neighbours[other], index)
							end
						end
					end
					table.insert(members, index)
				end
			end
		end
	end

	local anchored = {}
	for index = 1, count do
		if isAnchored(index) then
			anchored[index] = true
		end
	end
	local graph = { neighbours = neighbours, anchored = anchored, supported = {} }
	graph.supported = reached(graph, function()
		return true
	end)
	return graph
end

function Support.unsupported(graph, isStanding)
	local held = reached(graph, isStanding)
	local fallen = {}
	for index in pairs(graph.supported) do
		if not held[index] and isStanding(index) then
			table.insert(fallen, index)
		end
	end
	table.sort(fallen)
	return fallen
end

return Support

--[[
	WoundBudget  -  what a Reactor's wounds hold against its Max Pieces (Reactor/Wounds mixes
	these methods in; `self` is the wounds). Logic only.

	The budget is over every wound of the Reactor's grounds: the pieces of the groups that
	stay, and those a wound still being cut is expected to bring. A crack that would pass it
	first sweeps away the debris of blades that lies about, oldest wounds first (a gash stays,
	its bits are only litter), and then sends the oldest groups back early, but only while
	that can help: when the groups that must stay (the one a crack is about to break again,
	one still being cut) are over the budget by themselves, no other group is healed for
	nothing.

	WoundBudget.livePieces(wound) -> the pieces of a wound that count: all but those cut again
	WoundBudget.methods = { _held, _sweep, _send, _makeRoom, _room }
	    _held() -> the pieces the budget counts
	    _sweep(extra)               removes landed debris until `extra` more pieces would fit
	    _send(group, after, time)   every wound of a group starts on its way back
	    _makeRoom(extra, spare)     brings what is held, and `extra` more, under the budget
	    _room(wound)                what a later crack may add to a wound
]]

local Recut = require(script.Parent.Recut)

local LANDED = 2
local GONE = 3

local WoundBudget = {}
local methods = {}
WoundBudget.methods = methods

-- The pieces of a wound that count: all but those a later crack cut again.
function WoundBudget.livePieces(wound)
	local pieces = 0
	for _, piece in ipairs(wound.play.pieces) do
		if not piece.retired then
			pieces += 1
		end
	end
	return pieces
end

local livePieces = WoundBudget.livePieces

-- What the budget counts: the pieces of the groups that stay, and those a wound still being
-- cut is expected to bring.
function methods:_held()
	local pieces = 0
	for _, wound in ipairs(self.open) do
		if not wound.group.leaving then
			if wound.play then
				pieces += livePieces(wound)
			else
				pieces += wound.expected
			end
		end
	end
	return pieces
end

-- Every wound of a group starts on its way back now: `after` in `time` seconds, or in the
-- play's own After Time when nil.
function methods:_send(group, after, time)
	group.sent = true
	for _, wound in ipairs(group.wounds) do
		local play = wound.play
		if play and play.phase == "live" then
			play.settings.After = after
			play.settings.AfterDelay = 0
			if time then
				play.settings.AfterTime = time
			end
		end
	end
end

local function beingCut(group)
	for _, wound in ipairs(group.wounds) do
		if not wound.play then
			return true
		end
	end
	return false
end

-- A blade's debris that has come to rest is litter: the oldest wounds' is taken away until
-- `extra` more pieces would fit the budget. A swept bit is gone for good (retired), so a
-- wound that closes does not bring it back.
function methods:_sweep(extra)
	local over = self:_held() + extra - self.maxPieces
	for _, wound in ipairs(self.open) do
		local play = wound.play
		if play and play.phase == "live" then
			for index, piece in ipairs(play.pieces) do
				if over <= 0 then
					return
				end
				if piece.bit and not piece.retired and play.state[index] == LANDED then
					piece.retired = true
					play.state[index] = GONE
					play.display.drop(index)
					play.awake -= 1
					over -= 1
				end
			end
		end
	end
end

-- The pieces that are there and cannot be sent back now: those of `spare` and of every group
-- with a wound still being cut.
local function staying(self, spare)
	local pieces = 0
	for _, group in ipairs(self.groups) do
		if not group.leaving and (group == spare or beingCut(group)) then
			for _, wound in ipairs(group.wounds) do
				if wound.play then
					pieces += livePieces(wound)
				end
			end
		end
	end
	return pieces
end

-- Brings what is held, and `extra` pieces more, under the budget: the oldest groups are sent
-- back until it fits. Never one with a wound still being cut (so never the one just asked
-- for), nor `spare`, the group a later crack is about to break again; and none at all when
-- those are over the budget by themselves.
function methods:_makeRoom(extra, spare)
	self:_sweep(extra)
	if staying(self, spare) + extra > self.maxPieces then
		return
	end
	local position = 1
	while position <= #self.groups and self:_held() + extra > self.maxPieces do
		local group = self.groups[position]
		if group == spare or group.leaving or beingCut(group) then
			position += 1
		else
			self:_leave(group)
			if self.groups[position] == group then
				position += 1
			end
		end
	end
end

-- What a later crack may add to a wound: its play is held to the room all the wounds leave.
function methods:_room(wound)
	local settings = wound.play.settings
	local live = livePieces(wound)
	local held = self:_held()
	settings.MaxPieces = live + math.max(self.maxPieces - held, 0)
	settings.MostPieces = live + math.max(self.maxPieces * Recut.PLATE_ROOM - held, 0)
end

return WoundBudget

--[[
	Wounds  -  the cracks of a Reactor's ground parts. Logic only: instances, the engine's cut
	and the plays are reached through what Wounds.new is handed, so all of it runs under the
	luau CLI.

	A ground is a plain block-shaped part with Break = "Shards" and Shard Pattern "Cracks". It
	is never cut whole. An Impulse that reaches it opens a wound: a square of its struck face
	around the hit, a little wider than the Force can move, or for a Linear Force that lies
	along the face a strip around its split (Reactor/Footprint), less what open wounds hold
	already (Reactor/Ground). Each rectangle of that area is cut as cracked ground from a template
	of its own (Reactor/Patches), and the pieces are one ordinary Reactor/Play. A Force with a
	Cut carves instead (Footprint.ofBlade): its wound is the ground under its blade, with a gash
	as wide and as deep as the blade, whichever side of the ground its Force stands on (a
	crack is of the face it strikes, a cut goes through). Where it crosses a wound that is
	open already, what
	stands there of an earlier gash is cut again (Reactor/Recarve); cracked ground is left as
	it is, so a gash stops at an open crack. The rest of the
	ground is drawn as boxes around the open wounds (Reactor/GroundDisplay). A wound whose play
	is done gives its ground back, and a ground with no wound left is shown whole again.

	Wounds that touch are one GROUP, and a group heals as one: a crack near another shares
	ground with it (its crater may be the other's pieces, cracked again through
	Reactor/Recrack), so if one healed alone the other would be left cut off along a straight
	edge. A group waits its Delay from the moment the last of its pieces has come to rest
	after the last crack that touched it, and then every wound of it goes back together. What
	it does then (After) and how long it waits are the Reactor's, or those of the last Force
	that cracked it and has a word of its own (record.after, Force/Registry). Cracks that do
	not touch are groups of their own and heal each on its own time. A group that is on its
	way back when a new crack needs its ground is closed at once.

	The cut takes a few frames. A wound holds its ground from the moment it is asked for, and
	shows (pieces in, boxes redrawn) when its pieces are there; until then its ground is still
	drawn intact. The Force that asked has passed by then and kicks late (Play:strike).

	Wounds.new(options) -> wounds
	    grounds     { { part, frame, size }, ... }: frame is the part's place in the world
	    pieceCount  the Reactor's Pieces: the points a whole square is cut around, unless the
	                Force names a count of its own (record.pieces)
	    maxPieces   the Reactor's Max Pieces: the pieces that may be open at once over all
	                its grounds (Reactor/WoundBudget). A crack that would pass it sends the
	                oldest groups back early, a quick Return each (a wound with pieces in
	                the air goes at once), so the newest crack always shows. A group never
	                makes room for a crack of its own: that crack is cut into what room is
	                left, and into half as much again where it lands on plates too wide to
	                show it whole (Reactor/Recut).
	    after, afterDelay   the Reactor's After and Delay
	    snap        the least width of a strip of ground, in studs
	    cut(jobs, done)   jobs: one per rectangle (Reactor/Footprint.job): a template of
	                `size` cracked around `hit`, or along `line`, in the template's own space.
	                done(sets): sets[position] = shards (Reactor/Shards) or false. A whole
	                job is kept by Reactor/Patches, and a kept one is answered at once.
	    play(pieces, record) -> play, display   a play over the pieces whose display leaves the
	                ground itself alone
	    draw(ground, rectangles, face)   the intact rest of a ground as rectangles of its
	                face; rectangles = nil: the ground is whole again
	    isCurrent() -> whether these wounds are still their Reactor's
	    revive()    the Reactor has work again
	wounds:watch(record) -> boolean   the open wounds a Force could reach follow it
	wounds:strike(record)             an Impulse cracks the grounds it reaches. Safe to call
	                                  again for the same Force: one that has not moved half its
	                                  Range since it last cracked does nothing
	wounds:step(dt, override, frozen) -> "active" | "dormant" | "done"
	    Steps every wound by its own time: the slowest of the Forces that moved its pieces
	    (Force/Registry), or `override` when given; `frozen` stops them all. "active" as well
	    while a group waits to heal. A group's wait runs while nothing moves in its wounds
	    (Reactor/Play: busy); a Force that is merely still alive does not hold it up.
	wounds:restore()                  every wound closed, every ground whole
	wounds:busy() -> whether a wound is still being cut
	wounds:count() -> open wounds, their live pieces
]]

local Ground = require(script.Parent.Ground)
local Footprint = require(script.Parent.Footprint)
local Sites = require(script.Parent.Sites)
local Pieces = require(script.Parent.Pieces)
local Recrack = require(script.Parent.Recrack)
local Recarve = require(script.Parent.Recarve)
local WoundBudget = require(script.Parent.WoundBudget)
local Recut = require(script.Parent.Recut)
local Blade = require(script.Parent.Blade)
local Index = require(script.Parent.Index)
local Fields = require(script.Parent.Parent.Force.Fields)
local Registry = require(script.Parent.Parent.Force.Registry)

-- A wound follows a Force that reaches a ball this many times its square's half-diagonal:
-- its debris lies around it.
local WATCH_REACH = 1.5
-- A Force that travels cracks again once it has moved this share of its Range.
local STRIKE_AGAIN = 0.5
-- The seconds a wound takes to return when it makes room for a new one.
local QUICK_RETURN = 0.25

local Wounds = {}
Wounds.__index = Wounds
Wounds.PATCH_REACH = Footprint.PATCH_REACH
-- _held, _send, _makeRoom and _room: what the wounds hold against Max Pieces.
for name, method in pairs(WoundBudget.methods) do
	Wounds[name] = method
end
local livePieces = WoundBudget.livePieces

function Wounds.new(options)
	local self = setmetatable({}, Wounds)
	self.grounds = options.grounds
	self.pieceCount = options.pieceCount
	self.maxPieces = options.maxPieces
	self.after = options.after
	self.afterDelay = options.afterDelay
	self.snap = options.snap
	self.cut = options.cut
	self.play = options.play
	self.draw = options.draw
	self.isCurrent = options.isCurrent
	self.revive = options.revive
	-- Every wound that holds ground, oldest first; one being cut has no play yet.
	self.open = {}
	-- The groups of wounds that touch, oldest first: { wounds, idle, after, delay, sent, leaving }.
	self.groups = {}
	-- record -> where it last cracked; a record that is over is forgotten with it.
	self.struck = setmetatable({}, { __mode = "k" })
	return self
end

-- A ground with nothing held is free to crack on any face again.
local function settle(ground)
	if ground.sheet and ground.sheet:isWhole() then
		ground.sheet = nil
		ground.face = nil
	end
end

-- Sends a group back early, all of it, so none of its cracks is left cut off. A wound with
-- pieces in the air cannot return yet: it goes at once.
function Wounds:_leave(group)
	group.leaving = true
	for _, wound in ipairs(table.clone(group.wounds)) do
		local play = wound.play
		if play.phase == "live" and (#play.flying > 0 or #play.driven > 0 or #play.pendingWake > 0) then
			self:_close(wound)
			settle(wound.ground)
		end
	end
	self:_send(group, "Return", QUICK_RETURN)
end

-- What of a ground is drawn as intact: all of it but the wounds that show.
function Wounds:_draw(ground)
	local sheet = ground.sheet
	local unshown = {}
	local shown = false
	for _, wound in ipairs(self.open) do
		if wound.ground == ground then
			if wound.shown then
				shown = true
			else
				unshown[wound] = true
			end
		end
	end
	if not sheet or not shown then
		self.draw(ground, nil, nil)
	else
		self.draw(ground, sheet:remainder(unshown), ground.face)
	end
end

function Wounds:_close(wound, quiet)
	if wound.closed then
		return
	end
	wound.closed = true
	table.remove(self.open, table.find(self.open, wound))
	table.clear(wound.cracks)
	local group = wound.group
	table.remove(group.wounds, table.find(group.wounds, wound))
	if #group.wounds == 0 then
		table.remove(self.groups, table.find(self.groups, group))
	end
	-- The play is thrown away with its wound: only what it shows has to go.
	if wound.display then
		wound.display.clear()
	end
	local ground = wound.ground
	if ground.sheet then
		ground.sheet:release(wound)
	end
	if not quiet then
		self:_draw(ground)
	end
end

-- A crack has touched a group: its wait starts again. A Force may say what the ground does
-- after its crack, in place of the Reactor's After and Delay (record.after, Force/Registry):
-- a group takes the word of the last Force to crack it. One that is leaving keeps leaving.
local function touch(group, record)
	group.idle = 0
	if record.after and not group.leaving then
		group.after = record.after
		group.delay = record.afterDelay
	end
end

-- The ground keeps its face and its sheet: whoever closes a group is about to claim on it.
function Wounds:_closeGroup(group)
	for _, wound in ipairs(table.clone(group.wounds)) do
		self:_close(wound)
	end
end

-- Two groups a crack touches both become one, the older of them.
function Wounds:_merge(first, second)
	if not first or first == second then
		return second
	end
	local older, newer = first, second
	if table.find(self.groups, second) < table.find(self.groups, first) then
		older, newer = second, first
	end
	for _, wound in ipairs(newer.wounds) do
		wound.group = older
		table.insert(older.wounds, wound)
	end
	table.remove(self.groups, table.find(self.groups, newer))
	return older
end

-- A wound that is open and still its Reactor's: what Reactor/Recrack asks before it answers.
local function stillOpen(self, wound)
	return function()
		return not wound.closed and self.isCurrent()
	end
end

-- A later Force on a wound that shows: a blade cuts what stands in it again
-- (Reactor/Recarve), any other Impulse cracks it again where its rings fall (Reactor/Recrack).
function Wounds:_again(wound, record, kicked)
	touch(wound.group, record)
	self:_room(wound)
	local again = if record.cut then Recarve else Recrack
	again.request(wound, record, kicked, stillOpen(self, wound), self.revive)
end

-- A later Impulse on a wound that is open. One still being cut keeps the record until its
-- pieces are there.
function Wounds:_crackAgain(wound, record)
	local play = wound.play
	if not play then
		table.insert(wound.waiting, record)
		return
	end
	if play:watch(record) then
		-- A later cut adds pieces: older groups make room for it, as they do for a new wound,
		-- and it may add as many as the budget then has room for (Reactor/Recut).
		-- A blade's cut is made whatever the room, its debris only while there is some
		-- (Reactor/Recarve): old debris is swept for it, and no wound is sent back.
		if record.cut then
			self:_sweep(Footprint.bladePieces(record.cut.mode))
		else
			self:_makeRoom((record.pieces or self.pieceCount) * Sites.LAYERS, wound.group)
		end
		self:_again(wound, record, play.kicks[record])
	end
end

-- The pieces of a wound are there: it shows, and the Forces that wait for it strike.
function Wounds:_show(wound, jobs, sets)
	if wound.closed or not self.isCurrent() then
		return
	end
	local ground = wound.ground
	local pieces = {}
	local siblings = {}
	for position, job in ipairs(jobs) do
		local shards = sets[position]
		if shards and (#shards >= 2 or shards.slash) then
			Pieces.ofSet(pieces, ground.part, job.frame, shards, siblings, { size = job.size, face = job.face }, ground.layers)
		else
			-- The engine gave no cut: this rectangle stands in whole, and never moves. Of a
			-- stacked ground (Reactor/Layers) it is a block of each layer.
			local blocks = job.layers or { { offset = Vector3.zero, size = job.size } }
			for _, share in ipairs(blocks) do
				local part = ground.part
				if share.index then
					part = ground.layers[share.index].part
				end
				local piece = Pieces.ofBlock(part, job.frame * CFrame.new(share.offset), share.size)
				piece.fixed = true
				piece.siblings = siblings
				table.insert(pieces, piece)
				table.insert(siblings, #pieces)
			end
		end
	end
	-- The strikes are this Force's: Reactor/Crack tells by that which pieces its split reaches.
	for _, piece in ipairs(pieces) do
		if piece.strike then
			piece.strike.by = wound.record
		end
		if piece.slash then
			piece.slash.by = wound.record
		end
	end
	local play, display = self.play(pieces, wound.record)
	wound.play = play
	wound.display = display
	wound.shown = true
	-- When a wound goes back is its group's to say (step, below).
	play.settings.After = "Stay"
	touch(wound.group, wound.record)
	-- Waking one piece stands the whole wound in, at rest (Reactor/Display: siblings).
	display.wake(1)
	self:_draw(ground)

	play:strike(wound.record)
	for _, record in ipairs(wound.waiting) do
		local struck, kicked = play:strike(record)
		if struck then
			self:_again(wound, record, kicked)
		end
	end
	table.clear(wound.waiting)
	self.revive()
end

-- One ground under one Impulse.
function Wounds:_crack(ground, record, hit, reach)
